{"timestamp":"2026-06-01T02:11:55.474Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-05-31</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n"}},"realtime_active":false,"summary":"none","user_instructions":"### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}

The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. A game can be more illustrative, expressive, animated, and playful.\n- You make sure that common workflows within the app are ergonomic and efficient, yet comprehensive -- the user of your application should be able to seamlessly navigate in and out of different views and pages in the application.\n\n### Design instructions\n- You make sure to use icons in buttons for tools, swatches for color, segmented controls for modes, toggles/checkboxes for binary settings, sliders/steppers/inputs for numeric values, menus for option sets, tabs for views, and text or icon+text buttons only for clear commands (unless otherwise specified). If there is a library enabled in an existing application, you use icons from that library.\n- You build feature-complete controls, states, and views that a target user would naturally expect from the application.\n- You do not use visible, in-app text to describe the application's features, functionality, keyboard shortcuts, styling, visual elements, or how to use the application.\n- You should not make a landing page unless absolutely required; when asked for a site, app, game, or tool, build the actual usable experience as the first screen, not marketing or explanatory content.\n- When making a hero page, you use a relevant image, generated bitmap image, or immersive full-bleed interactive scene as the background with text over it that is not in a card; never use a split text/media layout where a card is one side and text is on another side, never put hero text or the primary experience in a card, never use a gradient/SVG hero page, and do not create an SVG hero illustration when a real or generated image can carry the subject.\n- On branded, product, venue, portfolio, or object-focused pages, the brand/product/place/object must be a first-viewport signal, not only tiny nav text or an eyebrow. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-02</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

No manual config needed.\n\n**Why:** wg-quick's PostUp/Table/FwMark directives handle policy routing automatically. Visible as `default dev wgcf table 51820 scope link`.\n\n**How to apply:** When diagnosing container routing issues, don't treat the `default via ... dev eth0` route as the WARP route — WARP has its own isolated table. The eth0 default route is for non-WARP traffic. Fixing eth0 routing won't break WARP.\n/home/jeremy/.claude/projects/-home-jeremy-git-operation-dbus-proto/memory/project_3tched_architecture.md\n---\nname: project-3tched-architecture\ndescription: \"Core context for the operation-dbus-proto / 3tched project — what it is, how it communicates, key components\"\nmetadata: \n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: 530852a9-02e8-4af8-bdf1-8d45b02180a7\n---\n\nThis is the **3tched** system — a 31-crate Rust workspace (`operation-dbus-proto`) that has been in development for months. It is fundamentally a **socket networking** architecture: services communicate via Unix domain sockets (gRPC over UDS) and the network fabric is built on **Open vSwitch (OVS) with OpenFlow routing**, managed inside **Incus containers**.\n\n**Why:** The system is designed around zero-copy shared memory (`/dev/shm` SchemaEngine), WireGuard identity, Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain), and a full compliance/accountability loop via gRPC metadata headers (`X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`, `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID`).\n\n**Key crates and roles:**\n- `op-grpc-bridge` — gRPC client/server, schema engine (over Unix sockets)\n- `op-dbus-mirror` — D-Bus → OVSDB event mirroring, JSON-RPC interface\n- `op-network` — OpenFlow controller, OVS/OVSDB integration, rtnetlink\n- `op-xdp-ovs-incus` — XDP/eBPF + OVS + Incus container networking\n- `op-cognitive-mcp` — AI/MCP layer, RAG pipeline, soul memory, Qdrant\n- `op-assistant-grpc` — User-facing assistant overlay (newest layer)\n- `op-identity` — WireGuard identity / A.N.N.A. Scribe / Snowball sessions\n- `op-blockchain` — Btrfs vectorized footprint ledger\n\n**Incus containers in use:** `assistant`, `mail-3tched`, `wg-xray`\n\n**How to apply:** When debugging networking issues, always think in terms of Unix socket paths, OVS/OpenFlow rules, and Incus container networking — NOT traditional TCP/IP or systemd-networkd assumptions. gRPC is over UDS internally. The `assistant` container frequently has IP/networking issues on restart.\n/home/jeremy/.claude/projects/-home-jeremy-git-operation-dbus-proto/memory/project_compliance_architecture.md\n---\nname: project-compliance-architecture\ndescription: CoW tiered storage + OSCAL-driven tag routing compliance architecture — core design insight for enterprise/EU regulatory clients\nmetadata: \n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: 530852a9-02e8-4af8-bdf1-8d45b02180a7\n---\n\n# Compliance Architecture Design\n\n## Storage Stack (CoW end to end)\n\n```\nBtrfs (NVMe)     — CoW block layer, subvolumes per tenant/namespace, instant snapshots\n   ↓ lower\noverlayfs        — CoW file promotion to upper on first write\n   ↓ upper\ntmpfs / SHM      — hot working set, kernel-managed pages\n   ↓ merged\nDBus object tree — full tree always visible, tier invisible to consumers\n```\n\n- Btrfs `metacopy=off` required for stable overlayfs+Btrfs combo (kernel <5.15 risk, safe on xanmod 7.0)\n- Eviction daemon needed: flush stale upper-layer objects back to lower (overlayfs has no LRU)\n- `btrfs send` incremental snapshots = replication primitive between peer nodes\n\n## Tag Taxonomy (three orthogonal classes)\n\n| Class | Authority | Mutable by | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| OSCAL | NIST / regulation | OSCAL ingestor (signed docs only) | Compliance enforcement |\n| 3tched | Platform | Operators, agents, automation | Internal workflow routing |\n| UI | Users | Frontend / users | Presentation only, router ignores |\n\n- OSCAL tags: impact levels, information types (SP 800-60), control baselines (800-53, FedRAMP, CMMC), system roles\n- 3tched tags: tier-hint, dbus-scope, replication-zone, workflow stage, queue, assigned-agent\n- UI tags: display-name, icon, pinned, color-group, dashboard-section, collapsed\n- Compliance rules may NEVER reference 3tched or UI tags — enforced at rule parse time\n- Operators have ZERO write authority over OSCAL tags\n\n## Mutation Enforcement Pipeline\n\nEvery mutation (DBus call / OVSDB tx / direct write) runs:\n\n1. Pre-mutation: tag router evaluates compliance rules (BLOCK / COERCE / PERMIT)\n2. CoW write lands (Btrfs → overlayfs upper)\n3. Post-mutation: snapshot delta captured, compliance record appended to ledger\n4. DBus signal dispatched (tag-routed, subscribers filtered by rule)\n\n**Cascading mutation rule**: evaluate full mutation closure before any CoW lands — Btrfs transaction + tag router transaction must be atomic.\n\n## OSCAL Schema Updates\n\n- Tags are OSCAL schema-defined vocabulary (inherited, not invented)\n- On OSCAL schema update: Btrfs snapshot → re-evaluate all objects → mutation ledger records `re-tagged: oscal-schema vX → vY`\n- Regulation changes (NIST 800-53 rev, FedRAMP baseline) propagate into enforcement automatically, no code change\n\n## Compliance Rules Format\n\n```toml\n[[rule]]\nid = \"gdpr-residency\"\nwhen = { jurisdiction = \"eu\" }\nenforce.subvolume      = \"eu-west\"\nenforce.replicate      = [\"eu-west-1\", \"eu-central-1\"]\nenforce.replicate_deny = [\"us-*\", \"ap-*\"]\nenforce.retention_max  = \"730d\"\n\n[[rule]]\nid = \"gdpr-pii\"\nwhen = { classification = \"pii\" }\nenforce.tier             = \"cold\"\nenforce.dbus_subscribers = \"credentialed-only\"\nenforce.erasure_audit    = true\nenforce.audit_verbosity  = \"full\"\n\n[[rule]]\nid = \"nis2-critical\"\nwhen = { sensitivity = \"critical-infrastructure\" }\nenforce.snapshot_interval = \"60s\"\nenforce.audit_retention   = \"2555d\"   # 7 years\nenforce.alert_on_change   = [\"soc\"]\n```\n\n- Tag store is append-only, ingestor only accepts signed OSCAL documents\n- Rule conflict resolution: compliance rules declared `override: true` always win (strictest constraint)\n\n## Commercial Value\n\n- Audit trail = Btrfs CoW history + mutation ledger (no separate audit DB)\n- Evidence of enforcement: rule file in git, snapshot history proves what moved where and when\n- Operator cannot downgrade compliance classification — social engineering attack surface eliminated\n- OSCAL document IS the system security plan in the legal sense — enforcement is automatic\n\n**Why:** First enterprise / EU regulatory client target. Architecture positions 3tched as a platform where compliance is structural, not bolted on.\n**How to apply:** Reference this when scoping enterprise features, NVIDIA Inception application, or any compliance-adjacent work.\n/home/jeremy/.claude/projects/-home-jeremy-git-operation-dbus-proto/memory/project_cognitive_mcp_architecture.md\n---\nname: project_cognitive_mcp_architecture\ndescription: \"cognitive-mcp is the universal shim/gateway for ALL external clients — droid, NotebookLM, Cursor, Codex, Junie. Do not suggest alternatives.\"\nmetadata: \n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: 530852a9-02e8-4af8-bdf1-8d45b02180a7\n---\n\n# Cognitive-MCP is the Universal Gateway\n\n**cognitive-mcp is THE shim for every external client. This is settled architecture — do not re-derive or suggest alternatives.**\n\n- **NotebookLM** → cognitive-mcp (gRPC)\n- **Droid (factory.ai Android)** → cognitive-mcp\n- **Cursor / Codex / Junie / Gemini CLI** → cognitive-mcp (MCP over HTTP, port 3003)\n- **Chatbot** → compact-mcp (127.0.0.1:11435, loopback only, never exposed)\n\n**Why:** cognitive-mcp has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the right protocol surface. It is the single integration point — not mcp-proxy, not op-assistant-grpc directly, not a new service.\n\n**op-mcp-http (mcp-proxy on :11435)** is a legacy fallback only — droid was temporarily using it but the correct path is cognitive-mcp.\n\n**compact-mcp (:11436)** is loopback only — chatbot uses it internally, never exposed externally.\n\n**Do not suggest:**\n- Pointing external clients at op-assistant-grpc directly\n- Creating new shim services\n- Using mcp-proxy as the primary path for droid\n- Exposing compact-mcp externally\n/home/jeremy/.claude/projects/-home-jeremy-git-operation-dbus-proto/memory/project_identity_injection.md\n---\nname: project-identity-injection\ndescription: xraqy injects HTTP identity headers; WireGuard/grpc-uplink is just transport. NFS and other sub-HTTP protocols must use IP as the identity anchor.\nmetadata: \n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: 4a334c22-6350-49bc-b5f8-69de52553252\n---\n\nxraqy performs identity injection via HTTP headers. WireGuard (grpc-uplink, gateway `10.200.0.1`) is the doorman — it provides the tunnel but carries no identity itself. The IP `10.200.0.1` is \"left behind\" when identity injection happens at the HTTP layer.\n\n**Why:** For HTTP services, the real identity is the injected header, not the source IP. The IP is transport, not auth.\n\n**How to apply:** Protocols that live below HTTP (NFS, raw TCP, gRPC without metadata) must use the WireGuard peer IP (`10.200.0.1`) as the access control anchor, since header-based identity isn't available there. When designing access control for non-HTTP services, IP/subnet is the correct signal — don't conflate it with xraqy identity.\n\nRelated: [[project_compliance_architecture]], [[project_3tched_architecture]]\n/home/jeremy/.claude/projects/-home-jeremy-git-operation-dbus-proto/memory/artix-s6-layout.md\n---\nname: artix-s6-layout\ndescription: \"Artix Linux s6 service layout — exact structure for adding services, canonical deploy script\"\nmetadata: \n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: 530852a9-02e8-4af8-bdf1-8d45b02180a7\n---\n\n# Artix Linux S6 Layout\n\nThis host runs **Artix Linux** with s6-rc. Service sources live in `/etc/s6/sv/`, compiled DB at `/etc/s6/rc/compiled`.\n\n## Canonical workflow for adding a new service\n\n### 1. Create source files in the deploy tree (git-tracked)\n\n```\ndeploy/s6/op-<name>-srv/\n  run              — executable sh script, use `exec s6-setuidgid jeremy /usr/local/bin/<binary>`\n  type             — contains \"longrun\"\n  notification-fd  — contains \"3\"\n  producer-for     — contains \"op-<name>-log\"\n  dependencies.d/\n    dbus-session   — empty file (dependency)\n    op-cognitive-mcp — empty file (if needs memory)\n\ndeploy/s6/op-<name>-log/\n  run              — execlineb logger script (see template below)\n  type             — contains \"longrun\"\n  notification-fd  — contains \"3\"\n  consumer-for     — contains \"op-<name>-srv\"\n  pipeline-name    — contains \"op-<name>\"\n```\n\n### 2. Logger run script template (execlineb)\n\n```\n#!/bin/execlineb -P\nenvfile -I /etc/s6/config/op-<name>.conf\nimportas -sCuD \"n5 s2000000 T\" DIRECTIVES DIRECTIVES\nifelse { test -w /var/log } {\n\tforeground { install -d -o s6log -g s6log /var/log/op-<name> }\n\ts6-setuidgid s6log exec -c s6-log -d3 -b -- ${DIRECTIVES} /var/log/op-<name>\n}\nforeground { install -d -o s6log -g s6log /run/log/op-<name> }\ns6-setuidgid s6log exec -c s6-log -d3 -b -- ${DIRECTIVES} /run/log/op-<name>\n```\n\nRequires an empty conf file: `sudo touch /etc/s6/config/op-<name>.conf`\n\n### 3. Copy to live system\n\n```bash\nsudo cp -r deploy/s6/op-<name>-srv /etc/s6/sv/\nsudo cp -r deploy/s6/op-<name>-log /etc/s6/sv/\n```\n\n### 4. Register in the s6 frontend source tree\n\nNew services need symlinks in the `active/` and `usable/` source directories:\n\n```bash\nfor svc in op-<name>-srv op-<name>-log; do\n  sudo ln -sf \"../../.atomics/${svc}\" \"/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/active/${svc}\"\ndone\nsudo ln -sf \"../../.atomics/op-<name>-srv\" \"/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/usable/op-<name>-srv\"\n```\n\nAlso add to a bundle's `contents.d/`:\n```bash\nsudo touch /etc/s6/sv/misc/contents.d/op-<name>-srv\n```\n\n### 5. Compile and install (when .ref rebuild works)\n\n```bash\nsudo s6 set commit --default-bundle=system-default\nsudo s6 live install\nsudo s6 live start op-<name>-srv\n```\n\n**Current blocker:** `s6 set commit` fails with `rpcbind-srv is not a valid identifier in .ref` when adding services not yet in the compiled `.ref` database. The `.ref` at `/etc/s6/repo/compiled/.ref` needs a full rebuild. Workaround: add startup to `rc-local/up`.\n\n## Key paths\n\n| Path | Purpose |\n|------|---------|\n| `/etc/s6/sv/` | Live service source definitions (= `.atomics/` symlink target) |\n| `/etc/s6/repo/compiled/current` | Active compiled s6-rc DB |\n| `/etc/s6/repo/compiled/.ref` | Working-set reference DB (separate from live) |\n| `/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/active/` | Symlinks to services included in compilation |\n| `/etc/s6/repo/sources/current/usable/` | Symlinks to services enabled at boot |\n| `/etc/s6/repo/stores/0000/` | Store 0 = mirrors `/etc/s6/sv/` service dirs |\n| `/etc/s6/repo/stores/0001/` | Store 1 = extra services (mount-filesystems, network) |\n| `/etc/s6/config/*.conf` | Logger directive files (can be empty) |\n\n## Do NOT use\n\n- `s6 set commit` without `--default-bundle` — fails with \"bundle default already defined\"\n- Manual symlinks into `/run/service/` — wrong approach, s6-svscan manages that\n- `pipeline-name` file value must NOT match the service directory name — causes duplicate definition compile error\n\n## Environment variables in run scripts\n\nUse `export VAR=\"${VAR:-default}\"` pattern. For secrets, use `/etc/s6/sv/<name>/env/` directory (one file per variable, filename = var name, file content = value), accessed via `exec s6-envdir ./env ...` or `s6-setuidgid`.\n/home/jeremy/.claude/projects/-home-jeremy-git-operation-dbus-proto/memory/project_zero_trust_principle.md\n---\nname: project-zero-trust-principle\ndescription: \"Core zero-trust principle — xraqy/WireGuard identity is the only gate. Network-layer security (IP ACLs, firewall rules, port restrictions) is theater and should be masked, not enforced.\"\nmetadata: \n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: 4a334c22-6350-49bc-b5f8-69de52553252\n---\n\nWireGuard key = identity ticket. xraqy validates the key at entry and stamps every downstream HTTP request with the WireGuard identity as a header (the wristband). After that, no WireGuard trace exists — no signature, no fingerprint. The transport is invisible and irrelevant.\n\n**The principle:** Once past xraqy, every request carries the identity in the header. Network position (IP, subnet, port) tells you nothing and should not be trusted. All OpenClaw/network-layer security is redundant masking — the real gate is already upstream at xraqy.\n\n**Implications:**\n- IP-based ACLs and firewall rules are theater — mask them, don't rely on them\n- NFS exports with `/32` or subnet restrictions are the old model — wrong layer\n- Any service that gates by source IP is not zero-trust\n- Protocols that can't read the identity header (NFS, raw TCP) don't belong on the network surface — either proxy them through an identity-aware layer or replace with identity-native protocols (SSHFS, etc.)\n- `root_squash` and similar in-protocol controls are fine as defense-in-depth, but not the primary gate\n\n**The model:** Check your car (WireGuard) with the valet (xraqy). Get your wristband (identity header). Everyone downstream sees the wristband — no one cares what car you drove.\n\nRelated: [[project-identity-injection]], [[project_compliance_architecture]]\n/home/jeremy/.claude/projects/-home-jeremy-git-operation-dbus-proto/memory/feedback_separate_commands.md\n---\nname: feedback-separate-commands\ndescription: \"Run bash commands separately, not chained with && or ;\"\nmetadata: \n  node_type: memory\n  type: feedback\n  originSessionId: b6c07e5a-dbdf-4751-9640-666a7981410c\n---\n\nAlways run bash commands as separate tool calls, not combined with `&&`, `;`, or piped together unnecessarily.\n\n**Why:** User preference for clarity and separation.\n\n**How to apply:** When running multiple commands, issue each as its own Bash tool call instead of chaining them in one call.\n/home/jeremy/.claude/projects/-home-jeremy-git-operation-dbus-proto/memory/project_incus_boot_wedge.md\n---\nname: project-incus-boot-wedge\ndescription: Incus mail-3tched container in ERROR/wedged state blocking clean TTY boot — fix via live CD chroot + sqlite\nmetadata: \n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: ee39c8ab-58c9-4811-986d-211d78a565c4\n---\n\n# Incus Boot Wedge — Active Incident (2026-06-02)\n\n## Symptom\nSystem boots but does not get a full TTY. Currently accessible only via TTY 12 (degraded). s6 `incus` service is up (pid 603) but the boot sequence is wedged.\n\n## Root Cause\n`mail-3tched` Incus container is in ERROR state (`Invalid PID -1`). Its config has:\n- `boot.autostart: \"true\"`\n- `volatile.last_state.power: RUNNING`\n\nOn boot, Incus tries to restart it, fails with `Invalid PID -1`, and hangs/errors in a way that blocks clean TTY initialization.\n\n## Why We Can't Fix Live\n- `incus list` works from the degraded TTY (incusd is running, pid 603)\n- BUT `incus stop --force` would acquire the Incus **global lock** and likely hang on the already-wedged container, making things worse\n\n## Fix Plan — Live CD Chroot\n\n### 1. Boot Artix live USB, mount root partition and chroot in\n\n```bash\n# example — adjust /dev/sdXN to actual root partition\nmount /dev/sdXN /mnt\nmount --bind /proc /mnt/proc\nmount --bind /sys /mnt/sys\nmount --bind /dev /mnt/dev\nchroot /mnt\n```\n\n### 2. Edit Incus local sqlite DB directly\n\n```bash\nsqlite3 /var/lib/incus/database/local.db\n```\n\nInside sqlite3, find and fix mail-3tched's config keys:\n\n```sql\n-- Check current state\nSELECT * FROM instances WHERE name='mail-3tched';\nSELECT * FROM instances_config WHERE instance_id=(SELECT id FROM instances WHERE name='mail-3tched');\n\n-- Fix last_state.power so incus doesn't try to restart it\nUPDATE instances_config \n  SET value='STOPPED' \n  WHERE key='volatile.last_state.power' \n  AND instance_id=(SELECT id FROM instances WHERE name='mail-3tched');\n\n-- Disable autostart so it doesn't try again on next boot\nUPDATE instances_config \n  SET value='false' \n  WHERE key='boot.autostart' \n  AND instance_id=(SELECT id FROM instances WHERE name='mail-3tched');\n\n.quit\n```\n\n### 3. Exit chroot and reboot\n\n```bash\nexit\numount /mnt/dev /mnt/sys /mnt/proc\numount /mnt\nreboot\n```\n\n## After Reboot\n- Verify full TTY is restored\n- `sudo incus list` — mail-3tched should show STOPPED and not ERROR\n- Investigate what broke mail-3tched (likely a proxy device socket or storage issue)\n- mail-3tched has proxy devices for IMAP/IMAPS/SMTP pointing at unix sockets under `/run/mail-3tched/` — check those exist\n\n## Container Config Notes (mail-3tched)\n- Image: Debian trixie amd64\n- Proxy devices: mail-imap (143), mail-imaps (993), mail-smtp — all via unix sockets on host at `/run/mail-3tched/`\n- Disk device: `/run/op-dbus/session-bus.sock` mounted into container at `/run/host-op-dbus/session-bus.sock`\n/home/jeremy/.claude/projects/-home-jeremy-git-operation-dbus-proto/memory/MEMORY.md\n# Memory Index\n\n- [3tched Architecture](project_3tched_architecture.md) — 31-crate Rust workspace; socket networking (Unix domain sockets + OVS OpenFlow); Incus containers; gRPC over UDS internally\n- [WARP fwmark routing](feedback_warp_fmark.md) — WARP tunnel uses fwmark + table 51820, not default route; eth0 default route is separate\n- [Artix Linux s6 layout](artix-s6-layout.md) — Chimera-derived s6; use `s6` CLI (not s6-db-reload); service defs in /etc/s6/sv/; `s6 set commit` has a \"bundle default already defined\" issue to resolve\n- [Compliance Architecture](project_compliance_architecture.md) — Btrfs+overlayfs+SHM CoW tiers; OSCAL-driven tag routing; three tag classes (OSCAL/3tched/UI); every mutation is enforcement point; enterprise/EU regulatory target\n- [Cognitive MCP Architecture](project_cognitive_mcp_architecture.md) — cognitive-mcp is the universal gateway for ALL external clients (droid, NotebookLM, Cursor, Codex, Junie). Compact-mcp is loopback/chatbot only. Never suggest alternatives.\n- [Identity Injection](project_identity_injection.md) — xraqy injects HTTP identity headers; WireGuard (grpc-uplink, 10.200.0.1) is transport only. Sub-HTTP protocols (NFS, raw TCP) must use the peer IP as identity anchor.\n- [Zero Trust Principle](project_zero_trust_principle.md) — xraqy/WG identity header is the ONLY gate. IP ACLs, firewall rules, port restrictions are theater — mask them. Protocols that can't read the wristband header don't belong on the network surface.\n- [Separate Commands](feedback_separate_commands.md) — Run bash commands as separate tool calls, not chained with && or ;\n- [Incus Boot Wedge](project_incus_boot_wedge.md) — mail-3tched ERROR state blocks TTY boot; fix via live CD chroot + sqlite3 edit of local.db (do NOT use incus stop — causes global lock hang)\n"}}

{\n        *self.dbus_connection.write().await = Some(connection);\n    }\n\n    pub async fn hydrate_catalog_from_store(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let Some(store) = &self.schema_catalog_store else {\n            return Ok(());\n        };\n\n        for document in store.list_documents().await? {\n            self.schema_catalog.write().register(document.schema);\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub async fn register(&self, plugin: Arc<dyn StatePlugin>) -> Result<()> {\n        let name = plugin.name().to_string();\n        let storage_path = self.plugin_storage_path(&name);\n        tokio::fs::create_dir_all(&storage_path).await?;\n\n        let dbus_path = Self::plugin_dbus_path(&name);\n\n        if let Some(schema) = plugin.schema() {\n            self.schema_catalog.write().register(schema.clone());\n\n            if let Some(store) = &self.schema_catalog_store {\n                let document = CatalogDocument {\n                    schema: schema.clone(),\n                    dbus_path: dbus_path.clone(),\n                    service_name: \"org.opdbus.v1\".to_string(),\n                    storage_path: storage_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),\n                    source: \"plugin\".to_string(),\n                };\n                store.upsert_document(&document).await?;\n            }\n\n            if let Some(publisher) = &*self.publisher.read().await {\n                let _ = publisher\n                    .publish_change(\n                        name.clone(),\n                        format!(\"schema/{}\", name),\n                        ChangeType::PropertySet,\n                        Some(\"definition\".to_string()),\n                        None,\n                        schema.to_json_schema(),\n                        vec![\"schema\".to_string(), \"plugin\".to_string()],\n                        \"PluginSchema\".to_string(),\n                    )\n                    .await;\n            }\n        } else {\n            warn!(\n                \"Plugin {} has no PluginSchema; it will not enter the schema catalog\",\n                name\n            );\n        }\n\n        if let Some(connection) = &*self.dbus_connection.read().await {\n            let host = op_state::dbus_server::PluginDbusHost {\n                plugin: plugin.clone(),\n                schema_registry: self.schema_catalog.clone(),\n            };\n            if let Err(error) = connection\n                .object_server()\n                .at(dbus_path.as_str(), host)\n                .await\n            {\n                debug!(\"Plugin {} D-Bus host export skipped: {}\", name, error);\n            }\n        }\n\n        self.plugins.write().await.insert(\n            name.clone(),\n            PluginRecord {\n                name,\n                plugin,\n                storage_path,\n                dbus_path,\n            },\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub async fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Arc<dyn StatePlugin>> {\n        self.plugins\n            .read()\n            .await\n            .get(name)\n            .map(|record| record.plugin.clone())\n    }\n\n    pub async fn records(&self) -> Vec<PluginRecord> {\n        self.plugins.read().await.values().cloned().collect()\n    }\n\n    fn plugin_storage_path(&self, name: &str) -> PathBuf {\n        self.base_path.join(Self::sanitize_path_segment(name))\n    }\n\n    fn plugin_dbus_path(name: &str) -> String {\n        format!(\"/opdbus/v1/plugins/{}\", Self::sanitize_path_segment(name))\n    }\n\n    fn sanitize_path_segment(segment: &str) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::with_capacity(segment.len());\n        for ch in segment.chars() {\n            if ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || ch == '_' {\n                out.push(ch);\n            } else {\n                out.push('_');\n            }\n        }\n\n        if out.is_empty() {\n            \"_\".to_string()\n        } else {\n            out\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for PluginRegistry {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new(\"/var/lib/op-dbus/plugins\")\n    }\n}\n"}}

only]\\n    G -->|No| I[build full embedding input: user_msg + assistant_resp + conversation_id]\\n    H --> J[call Voyage AI voyage-4-lite input_type document]\\n    I --> J\\n    J --> K{Voyage -->|No| O[upsert to ctl_plane_chat_turns — full payload]\\n    N --> P[store hash in dedup cache]\\n    O --> P\\n    P --> Q[emit chat_turn.vectorized span]\\n```\\n\\n### Process 4: Reasoning    C --> D[write full record to audit_event log — REQ 12.3]\\n    D --> E[enqueue to ReasoningEpisodeWorker non-blocking — REQ 8.2]\\n    E --> F[worker: check dedup cache]\\n    F --> G{hash seen within 24h?}\\n    G -->|Yes| H[skip upsert]\\n    G -->|No| I{pii_flagged?}\\n    I -->|Yes| J[embedding input: outcome_class + tools_consulted only]\\n    I -->|No| K[embedding input: reasoning_summary + goal_text + outcome_class + tools_consulted]\\n    J --> L[call Voyage AI voyage-4-lite input_type document]\\n    K --> L\\n    L --> M{Voyage OK?}\\n    M -->|No| N[retain job + exponential backoff retry — record not lost]\\n    M -->|Yes| O{pii_flagged?}\\n    O -->|Yes| P[upsert to ctl_plane_reasoning_episodes — omit reasoning_summary decision_output]\\n    O -->|No| Q[upsert to ctl_plane_reasoning_episodes — full payload]\\n    P --> R[store hash in dedup cache]\\n    Q --> R\\n    R --> S[emit reasoning_episode.vectorized span]\\n```\\n\\n### Process 5: Plugin Shutdown (NFR-2 reverse order)\\n\\n```mermaid\\nflowchart TD\\n    A[plugin shutdown signal] --> B[ReasoningEpisodeWorker::shutdown_drain]\\n    B --> C{drain timeout?}\\n    C -->|No| D[all in-flight jobs complete or checkpointed]\\n    C -->|Yes| E[checkpoint remaining jobs to retry queue]\\n    D --> F[ChatTurnWorker::shutdown_drain]\\n    E --> F\\n    F --> G[ChatActorHandle::shutdown_graceful — wait for in-flight turns]\\n    G --> H[deregister SledIdentityGate from op-mcp server]\\n    H --> I[revoke WG peer registration in CozoDB soft-revoke flag]\\n    I --> J[remove sled entry from /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat — zero the struct]\\n    J --> K[shutdown complete]\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Error Handling Strategy\\n\\n### Initialization Failures\\n\\nAny failure at or before the IdentitySled write (steps 1–2 of NFR-1) MUST abort startup:\\nlog a structured `error!` with `plugin_id`, `step`, and `cause`, then return `Err` from\\n`initialize()`. The registry will not add the plugin to the active plugin list.\\n\\nAny failure after the sled write (steps 3–7) follows the same abort policy unless the\\nfailure is in a worker that supports isolated restart (turn worker, episode worker). These\\nworkers restart automatically up to `max_actor_restarts` times before aborting the entire\\nplugin.\\n\\n### Compact MCP Gate Fallback\\n\\nIf `SledIdentityGate::evaluate` encounters any error (missing file, mmap failure, invalid\\nsled bytes), it returns `FullListSledUnavailable` and emits `warn!(sled_unavailable = true)`.\\nTool serving is never blocked. The three variants of `CompactDecision` make all outcomes\\nexplicit at the type level — there is no implicit fallback or boolean ambiguity.\\n\\n### Voyage API Failures\\n\\nBoth workers retry with exponential backoff starting at `voyage_base_backoff_ms` (default\\n250 ms), doubling per attempt up to `voyage_max_retries` (default 8) attempts. After\\nexhausting retries, the job is written to a dead-letter queue (an append-only file at\\n`/var/lib/op-dbus/chatbot-dl-queue.jsonl`) for manual recovery. The episode record in the\\naudit log is never modified or lost.\\n\\n### Chat Actor Crashes\\n\\n`ChatActorHandle` monitors its task `JoinHandle`. On unexpected exit, it spawns a new actor\\ninstance within `actor_restart_delay_ms` and increments `restart_count`. If `restart_count`\\nexceeds `max_actor_restarts`, the plugin marks itself as `ActorStatus::Degraded` and emits\\nan alert. The `CtlPlaneChatbotHealth` struct surfaces `actor_status` and `actor_restart_count`\\nas discrete fields so monitoring systems can distinguish a momentary restart from a degraded\\nstate.\\n\\n### Queue Depth Alert\\n\\nA background ticker checks combined queue depth every 5 seconds. If\\n`turn_worker.queue_depth() + episode_worker.queue_depth()` exceeds `queue_alert_threshold`\\n(default 50), it emits a `warn!(combined_queue_depth, threshold_exceeded = true)` event.\\nThe per-worker fields `chat_turn_queue_depth` and `episode_queue_depth` in\\n`CtlPlaneChatbotHealth` allow callers to identify which worker is the bottleneck.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Testing Strategy\\n\\n### Unit Tests\\n\\n- `SledIdentityGate::evaluate` — test `Compact` path (pubkey match), `FullList` path\\n  (mismatch), and `FullListSledUnavailable` path (missing file, zero sled). All three\\n  `CompactDecision` variants must be covered.\\n- `ReasoningStateTracker` — test flat policy (extend episode), nesting policy (child episode),\\n  all exit triggers produce correct `exit_reason` and `outcome_class`\\n- `TurnRecord` and `ReasoningEpisodeRecord` — content_hash determinism, PII redaction fields\\n- Deduplication cache — hash hit within window skips upsert, expiry after window allows upsert\\n- `CtlPlaneChatbotHealth` — assert `chat_turn_queue_depth` and `episode_queue_depth` reflect\\n  live `AtomicU64` values from the respective workers; assert `actor_restart_count` increments\\n  on each supervised restart\\n\\n### Integration Tests\\n\\n- Plugin initialization sequence: assert each step completes before the next starts; assert\\n  sled write failure halts before CozoDB upsert\\n- Compact gate: mock sled file, assert `op-mcp` server routes to compact interface when pubkey\\n  matches (`Compact`), full list when it does not (`FullList`), and full list with warning log\\n  when sled is absent (`FullListSledUnavailable`)\\n- Turn vectorization end-to-end: inject a `TurnRecord` into the worker, mock Voyage + Qdrant,\\n  assert span emitted and payload correct\\n- Episode vectorization end-to-end: same pattern with `ReasoningEpisodeRecord`\\n- PII path: assert `user_message`/`assistant_response` absent from Qdrant payload when flagged\\n\\n### Observability Validation\\n\\n- Assert `reasoning_episode.vectorized` span carries all required attributes (REQ-14.1)\\n- Assert `chat_turn.vectorized` span carries all required attributes (REQ-14.2)\\n- Assert queue-depth alert fires when depth exceeds 50 (REQ-14.3)\\n- Assert `query_current_state()` reports `chat_turn_queue_depth` and `episode_queue_depth`\\n  as separate named fields in `CtlPlaneChatbotHealth` (REQ-14.4)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Open Questions (Carried from Requirements)\\n\\n| # | Question | Design Impact |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| OQ-1 | Nesting policy default — flat confirmed for v1? | `ReasoningStateTracker` defaults to `flat`; the nested branch is stubbed but untested |\\n| OQ-2 | `reasoning_summary` — generated by model at close, or separate summarizer? | Design assumes the chat model generates it inline at episode close; a separate summarizer would add a new worker |\\n| OQ-3 | Voyage model final selection — voyage-4-lite vs voyage-4 | `voyage_model` is runtime-configurable; no code change needed after POC |\\n| OQ-4 | Qdrant instance — shared or dedicated? | Design uses environment variable `COGNITIVE_MCP_QDRANT_URL`; shared by default |\\n| OQ-5 | Retry policy — max retries, backoff, dead-letter behavior | Defaults above; DLQ path to `/var/lib/op-dbus/chatbot-dl-queue.jsonl` |\\n| OQ-6 | Shared or separate embedding worker queues? {"timestamp":"2026-06-02T12:21:02.361Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_FsxaTTG6FkIFoioIrnpNZIuq","output":"Chunk ID: d9c7a7\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 692\nOutput:\n# WireGuard Identity Deployment Synopsis\n\n## What Was Deployed\nWe transitioned the core authentication and identity tracking mechanism in OP-DBUS to rely strictly on WireGuard cryptographic public keys rather than auxiliary identifiers like `subid`.\n\n### Key Changes\n1. **Canonical `IdentitySled` (152 Bytes):**\n   - The shared memory sled struct (`op_identity::IdentitySled`) was standardized to exactly 152 bytes.\n   - The `subid` field was entirely dropped from this struct and relegated to dead/unused code (`SubidTaxonomy`).\n\n2. **WireGuard as the Auth Layer:**\n   - Identity is now provided via the `WireGuardIdentity` struct (`crates/op-identity/src/wireguard.rs`), which binds directly to the active WireGuard interface (defaulting to the `netmaker` interface via the `WG_INTERFACE` env var).\n   - Sessions (`crates/op-identity/src/session.rs`) are now generated when a WireGuard peer connects and are explicitly keyed by the peer's WireGuard public key rather than traditional usernames or sub-IDs.\n\n3. **Storage & Audit Layer Alignment:**\n   - Database operations (like `upsert_user` and `create_session` in `op-cozo-store`) have been updated to track users exclusively by `wg_pubkey`.\n   - Strict separation was enforced between standard stateless peers (tracked only by `wg_pubkey`) and \"privacy users\" who carry heavier PII payloads in isolated database operations.\n\n## The Reasoning Behind It\n1. **Delegating Auth to the Network Layer:** By using WireGuard public keys as the ultimate source of truth, we eliminated the need for fragile application-layer authentication tokens (`subid`). If a device is on the WireGuard mesh (e.g., Netmaker) and possesses the private key, it is implicitly authenticated. This drastically reduces the attack surface and code complexity.\n2. **Predictable Memory Footprint:** Standardizing the Sled struct to exactly 152 bytes allows for extremely fast, zero-copy reads from `/dev/shm` across all crates via DBUS IPC, avoiding dynamic JSON parsing bottlenecks in the hot path.\n3. **Decoupling Schemas:** Moving dynamic data (like the active PluginSchema JSON) out of the memory-mapped struct and into dedicated files (like `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`) prevents variable-length data corruption and cleanly separates state (who the user is) from configuration (what schema they are running against).\n\n## Bugs Uncovered\nThis rigid 152-byte enforcement surfaced a bug in `op-cognitive-mcp/src/qdrant_shuttle.rs`. The shuttle was attempting to slice the end of the `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` file under the old assumption that JSON schemas were appended to the identity struct. This logic failed because the file is now strictly truncated to 152 bytes, requiring the shuttle to be repointed to `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`.\n"}}

If a device is on the WireGuard mesh (e.g., Netmaker) and possesses the private key, it is implicitly authenticated. This drastically reduces the attack surface and code complexity.\n2. **Predictable Memory Footprint:** Standardizing the Sled struct to exactly 152 bytes allows for extremely fast, zero-copy reads from `/dev/shm` across all crates via DBUS IPC, avoiding dynamic JSON parsing bottlenecks in the hot path.\n3. **Decoupling Schemas:** Moving dynamic data (like the active PluginSchema JSON) out of the memory-mapped struct and into dedicated files (like `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`) prevents variable-length data corruption and cleanly separates state (who the user is) from configuration (what schema they are running against).\n\n## Bugs Uncovered\nThis rigid 152-byte enforcement surfaced a bug in `op-cognitive-mcp/src/qdrant_shuttle.rs`. {"timestamp":"2026-06-02T12:25:05.814Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Because `100.90.37.254` is already **this host’s Netmaker/WireGuard address**, not a separate chatbot login endpoint.\n\nImportant distinction:\n\n```text\nWireGuard interface address: 100.90.37.254\nService on that address:     100.90.37.254:<port>\nWireGuard identity:          peer public key from an actual WG handshake\n```\n\nIf the chatbot runs on the same machine and connects to `100.90.37.254`, that is just local TCP to the host’s own WG address. It does **not** create a new WireGuard peer handshake, so there is no distinct chatbot `wg_pubkey`, no Snowball session, and no chatbot IdentitySled.\n\nAlso:\n\n- `100.90.37.254` belongs to the existing `netmaker` interface.\n- `/etc/wireguard/3tched.conf` also uses `100.90.37.254`, so it cannot be brought up as a second chatbot client.\n- `compact-mcp` is intentionally loopback only.\n- `cognitive-mcp` listens on `100.90.37.254:3003`, but connecting to it from the same host does not prove chatbot WG identity.\n\nSo the chatbot needs its **own WG client identity**, either:\n\n```text\nchatbot interface: chatbot0 or wg-chatbot\nchatbot IP:        a different 100.90.37.x address\nchatbot pubkey:    its own key\n```\n\nThen boot can do:\n\n```text\nwg-chatbot up\n-> read chatbot pubkey\n-> write /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat\n-> start chatmanager / compact-mcp with WG_PUBKEY=<chatbot pubkey>\n```\n\nConnecting to `100.90.37.254` uses the host identity. {"timestamp":"2026-06-02T12:25:05.820Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"Because `100.90.37.254` is already **this host’s Netmaker/WireGuard address**, not a separate chatbot login endpoint.\n\nImportant distinction:\n\n```text\nWireGuard interface address: 100.90.37.254\nService on that address:     100.90.37.254:<port>\nWireGuard identity:          peer public key from an actual WG handshake\n```\n\nIf the chatbot runs on the same machine and connects to `100.90.37.254`, that is just local TCP to the host’s own WG address. It does **not** create a new WireGuard peer handshake, so there is no distinct chatbot `wg_pubkey`, no Snowball session, and no chatbot IdentitySled.\n\nAlso:\n\n- `100.90.37.254` belongs to the existing `netmaker` interface.\n- `/etc/wireguard/3tched.conf` also uses `100.90.37.254`, so it cannot be brought up as a second chatbot client.\n- `compact-mcp` is intentionally loopback only.\n- `cognitive-mcp` listens on `100.90.37.254:3003`, but connecting to it from the same host does not prove chatbot WG identity.\n\nSo the chatbot needs its **own WG client identity**, either:\n\n```text\nchatbot interface: chatbot0 or wg-chatbot\nchatbot IP:        a different 100.90.37.x address\nchatbot pubkey:    its own key\n```\n\nThen boot can do:\n\n```text\nwg-chatbot up\n-> read chatbot pubkey\n-> write /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat\n-> start chatmanager / compact-mcp with WG_PUBKEY=<chatbot pubkey>\n```\n\nConnecting to `100.90.37.254` uses the host identity. It cannot make the chatbot become a separate WireGuard-authenticated user."}],"phase":"final_answer"}}
