{"timestamp":"2026-06-02T12:25:37.227Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Right: users access gRPC at `100.90.37.254` **after** they are already on the WireGuard mesh.\n\nThe difference is where the packet originates.\n\nRemote user flow:\n\n```text\nuser device WG peer\n  -> WireGuard handshake proves user's pubkey\n  -> tunnel route to 100.90.37.254\n  -> xray/gRPC gateway injects identity headers\n  -> gRPC sees authenticated identity\n```\n\nLocal chatbot flow today:\n\n```text\nsame host process\n  -> connect 100.90.37.254\n  -> kernel treats it as local address\n  -> no WireGuard handshake\n  -> no distinct chatbot pubkey\n  -> no chatbot identity sled\n```\n\nSo `100.90.37.254` is the correct gateway address, but the chatbot has to approach it like a user, not like a local process.\n\nThat means one of these:\n\n1. Run chatbot in its own Incus container/netns with a chatbot WireGuard client.\n2. Give chatbot its own WG interface in a separate network namespace.\n3. Route chatbot through `wg-xray` so the path is `chatbot WG client -> xray -> identity injection -> gRPC`.\n\nDo not make a second host WG config using `100.90.37.254`; that collides with the host identity. The chatbot needs its own peer key and assigned mesh IP, then it can connect to `100.90.37.254` exactly like every other user.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-02T12:26:07.189Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes. The chatbot must connect through the same WireGuard ingress path as a regular user. Otherwise it never gets a real WG-authenticated session and The Sled stays missing/stale.\n\nCorrect boot model:\n\n```text\nchatbot process\n  -> chatbot WG client/key\n  -> connects through WG mesh to 100.90.37.254\n  -> xray/gateway sees chatbot peer identity\n  -> injects X-Ghostbridge-Footprint / X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID or WG pubkey\n  -> A.N.N.A. Scribe creates Snowball session\n  -> /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat gets populated with chatbot pubkey\n  -> memory loop and compact-mcp can trust chatbot identity\n```\n\nThe important correction: the chatbot does not “get” The Sled as a file from the network. {"timestamp":"2026-06-02T12:27:43.692Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Exactly. The boot dependency should be:\n\n```text\nnetmaker host mesh up\n  -> chatbot starts its own WG client\n  -> chatbot connects to 100.90.37.254:<wireguard-port>\n  -> WG handshake proves chatbot pubkey\n  -> gateway/A.N.N.A. Scribe creates chatbot session\n  -> IdentitySled is written in /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat\n  -> chatmanager / compact-mcp start with valid chatbot identity\n```\n\nCritical detail: the chatbot has to do this from a separate network context, like an Incus container or netns. If it runs in the host namespace and connects to `100.90.37.254`, Linux treats that as local traffic and bypasses the WG login path.\n\nSo the fix is not just env vars. It is boot ordering plus network placement:\n\n```text\nwg-netmaker\n  -> chatbot-netns/container\n  -> wg-chatbot-login\n  -> identity-sled-ready\n  -> chatmanager\n  -> op-mcp-compact\n```\n\nAnd the chatbot WG config must have its own key/IP, not `100.90.37.254`. That address remains the login/gateway target.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n</collaboration_mode>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<apps_instructions>\n## Apps (Connectors)\nApps (Connectors) can be explicitly triggered in user messages in the format `[$app-name](app://{connector_id})`. Apps can also be implicitly triggered as long as the context suggests usage of available apps.\nAn app is equivalent to a set of MCP tools within the `codex_apps` MCP.\nAn installed app's MCP tools are either provided to you already, or can be lazy-loaded through the `tool_search` tool. If `tool_search` is available, the apps that are searchable by `tools_search` will be listed by it.\nDo not additionally call list_mcp_resources or list_mcp_resource_templates for apps.\n</apps_instructions>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<skills_instructions>\n## Skills\nA skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking Critical commands, piping, error handling, scripting. Use when working on macOS or Linux systems.\"\nrisk: unknown\nsource: community\ndate_added: \"2026-02-27\"\n---\n\n# Bash Linux Patterns\n\n> Essential patterns for Bash on Linux/macOS.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Operator Syntax\n\n### Chaining Commands\n\n| Operator | Meaning | Example |\n|----------|---------|---------|\n| `;` | Run sequentially | `cmd1; cmd2` |\n| `&&` | Run if previous succeeded | `npm install && npm run dev` |\n| `\\|\\|` | Run if previous failed | `npm test \\|\\| echo \"Tests failed\"` |\n| `\\|` | Pipe output | `ls \\| grep \".js\"` |\n\n---\n\n## 2. File Operations\n\n### Essential Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n|------|---------|\n| List all | `ls -la` |\n| Find files | `find . -name \"*.js\" -type f` |\n| File content | `cat file.txt` |\n| First N lines | `head -n 20 file.txt` |\n| Last N lines | `tail -n 20 file.txt` |\n| Follow log | `tail -f log.txt` |\n| Search in files | `grep -r \"pattern\" --include=\"*.js\"` |\n| File size | `du -sh *` |\n| Disk usage | `df -h` |\n\n---\n\n## 3. Process Management\n\n| Task | Command |\n|------|---------|\n| List processes | `ps aux` |\n| Find by name | `ps aux \\| grep node` |\n| Kill by PID | `kill -9 <PID>` |\n| Find port user | `lsof -i :3000` |\n| Kill port | `kill -9 $(lsof -t -i :3000)` |\n| Background | `npm run dev &` |\n| Jobs | `jobs -l` |\n| Bring to front | `fg %1` |\n\n---\n\n## 4. Text Processing\n\n### Core Tools\n\n| Tool | Purpose | Example |\n|------|---------|---------|\n| `grep` | Search | `grep -rn \"TODO\" src/` |\n| `sed` | Replace | `sed -i 's/old/new/g' file.txt` |\n| `awk` | Extract columns | `awk '{print $1}' file.txt` |\n| `cut` | Cut fields | `cut -d',' -f1 data.csv` |\n| `sort` | Sort lines | `sort -u file.txt` |\n| `uniq` | Unique lines | `sort file.txt \\| uniq -c` |\n| `wc` | Count | `wc -l file.txt` |\n\n---\n\n## 5. Environment Variables\n\n| Task | Command |\n|------|---------|\n| View all | `env` or `printenv` |\n| View one | `echo $PATH` |\n| Set temporary | `export VAR=\"value\"` |\n| Set in script | `VAR=\"value\" command` |\n| Add to PATH | `export PATH=\"$PATH:/new/path\"` |\n\n---\n\n## 6. Network\n\n| Task | Command |\n|------|---------|\n| Download | `curl -O https://example.com/file` |\n| API request | `curl -X GET https://api.example.com` |\n| POST JSON | `curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"key\":\"value\"}' URL` |\n| Check port | `nc -zv localhost 3000` |\n| Network info | `ifconfig` or `ip addr` |\n\n---\n\n## 7. Script Template\n\n```bash\n#!/bin/bash\nset -euo pipefail  # Exit on error, undefined var, pipe fail\n\n# Colors (optional)\nRED='\\033[0;31m'\nGREEN='\\033[0;32m'\nNC='\\033[0m'\n\n# Script directory\nSCRIPT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"\n\n# Functions\nlog_info() { echo -e \"${GREEN}[INFO]${NC} $1\"; }\nlog_error() { echo -e \"${RED}[ERROR]${NC} $1\" >&2; }\n\n# Main\nmain() {\n    log_info \"Starting...\"\n    # Your logic here\n    log_info \"Done!\"\n}\n\nmain \"$@\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## 8. Common Patterns\n\n### Check if command exists\n\n```bash\nif command -v node &> /dev/null; then\n    echo \"Node is installed\"\nfi\n```\n\n### Default variable value\n\n```bash\nNAME=${1:-\"default_value\"}\n```\n\n### Read file line by line\n\n```bash\nwhile IFS= read -r line; do\n    echo \"$line\"\ndone < file.txt\n```\n\n### Loop over files\n\n```bash\nfor file in *.js; do\n    echo \"Processing $file\"\ndone\n```\n\n---\n\n## 9. Differences from PowerShell\n\n| Task | PowerShell | Bash |\n|------|------------|------|\n| List files | `Get-ChildItem` | `ls -la` |\n| Find files | `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` | `find . -type f` |\n| Environment | `$env:VAR` | `$VAR` |\n| String concat | `\"$a$b\"` | `\"$a$b\"` (same) |\n| Null check | `if ($x)` | `if [ -n \"$x\" ]` |\n| Pipeline | Object-based | Text-based |\n\n---\n\n## 10. Error Handling\n\n### Set options\n\n```bash\nset -e          # Exit on error\nset -u          # Exit on undefined variable\nset -o pipefail # Exit on pipe failure\nset -x          # Debug: print commands\n```\n\n### Trap for cleanup\n\n```bash\ncleanup() {\n    echo \"Cleaning up...\"\n    rm -f /tmp/tempfile\n}\ntrap cleanup EXIT\n```\n\n---\n\n> **Remember:** Bash is text-based. {"timestamp":"2026-06-02T12:38:42.145Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_cjNLp1c3GuLRhlei2IbcEetz","output":"Chunk ID: 04635e\nWall time: 0.0001 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 844\nOutput:\n-rwxr-xr-x 1 root   root    23337152 May 26 16:32 /usr/local/bin/op-cog-admin\n-rwxr-xr-x 2 jeremy jeremy 164783112 Jun  2 01:47 target/debug/op-cog-admin\n//! Minimal admin CLI for the op-cognitive-mcp cozo store.\n//!\n//! Examples:\n//!   op-cog-admin --db /var/lib/op-dbus/cognitive.db user-add <wg_pubkey>\n//!   op-cog-admin --db /var/lib/op-dbus/cognitive.db user-list\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse clap::{Parser, Subcommand};\nuse op_cozo_store::CozoGraphShuttle;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\n\n#[derive(Parser)]\n#[command(name = \"op-cog-admin\", about = \"Cozo store admin for op-cognitive-mcp\")]\nstruct Cli {\n    #[arg(\n        long,\n        env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_DB_PATH\",\n        default_value = \"/var/lib/op-dbus/cognitive.db\"\n    )]\n    db: String,\n    #[command(subcommand)]\n    cmd: Cmd,\n}\n\n#[derive(Subcommand)]\nenum Cmd {\n    /// Insert or refresh a user keyed by wg_pubkey\n    UserAdd { wg_pubkey: String },\n    /// List all users\n    UserList,\n}\n\nfn main() -> Result<()> {\n    let cli = Cli::parse();\n    let shuttle = CozoGraphShuttle::new_persistent(PathBuf::from(&cli.db))\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"opening cozo at {}\", cli.db))?;\n\n    match cli.cmd {\n        Cmd::UserAdd { wg_pubkey } => {\n            shuttle.upsert_user(&wg_pubkey)?;\n            println!(\"ok: user {} upserted\", wg_pubkey);\n        }\n        Cmd::UserList => {\n            let json = shuttle.run_query(\n                \"?[wg_pubkey, created_at] := *users[wg_pubkey, created_at]\",\n                None,\n            )?;\n            println!(\"{}\", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&json)?);\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n        p.insert(\"reason\".into(), DataValue::Str(reason.into()));\n        p.insert(\"cref\".into(), DataValue::Str(control_ref.into()));\n        p.insert(\"ts\".into(), DataValue::Str(now_rfc3339().into()));\n        cozo_run(&self.db, query, p).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"append audit event: {e}\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    // ── Users (wg_pubkey-keyed) ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Insert or refresh a user keyed by WireGuard public key. No PII stored.\n    pub fn upsert_user(&self, wg_pubkey: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        let query = r#\"\n            ?[wg_pubkey, created_at] <- [[$wg, $ts]]\n            :put users { wg_pubkey => created_at }\n        \"#;\n        let mut p: Params = BTreeMap::new();\n        p.insert(\"wg\".into(), DataValue::Str(wg_pubkey.into()));\n        p.insert(\"ts\".into(), DataValue::Str(now_rfc3339().into()));\n        cozo_run(&self.db, query, p).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"upsert user: {e}\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// True if a user row exists for this wg_pubkey.\n    pub fn user_exists(&self, wg_pubkey: &str) -> Result<bool> {\n        let mut p: Params = BTreeMap::new();\n        p.insert(\"wg\".into(), DataValue::Str(wg_pubkey.into()));\n        let r = cozo_run(\n            &self.db,\n            \"?[wg_pubkey] := *users[wg_pubkey, _], wg_pubkey = $wg\",\n            p,\n        )\n        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"user exists: {e}\"))?;\n        Ok(!r.rows.is_empty())\n    }\n\n    // ── Privacy Users (full PII per explicit directive) ─────────────────────────\n\n    pub fn upsert_privacy_user(\n        &self,\n        id: &str,\n        email: &str,\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-02T14:59:37.676Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes. If SSH is meant to be reachable only through the tunnels, `0.0.0.0` is a simpler and more reliable bind than pinning `100.90.37.254`, because it avoids the boot-time race where `sshd` starts before WireGuard exists.\n\nThe important part is not the bind address by itself, it’s that the firewall and routing keep SSH off the public WAN and only reachable over the tunnel paths. On this host, the current problem was the `ListenAddress 100.90.37.254:22` binding too early; `0.0.0.0` would sidestep that.\n\nTwo sane options:\n1. Switch `sshd` to `0.0.0.0` and keep access control in firewall/tunnel policy.\n2. Keep the Netmaker-only bind, but make `sshd-srv` depend on `wg-netmaker` so it starts after the interface exists.\n\nI already proved the SSH path works once the interface is up, so this is now a policy choice rather than a tunnel failure.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

If SSH is meant to be reachable only through the tunnels, `0.0.0.0` is a simpler and more reliable bind than pinning `100.90.37.254`, because it avoids the boot-time race where `sshd` starts before WireGuard exists.\n\nThe important part is not the bind address by itself, it’s that the firewall and routing keep SSH off the public WAN and only reachable over the tunnel paths. On this host, the current problem was the `ListenAddress 100.90.37.254:22` binding too early; `0.0.0.0` would sidestep that.\n\nTwo sane options:\n1. Switch `sshd` to `0.0.0.0` and keep access control in firewall/tunnel policy.\n2. Keep the Netmaker-only bind, but make `sshd-srv` depend on `wg-netmaker` so it starts after the interface exists.\n\nI already proved the SSH path works once the interface is up, so this is now a policy choice rather than a tunnel failure."}],"phase":"final_answer"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-02T16:57:01.612Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"The script that connects the chatbot to identity is:\n\n[deploy/s6/wg-chatbot/shell_up](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/deploy/s6/wg-chatbot/shell_up:4)\n\nThat does the boot identity work:\n\n```sh\niface=\"${OP_CHATBOT_WG_INTERFACE:-wg-chatbot}\"\nconf=\"${OP_CHATBOT_WG_CONF:-/etc/wireguard/wg-chatbot.conf}\"\nsled_bin=\"${OP_IDENTITY_SLED_BIN:-/usr/local/bin/op-identity-sled}\"\n\nwg-quick up \"$conf\"\npubkey=\"$(wg show \"$iface\" public-key)\"\nWG_INTERFACE=\"$iface\" WG_PUBKEY=\"$pubkey\" \"$sled_bin\" --refresh --iface \"$iface\" --pretty\n```\n\nThe chatbot process then receives that identity through:\n\n[deploy/s6/chatmanager/run](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/deploy/s6/chatmanager/run:8)\n\nThat exports `WG_INTERFACE=wg-chatbot` and `WG_PUBKEY`, then starts `/usr/local/bin/op-chat`.\n\nThe Rust side that registers chatbot as a Cozo user is:\n\n[main.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-chat/src/main.rs:37)\n\nIt calls `op_identity::WireGuardIdentity::new()`, reads `WG_PUBKEY`, and runs `cozo_arc.upsert_user(&pubkey)`.\n\nSo the chain is:\n\n`wg-chatbot/shell_up` -> `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` via `op-identity-sled` -> `chatmanager/run` exports `WG_PUBKEY` -> `op-chat` registers that pubkey in Cozo.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking prost_types::{value::Kind as ProstKind, Struct as ProstStruct, Value as ProstValue};\nuse tokio::sync::RwLock;\nuse tonic::transport::{Channel, Endpoint};\nuse tracing::info;\n\nuse crate::proto::{\n    event_chain_service_client::EventChainServiceClient,\n    plugin_service_client::PluginServiceClient, state_sync_client::StateSyncClient,\n    CallMethodRequest, GetStateRequest, MutateRequest, address: String,\n    pub tls_enabled: bool,\n    pub connect_timeout: Duration,\n    pub request_timeout: Duration,\n}\n\nimpl Default for RemoteEndpoint {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            address: \"http://127.0.0.1:50051\".to_string(),\n            tls_enabled: false,\n            connect_timeout: Duration::from_secs(5),\n            request_timeout: Duration::from_secs(30),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// gRPC client pool for connecting to remote Operation services\npub struct GrpcClientPool {\n    /// Map of endpoint address to channel\n    channels: RwLock<HashMap<String, Channel>>,\n    /// Default endpoint configuration\n    default_config: RemoteEndpoint,\n}\n\nimpl Default for GrpcClientPool {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl GrpcClientPool {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            channels: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),\n            default_config: RemoteEndpoint::default(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn with_default_config(config: RemoteEndpoint) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            channels: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),\n            default_config: config,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get or create a channel to the specified address (supports comma-separated endpoints for load balancing)\n    async fn get_channel(&self, address: &str) -> Result<Channel, GrpcClientError> {\n        {\n            let channels = self.channels.read().await;\n            if let Some(channel) = channels.get(address) {\n                return Ok(channel.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        let addrs: Vec<&str> = address\n            .split(',')\n            .map(|s| s.trim())\n            .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())\n            .collect();\n\n        let channel = if addrs.len() > 1 {\n            // Native Tonic Load Balancing\n            let endpoints = addrs\n                .into_iter()\n                .map(|addr| {\n                    Endpoint::from_shared(addr.to_string()).map(|e| {\n                        e.connect_timeout(self.default_config.connect_timeout)\n                            .timeout(self.default_config.request_timeout)\n                    })\n                })\n                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()\n                .map_err(|e| {\n                    GrpcClientError::ConnectionFailed(format!(\"Invalid endpoint: {}\", e))\n                })?;\n\n            Channel::balance_list(endpoints.into_iter())\n        } else {\n            // Single endpoint\n            let endpoint = Endpoint::from_shared(address.to_string())\n                .map_err(|e| GrpcClientError::ConnectionFailed(e.to_string()))?\n serde_to_prost_value(&serde_value)\n}\n\nfn serde_to_prost_value(value: &serde_json::Value) -> ProstValue {\n    match value {\n        serde_json::Value::Null => ProstValue {\n            kind: Some(ProstKind::StringValue(s.clone())),\n        },\n        serde_json::Value::Array(arr) => ProstValue {\n            kind: Some(ProstKind::ListValue(prost_types::ListValue {\n {"timestamp":"2026-06-02T17:58:24.278Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_je84X81GmxAXnFfQZhdmWvcP","output":"Chunk ID: e4a883\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 805\nOutput:\n        return Err(std::io::Error::new(\n            std::io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied,\n            format!(\n                \"Zero-Btrfs Overhead violation: {} is on filesystem type {}, not tmpfs\",\n                parent.display(),\n                buf.f_type\n            ),\n        ));\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n// ── Writer side (called from SchemaEngine) ───────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Atomically write the active sled into `/dev/shm`.\n///\n/// Uses a tmp-file + rename so readers never see a partial write.\n/// Aborts if the target path is not on tmpfs (Zero-Btrfs Overhead rule).\npub fn write_sled(sled: &IdentitySled) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    assert_tmpfs_or_abort(SHM_SLED_PATH)?;\n\n    let tmp = format!(\"{}.tmp\", SHM_SLED_PATH);\n    let bytes: &[u8] = unsafe {\n        std::slice::from_raw_parts(sled as *const IdentitySled as *const u8, IdentitySled::SIZE)\n    };\n    let mut f = File::create(&tmp)?;\n    f.write_all(bytes)?;\n    f.sync_data()?;\n    fs::rename(&tmp, SHM_SLED_PATH)?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n// ── Reader side (the Shuttle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Read the sled from shm — zero copy, no allocation.\n///\n/// # Safety\n/// The caller must ensure no concurrent writer is modifying the file\n/// mid-read.  `write_sled` uses rename so this is safe in practice.\npub fn read_sled() -> std::io::Result<(*const IdentitySled, memmap2::Mmap)> {\n    let file = File::open(SHM_SLED_PATH)?;\n    let mmap = unsafe { MmapOptions::new().len(IdentitySled::SIZE).map(&file)? };\n    let ptr = mmap.as_ptr() as *const IdentitySled;\n    Ok((ptr, mmap))\n}\n\n// ── Unix socket endpoint ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A unix socket endpoint proxied into an xray inbound + outbound pair.\n///\n/// Declared via `UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS=label:path:port[,…]`, e.g.:\n///   `qdrant:/run/qdrant.sock:6334`\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct SocketEntry {\n    /// Xray tag suffix (e.g. `\"qdrant\"`) — becomes `\"to-<label>\"` / `\"<label>-in\"`.\n    pub label: String,\n    /// Filesystem path of the unix domain socket.\n    pub path: String,\n    /// Local TCP port xray should listen on and proxy into the socket.\n    pub port: u16,\n}\n\n/// Parse `UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS` env var into a list of `SocketEntry`.\n///\n/// Format: `label:/path/to/sock:port[,…]`\n/// Example: `qdrant:/run/qdrant.sock:6334`\npub fn socket_entries_from_env() -> Vec<SocketEntry> {\n    let Ok(raw) = env::var(\"UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS\") else {\n        return vec![];\n    };\n    raw.split(',')\n        .filter_map(|entry| {\n            // Split into exactly 3 parts: label, path, port\n            let mut parts = entry.trim().splitn(3, ':');\n            let label = parts.next()?.to_string();\n            let path = parts.next()?.to_string(); // already has leading '/'\n            let port: u16 = parts.next()?.trim().parse().ok()?;\n            Some(SocketEntry { label, path, port })\n        })\n        .collect()\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-02T18:12:33.196Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Two issues showed up in testing. First, the old `.1` iptables DNAT for `50051` is still stealing packets before Xray can terminate TLS. Second, Xray `dokodemo-door` is not the right reverse-TLS mode here; it produced a TLS handshake, then leaked the backend plaintext response. I’m switching the `443` and `50051` listeners to Xray VLESS+TLS fallback mode, which is the Xray path meant to terminate TLS and pass plain HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1 to the local backend.","phase":"commentary","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-02T18:12:33.196Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"Two issues showed up in testing. Use their underlying skills, MCP tools, and app tools to help solve the task.\n- Preference: When a relevant plugin is available, prefer using capabilities associated with that plugin over standalone capabilities that provide similar functionality.\n- Missing/blocked: If the user requests a plugin that is not listed above, or the plugin does not have relevant callable capabilities for the task, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.\n</plugins_instructions>"}]},{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking Zeroclaw / Antigravity proxy handlers\n//!\n//! Proxies chat requests to the antigravity Python SDK bot running on\n//! 127.0.0.1:8081, and serves the combined schema (OpenAPI + zeroclaw\n//! projection) for schema-driven UI rendering.\n\nuse axum::{\n    body::Body,\n    extract::Extension,\n    http::StatusCode,\n    response::Response,\n    Json,\n};\nuse serde::Deserialize;\nuse simd_json::prelude::*;\nuse simd_json::{json, OwnedValue as Value};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tracing::{error, info};\n\nuse crate::state::AppState;\n\n/// Antigravity bridge base URL - defaults to standard Antigravity IDE bridge port\n/// Can be overridden with ANTIGRAVITY_BRIDGE_URL env var\nfn antigravity_base() -> String {\n    std::env::var(\"ANTIGRAVITY_BRIDGE_URL\")\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"http://127.0.0.1:3333\".to_string())\n}\n\n/// Get WireGuard identity for auth headers\nfn wireguard_identity_headers() -> Vec<(&'static str, String)> {\n    let mut headers = Vec::new();\n    \n    // X-WireGuard-Pubkey from environment (set by wg-xray container or host)\n    if let Ok(pubkey) = std::env::var(\"WG_PUBKEY\") {\n        headers.push((\"X-WireGuard-Pubkey\", pubkey));\n    }\n    \n    // X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID for accountability loop\n    if let Ok(trace_id) = std::env::var(\"GHOSTBRIDGE_TRACE_ID\") {\n        headers.push((\"X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID\", trace_id));\n    }\n    \n    // Container-scoped identity for wg-xray\n    if let Ok(container_id) = std::env::var(\"CONTAINER_ID\") {\n        headers.push((\"X-Container-ID\", container_id));\n    }\n    \n    headers\n}\n\n/// Schema-driven chat request — shape matches the antigravity bot's\n/// `ChatRequest` so we can forward verbatim.\n#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]\npub struct ZeroclawChatRequest {\n    pub message: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub session_id: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub provider: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub model: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Proxy chat request to the antigravity bot.\n/// POST /api/zeroclaw/chat\npub async fn zeroclaw_chat_handler(\n    Extension(_state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,\n    Json(req): Json<ZeroclawChatRequest>,\n) -> Response {\n    let client = match reqwest::Client::builder()\n        .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(120))\n        .build()\n    {\n        Ok(c) => c,\n        Err(e) => {\n            error!(\"Failed to build HTTP client: {}\", e);\n            return json_error_response(\n                StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,\n                \"Failed to build HTTP client\",\n            );\n        }\n    };\n\n    let url = format!(\"{}/api/chat\", antigravity_base());\n\n    let body = json!({\n        \"message\": req.message,\n        \"session_id\": req.session_id,\n        \"provider\": req.provider,\n        \"model\": req.model,\n    });\n\n    info!(\n        \"Proxying zeroclaw chat to antigravity bot: {} chars\",\n        req.message.len()\n    );\n\n    let mut request_builder = client\n        .post(&url)\n        .header(\"Content-Type\", \"application/json\");\n    \n    // Add WireGuard identity headers for auth\n    for (key, value) in wireguard_identity_headers() {\n        request_builder = request_builder.header(key, value);\n    }\n\n    match request_builder\n        .body(simd_json::to_string(&body).unwrap_or_default())\n        .send()\n        .await\n    {\n        Ok(resp) => {\n            let status = resp.status();\n            let body_bytes = match resp.bytes().await {\n                Ok(b) => b,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    error!(\"Failed to read antigravity response body: {}\", e);\n                    return json_error_response(\n                        StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,\n                        \"Failed to read antigravity response\",\n                    );\n                }\n            };\n\n            let axum_status = StatusCode::from_u16(status.as_u16())\n                .unwrap_or(StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY);\n            Response::builder()\n                .status(axum_status)\n                .header(\"Content-Type\", \"application/json\")\n                .body(Body::from(body_bytes))\n                .unwrap_or_else(|_| json_error_response(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, \"Failed to build response\"))\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            error!(\"Antigravity bot unreachable: {}\", e);\n            json_error_response(\n                StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,\n                &format!(\"Antigravity bot unreachable: {}\", e),\n            )\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Proxy streaming chat request to the antigravity bot SSE endpoint.\n/// POST /api/zeroclaw/chat/stream\npub async fn zeroclaw_chat_stream_handler(\n    Extension(_state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,\n    Json(req): Json<ZeroclawChatRequest>,\n) -> Response {\n    let client = match reqwest::Client::builder()\n        .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(300))\n        .build()\n    {\n        Ok(c) => c,\n        Err(e) => {\n            error!(\"Failed to build HTTP client: {}\", e);\n            return json_error_response(\n                StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,\n                \"Failed to build HTTP client\",\n            );\n        }\n    };\n\n    let url = format!(\"{}/api/chat/stream\", antigravity_base());\n\n    let body = json!({\n        \"message\": req.message,\n        \"session_id\": req.session_id,\n        \"provider\": req.provider,\n        \"model\": req.model,\n    });\n\n    info!(\n        \"Proxying zeroclaw chat stream to antigravity bot: {} chars\",\n        req.message.len()\n    );\n\n    let mut request_builder = client\n        .post(&url)\n        .header(\"Content-Type\", \"application/json\")\n        .header(\"Accept\", \"text/event-stream\");\n    \n    // Add WireGuard identity headers for auth\n    for (key, value) in wireguard_identity_headers() {\n        request_builder = request_builder.header(key, value);\n    }\n\n    match request_builder\n        .body(simd_json::to_string(&body).unwrap_or_default())\n        .send()\n        .await\n    {\n        Ok(resp) => {\n            let status = resp.status();\n            let body_bytes = match resp.bytes().await {\n                Ok(b) => b,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    error!(\"Failed to read antigravity stream body: {}\", e);\n                    return json_error_response(\n                        StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,\n                        \"Failed to read antigravity stream\",\n                    );\n                }\n            };\n\n            let axum_status = StatusCode::from_u16(status.as_u16())\n                .unwrap_or(StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY);\n            Response::builder()\n                .status(axum_status)\n                .header(\"Content-Type\", \"text/event-stream\")\n                .header(\"Cache-Control\", \"no-cache\")\n                .body(Body::from(body_bytes))\n                .unwrap_or_else(|_| json_error_response(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, \"Failed to build stream response\"))\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            error!(\"Antigravity bot unreachable: {}\", e);\n            json_error_response(\n                StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,\n                &format!(\"Antigravity bot unreachable: {}\", e),\n            )\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Helper to build a JSON error response.\nfn json_error_response(status: StatusCode, message: &str) -> Response {\n    let body = simd_json::to_string(&json!({\"error\": message})).unwrap_or_default();\n    Response::builder()\n        .status(status)\n        .header(\"Content-Type\", \"application/json\")\n        .body(Body::from(body))\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| {\n            Response::builder()\n                .status(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR)\n                .body(Body::empty())\n                .unwrap()\n        })\n}\n\n/// Read zeroclaw schema directly from shared memory (Absolute Base)\n/// Per AGENTS.md: \"The Absolute Base: PluginSchema is the single source of truth\"\nfn read_zeroclaw_from_shm() -> Option<Value> {\n    use std::fs;\n    \n    const SHM_SCHEMA_PATH: &str = \"/dev/shm/live-schema.json\";\n    \n    let content = fs::read_to_string(SHM_SCHEMA_PATH).ok()?;\n    let mut bytes = content.into_bytes();\n    let schema: Value = simd_json::to_owned_value(&mut bytes).ok()?;\n    \n    // Extract zeroclaw from the schema examples (the canonical source)\n    let zeroclaw_schema = schema.get(\"zeroclaw\")?.as_array()?.first()?;\n    let fields = zeroclaw_schema.get(\"fields\")?.as_array()?;\n    \n    // Helper: find field example by name\n    fn find_example(fields: &[Value], name: &str) -> Option<Value> {\n        for f in fields {\n            let field_name = f.get(\"name\")?.as_str()?;\n            if field_name == name {\n                return f.get(\"example\").cloned();\n            }\n"}}

OpenClaw selects the target agent and that agent's configured model stack.\",\n                \"routing\": \"agent\",\n                \"available\": true\n            }\n        ],\n        \"source\": \"configured-default\",\n        \"note\": \"OpenClaw's OpenAI-compatible endpoint routes requests by agent id (for example model=openclaw:<agentId> or x-openclaw-agent-id). /v1/models may not be implemented on the gateway.\"\n    })\n}\n\nfn openclaw_host_label(base_url: &str) -> String {\n    base_url\n        .strip_prefix(\"http://\")\n        .or_else(|| base_url.strip_prefix(\"https://\"))\n        .unwrap_or(base_url)\n        .split(':')\n        .next()\n        .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_OPENCLAW_HOST)\n        .to_string()\n}\n\n#[derive(Serialize)]\npub struct OpenClawStatusResponse {\n    pub available: bool,\n    pub endpoint: String,\n    pub model: String,\n    pub container_ip: String,\n    pub internal_only: bool,\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub error: Option<String>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Serialize)]\npub struct OpenClawConfigResponse {\n    pub endpoint: String,\n    pub model: String,\n    pub internal_only: bool,\n    pub container_ip: String,\n    pub container_port: u16,\n}\n\n/// GET /api/openclaw/status - Check OpenClaw gateway health\npub async fn openclaw_status_handler(\n    Extension(_state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,\n) -> Json<OpenClawStatusResponse> {\n    let base_url = openclaw_base_url();\n    let default_model = openclaw_default_model();\n\n    let container_ip = openclaw_host_label(&base_url);\n\n    // Try to ping OpenClaw\n    let client = Client::builder()\n        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(5))\n        .build()\n        .unwrap();\n\n    let ping_url = format!(\"{}/v1/chat/completions\", base_url);\n    let mut response = OpenClawStatusResponse {\n        available: false,\n        endpoint: base_url.clone(),\n        model: default_model,\n        container_ip,\n        internal_only: true,\n        error: None,\n    };\n\n    match client.get(&ping_url).send().await {\n        Ok(resp) => {\n            let status = resp.status();\n            if status.is_success()\n                || status == reqwest::StatusCode::METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED\n                || status == reqwest::StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST\n            {\n                debug!(\"OpenClaw gateway is available at {}\", base_url);\n                response.available = true;\n            } else {\n                response.error = Some(format!(\"HTTP {}\", status));\n                debug!(\"OpenClaw returned status {}\", status);\n            }\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            error!(\"Failed to reach OpenClaw: {}\", e);\n            response.error = Some(e.to_string());\n        }\n    }\n\n    Json(response)\n}\n\n/// GET /api/openclaw/config - Get OpenClaw configuration\npub async fn Identity Sled Handler — Read the live identity sled from shared memory.\n//!\n//! GET /api/identity/sled — returns the current sled contents as JSON.\n//! Readable by any WireGuard-connected device without root access.\n\nuse axum::{\n    body::Body,\n    extract::Extension,\n    http::{header, StatusCode},\n    response::Response,\n};\nuse op_identity::schema_bridge::{read_sled, IdentitySled};\nuse serde_json::json;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tracing::{info, warn};\n\nuse crate::state::AppState;\n\n/// GET /api/identity/sled\npub async fn identity_sled_handler(Extension(_state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>) -> Response {\n    match read_sled() {\n        Ok((ptr, _mmap)) => {\n            let sled: &IdentitySled = unsafe { &*ptr };\n\n            let schema_catalog_hash = std::fs::read(\"/dev/shm/live-schema.json\")\n                .map(|bytes| hex::encode(blake3::hash(&bytes).as_bytes()))\n                .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"(missing)\".to_string());\n\n            let is_valid = sled.hashed_footprint != [0u8; 32] && sled.trace_id != [0u8; 16];\n\n            let body = json!({\n                \"path\": op_identity::schema_bridge::SHM_SLED_PATH,\n                \"is_valid\": is_valid,\n                \"wireguard_pubkey\": encode_b64(&sled.wireguard_pubkey),\n                \"wireguard_pubkey_hex\": hex::encode(sled.wireguard_pubkey),\n                \"mutation_index\": sled.mutation_index,\n                \"hashed_footprint\": hex::encode(sled.hashed_footprint),\n                \"trace_id\": sled.trace_id_hex(),\n                \"schema_version\": sled.schema_version,\n                \"schema_catalog_hash\": schema_catalog_hash,\n            });\n\n            info!(\"Served identity sled from shared memory\");\n            Response::builder()\n                .status(StatusCode::OK)\n                .header(header::CONTENT_TYPE, \"application/json\")\n                .body(Body::from(serde_json::to_vec(&body).unwrap()))\n                .unwrap()\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            warn!(error = %e, \"Identity sled not available\");\n            Response::builder()\n                .status(StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE)\n                .header(header::CONTENT_TYPE, \"application/json\")\n                .body(Body::from(format!(\n                    r#\"{{\"error\":\"Identity sled not available\",\"detail\":\"{}\"}}\"#,\n                    e\n                )))\n                .unwrap()\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn encode_b64(bytes: &[u8; 32]) -> String {\n    use base64::Engine;\n    base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(bytes)\n}\n"}}

Known mode names are Default and Plan.\n\n## request_user_input availability\n\nUse the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.\n\nIn Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n</collaboration_mode>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<apps_instructions>\n## Apps (Connectors)\nApps (Connectors) can be explicitly triggered in user messages in the format `[$app-name](app://{connector_id})`. Apps can also be implicitly triggered as long as the context suggests usage of available apps.\nAn app is equivalent to a set of MCP tools within the `codex_apps` MCP.\nAn installed app's MCP tools are either provided to you already, or can be lazy-loaded through the `tool_search` tool. If `tool_search` is available, the apps that are searchable by `tools_search` will be listed by it.\nDo not additionally call list_mcp_resources or list_mcp_resource_templates for apps.\n</apps_instructions>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<skills_instructions>\n## Skills\nA skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking
