Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-08</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

No authentication layer, TLS client certificates (mTLS), token verification, or encryption has been configured on the Tonic transport server.\n./crates/audits/op-services/11_11_Configuration_Feature_Flags.md:107:  * Integrate an authentication/authorization middleware (e.g. validating local system tokens, JWTs, or polkit credentials) before processing operations inside `GrpcServer`.\n./crates/audits/op-services/11_11_Configuration_Feature_Flags.md:118:  The string representation of `ServiceName` is re-exported from `op-plugins`. If this type fails to sanitize path inputs to reject folder traversal tokens (such as `../`), an authenticated D-Bus or gRPC caller can trigger arbitrary file deletion (e.g., requesting the deletion of service `../../etc/shadow` or `../../boot/vmlinuz`).\n./crates/audits/op-execution-tracker/16_16_Improvement_Suggestions.md:38:2. **Suggestion**: Unify duplicate `ExecutionStatus` enums | **Rationale**: The crate defines two separate enums representing execution state: `execution_context::ExecutionStatus` and `record::ExecutionStatus`. They have different variants and serialization setups, requiring redundant mapping logic and creating high cognitive overhead for downstream modules trying to track execution states. | **Example**: `crates/op-execution-tracker/src/record.rs:22`\n./crates/audits/op-workflows/17_17_DBus_IPC_Attack_Surface.md:11:* **Direct Tool Execution:** `Orchestrator::execute_tool` (`crates/op-workflows/src/orchestrator.rs:341`) runs tools directly from `tool_registry` using raw, unchecked JSON inputs without authorization verification.\n./crates/audits/op-workflows/17_17_DBus_IPC_Attack_Surface.md:14:* **State Mutation via Nodes:** `WorkflowEngine::execute_definition` (`crates/op-workflows/src/engine.rs:114`) schedules and executes arbitrary workflow nodes. If exposed via an outer IPC daemon, any unauthenticated caller can execute nodes like `DbusMethodNode` (`crates/op-workflows/src/builtin/dbus_node.rs:55`) or `PluginNode` (`crates/op-workflows/src/builtin/plugin_node.rs:109`), which mutate configuration or invoke privileged system D-Bus interfaces.\n./crates/audits/op-workflows/17_17_DBus_IPC_Attack_Surface.md:15:* **Process Execution via Tools:** `ToolNode::execute` (`crates/op-workflows/src/builtin/tool_node.rs:52`) executes system tools (e.g., cargo format, cargo test, or deploy tasks) based on workflow instructions. There is no gating mechanism to prevent an unauthenticated user from specifying arbitrary target fields.\n./crates/audits/op-workflows/17_17_DBus_IPC_Attack_Surface.md:66:  Since the engine recursively interpolates object/array variables (`interpolate_value` in `crates/op-workflows/src/context.rs:133`) and processes strings sequentially, an attacker who controls the value of a runtime variable can inject pattern sequences (e.g., `${target_variable}`) into their input. This triggers nested, unauthorized variable expansions or parameters spoofing. Cognitive MCP Server Binary\n//!\n//! Transports started in parallel:\n//! - HTTP/SSE  (MCP protocol, port 3003)\n//! - gRPC      (CognitiveToolService, port 50052)\n//! - D-Bus     (org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp / /org/opdbus/v1/cognitive)\n//!\n//! On startup the server reads the local WireGuard public key (from the\n//! interface named by $WG_INTERFACE, defaulting to \"netmaker\") and writes the\n//! canonical IdentitySled to /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat so the Ghostbridge\n//! interceptor and Qdrant shuttle can authenticate outbound gRPC calls.\n//!\n//! Bind address resolution order (highest priority first):\n//!   1. COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND / COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND env vars\n//!   2. --http / --grpc CLI flags\n//!   3. WireGuard interface IP detected at startup (if interface is up)\n//!   4. 0.0.0.0 fallback\n\nuse clap::Parser;\nuse op_cognitive_mcp::CognitiveMcpServer;\nuse op_identity::{write_sled_from_wg, WireGuardIdentity};\nuse tracing::{info, warn, Level};\nuse tracing_subscriber::FmtSubscriber;\n\n#[derive(Parser)]\n#[command(name = \"cognitive-mcp-server\")]\n#[command(about = \"Cognitive MCP Server with memory, NotebookLM bridge, gRPC, and D-Bus\")]\nstruct Cli {\n    /// HTTP/SSE server address (MCP protocol).\n    /// If left at 0.0.0.0 the WireGuard interface IP is used when available.\n    /// Override with COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND env var or this flag.\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND\", default_value = \"0.0.0.0:3003\")]\n    http: String,\n\n    /// gRPC server address (CognitiveToolService).\n    /// If left at 0.0.0.0 the WireGuard interface IP is used when available.\n    /// Override with COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND env var or this flag.\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND\", default_value = \"0.0.0.0:50052\")]\n    grpc: String,\n\n    /// CozoDB database path\n    #[arg(\n        long,\n        env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_DB_PATH\",\n        default_value = \"/var/lib/op-cognitive-mcp/memory.db\"\n    )]\n    db: String,\n\n    /// WireGuard interface to read identity from\n    #[arg(long, env = \"WG_INTERFACE\", default_value = \"netmaker\")]\n    wg_interface: String,\n\n    /// Log level\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_LOG_LEVEL\", default_value = \"info\")]\n    log_level: String,\n\n    /// Disable gRPC server\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_DISABLED\")]\n    no_grpc: bool,\n\n    /// Disable HTTP/SSE server\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_HTTP_DISABLED\")]\n    no_http: bool,\n\n    /// Disable D-Bus registration\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_DBUS_DISABLED\")]\n    no_dbus: bool,\n}\n\n/// Promote an `0.0.0.0:PORT` default address to `<wg_ip>:PORT` when the WG\n/// interface is up.  Explicit addresses (not starting with `0.0.0.0:`) are\n/// returned unchanged so env-var or flag overrides always win.\nfn resolve_bind(addr: &str, wg_ip: Option<&str>) -> String {\n    if let Some(rest) = addr.strip_prefix(\"0.0.0.0:\") {\n        if let Some(ip) = wg_ip {\n            return format!(\"{ip}:{rest}\");\n        }\n    }\n    addr.to_string()\n}\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let cli = Cli::parse();\n\n    let level = match cli.log_level.as_str() {\n        \"trace\" => Level::TRACE,\n        \"debug\" => Level::DEBUG,\n        \"warn\" => Level::WARN,\n        \"error\" => Level::ERROR,\n        _ => Level::INFO,\n    };\n\n    let subscriber = FmtSubscriber::builder()\n        .with_max_level(level)\n        .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n        .finish();\n    tracing::subscriber::set_global_default(subscriber)?;\n\n    // ── WireGuard identity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    // 1. Detect local WG IP for bind address resolution.\n    // 2. Write canonical IdentitySled to /dev/shm for Ghostbridge auth.\n    let wg_id = WireGuardIdentity::with_interface(&cli.wg_interface);\n    let wg_ip = wg_id.get_local_ip();\n\n    match wg_id.get_local_pubkey() {\n        Ok(pubkey) => {\n            info!(\n                interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n                pubkey = %pubkey,\n                wg_ip = ?wg_ip,\n                \"Writing WireGuard identity sled to /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat\"\n            );\n            if let Err(e) = write_sled_from_wg(&pubkey) {\n                warn!(\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"Failed to write identity sled — gRPC Ghostbridge auth will not work\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            warn!(\n                interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n                error = %e,\n                \"Could not read WireGuard public key — identity sled not written; \\\n                 set WG_PUBKEY env var to override\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Resolve bind addresses: promote 0.0.0.0 defaults to WG interface IP.\n    let http_addr = resolve_bind(&cli.http, wg_ip.as_deref());\n    let grpc_addr = resolve_bind(&cli.grpc, wg_ip.as_deref());\n\n    info!(\n        http = %http_addr,\n        grpc = %grpc_addr,\n        db = %cli.db,\n        wg_interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n        \"Starting Cognitive MCP Server\"\n    );\n\n    let server = CognitiveMcpServer::new(&cli.db).await?;\n\n    // D-Bus: start first, keep connection alive for the process lifetime.\n    let _dbus_conn = if !cli.no_dbus {\n        match server.start_dbus().await {\n            Ok(conn) => {\n                info!(\"D-Bus registered: org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp\");\n                Some(conn)\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                warn!(\"D-Bus registration failed (continuing without it): {e}\");\n                None\n            }\n        }\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n\n    match (cli.no_grpc, cli.no_http) {\n        (true, true) => {\n            eprintln!(\"Error: both --no-grpc and --no-http specified. Nothing to run.\");\n            std::process::exit(1);\n        }\n        (true, false) => {\n            info!(\"Running HTTP/SSE only\");\n            server.start_http_server(&http_addr).await?;\n        }\n        (false, true) => {\n            info!(\"Running gRPC only\");\n            server.start_grpc_server(&grpc_addr).await?;\n        }\n        (false, false) => {\n            info!(\"Running HTTP/SSE + gRPC\");\n            server.start_dual(&http_addr, &grpc_addr).await?;\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n"}}

listening\");\n\n            tonic::transport::Server::builder()\n                .accept_http1(true)\n                .add_service(tonic_web::enable(\n                    CognitiveToolServiceServer::with_interceptor(\n                        grpc_service,\n                        crate::interceptor::ghostbridge_interceptor,\n                    ),\n                ))\n                .add_service(tonic_web::enable(reflection))\n                .add_service(tonic_web::enable(health_service))\n                .serve(socket_addr)\n                .await\n                .expect(\"gRPC server failed\");\n        });\n\n        self.start_http_server(&http_addr).await?;\n        grpc_handle.await?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn memory_store(&self) -> crate::dbus_interface::CognitiveMcpInterface;\n\n        let conn = zbus::Connection::system().await?;\n        conn.request_name(\"org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp\").await?;\n\n        let iface = CognitiveMcpInterface::new(self.tool_registry.clone());\n        conn.object_server()\n            .at(\"/org/opdbus/v1/cognitive\", iface)\n            .await?;\n\n        tracing::info!(\"Cognitive MCP D-Bus interface registered at /org/opdbus/v1/cognitive\");\n        Ok(conn)\n    }\n\n    pub fn qdrant_shuttle(&self) -> Option<Arc<QdrantSemanticShuttle>> {\n {"timestamp":"2026-06-08T09:07:19.415Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_bJvkmYHpRO7g67e3BX9fNTGw","output":"Chunk ID: 846b54\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 818\nOutput:\n# op-dbus MCP Server Configuration Examples\n\nThis directory contains example MCP server configurations for various AI clients.\n\n## MCP Endpoints\n\nThe op-dbus MCP server exposes three main modes at `https://op-dbus.ghostbridge.tech`:\n\n| Mode | SSE Endpoint | POST Endpoint | Description |\n|------|--------------|---------------|-------------|\n| **Compact** | `/mcp/compact` | `/mcp/compact/message` | 5 lazy meta-tools for efficient tool discovery |\n| **Standard** | `/mcp/sse` | `/mcp/message` | All tools exposed directly |\n| **Agents** | `/mcp/agents` | `/mcp/agents/message` | Specialized AI agents |\n\n### Compact Mode (Recommended for AI Clients)\nExposes 5 lazy meta-tools instead of the full tool list:\n- `list_tools` - Browse tools with pagination\n- `search_tools` - Search tools by keyword\n- `get_tool_schema` - Get schema for a specific tool\n- `execute_tool` - Execute any underlying tool\n- `respond` - Return the final response\n\n### Standard Mode\nExposes all tools directly via `tools/list`. Best for clients that can handle large tool lists.\n\n### Agents Mode\nSpecialized AI agents for enhanced capabilities:\n- `memory` - Key-value memory (remember, recall, forget)\n- `context_manager` - Context persistence (save, load, list, delete)\n- `sequential_thinking` - Step-by-step reasoning\n- `mem0` - Semantic memory (add, search, get_all, delete, update)\n- `search_specialist` - Code/docs/web search\n- `deployment` - Service deployment (deploy, rollback, status)\n- `python_pro` - Python analysis and refactoring\n- `debugger` - Error analysis and tracing\n- `prompt_engineer` - Prompt generation and optimization\n\n## Configuration Files\n\n| File | Client | Notes |\n|------|--------|-------|\n| `cursor-mcp.json` | Cursor IDE | Uses `url` key |\n| `codex-mcp.json` | Codex Client | Uses `mcpServers` with SSE transport |\n| `vscode-mcp.json` | VS Code (Copilot Chat) | Uses `mcp.servers` structure |\n| `claude-desktop-mcp.json` | Claude Desktop | Prefers stdio transport |\n| `openai-mcp.json` | OpenAI tools | Array-based servers list |\n| `generic-mcp.json` | Reference | Complete with all endpoints |\n\n## Installation\n\n### System-wide (Recommended)\n```bash\nsudo mkdir -p /etc/mcp\nsudo cp *.json /etc/mcp/\n```\n\n### Cursor\n```bash\n# Project-level\nmkdir -p .cursor\ncp cursor-mcp.json .cursor/mcp.json\n\n# User-level\ncp cursor-mcp.json ~/.cursor/mcp.json\n```\n\n### VS Code\nAdd the contents of `vscode-mcp.json` to your VS Code `settings.json`:\n```json\n{\n  \"mcp\": {\n    \"servers\": { ... }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Claude Desktop\nClaude Desktop prefers stdio-based MCP servers. Options:\n1. Use the native `op-mcp-server` binary (recommended)\n2. Use mcp-proxy to bridge SSE to stdio\n\n## Testing Connection\n\n```bash\n# Test health endpoint\ncurl https://op-dbus.ghostbridge.tech/api/health\n\n# Test MCP initialize\ncurl -X POST https://op-dbus.ghostbridge.tech/mcp/message \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -d '{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":1,\"method\":\"initialize\",\"params\":{}}'\n\n# Test tools/list\ncurl -X POST https://op-dbus.ghostbridge.tech/mcp/message \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -d '{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":2,\"method\":\"tools/list\",\"params\":{}}'\n```\n\n## See Also\n\n- [MCP Protocol Specification](https://spec.modelcontextprotocol.io/)\n- [op-dbus Documentation](../../../docs/)\n"}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-08T09:07:19.447Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_07LgQgDs8CD3yOWxhU4EXAo8","output":"Chunk ID: 71a2fd\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1863\nOutput:\n//! MCP Protocol Handler (Clean Implementation)\n//!\n//! Implements the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server endpoints.\n//! - Standard Mode: Exposes all tools via `tools/list`\n//! - Compact Mode: Exposes meta-tools via `mcp_compact` module\n//! - SSE Support: For server-initiated events\n\nuse axum::{\n    extract::{Extension, Json},\n    response::sse::{Event, Sse},\n    routing::{get, post},\n    Router,\n};\nuse futures::stream::{self, Stream};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse simd_json::prelude::*;\nuse simd_json::{json, OwnedValue as Value};\nuse std::convert::Infallible;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tokio::sync::broadcast;\nuse tokio_stream::wrappers::BroadcastStream;\nuse tokio_stream::StreamExt;\nuse tracing::{debug, error, info};\n\nuse crate::state::AppState;\n\n/// SSE broadcaster for MCP responses\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct SseBroadcaster {\n    tx: broadcast::Sender<String>,\n}\n\nimpl Default for SseBroadcaster {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl SseBroadcaster {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        let (tx, _) = broadcast::channel(100);\n        Self { tx }\n    }\n\n    pub fn broadcast(&self, data: &str) {\n        let _ = self.tx.send(data.to_string());\n    }\n\n    pub fn subscribe(&self) -> broadcast::Receiver<String> {\n        self.tx.subscribe()\n    }\n}\n\n// Global SSE broadcaster\nlazy_static::lazy_static! {\n    static ref GLOBAL_BROADCASTER: SseBroadcaster = SseBroadcaster::new();\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]\npub struct McpRequest {\n    pub jsonrpc: String,\n    pub id: Option<Value>,\n    pub method: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub params: Option<Value>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]\npub struct McpResponse {\n    pub jsonrpc: String,\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub id: Option<Value>,\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub result: Option<Value>,\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub error: Option<McpError>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]\npub struct McpError {\n    pub code: i32,\n    pub message: String,\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub data: Option<Value>,\n}\n\nimpl McpResponse {\n    fn success(id: Option<Value>, result: Value) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            jsonrpc: \"2.0\".to_string(),\n            id,\n            result: Some(result),\n            error: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn error(id: Option<Value>, code: i32, message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            jsonrpc: \"2.0\".to_string(),\n            id,\n            result: None,\n            error: Some(McpError {\n                code,\n                message: message.into(),\n                data: None,\n            }),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Create MCP router\npub fn create_mcp_router() -> Router {\n    Router::new()\n        // Compact mode (Preferred)\n        .route(\n            \"/compact\",\n            get(crate::mcp_compact::mcp_compact_sse_handler)\n                .post(crate::mcp_compact::mcp_compact_message_handler),\n        )\n        .route(\n            \"/compact/message\",\n            post(crate::mcp_compact::mcp_compact_message_handler),\n        )\n        // Standard endpoints (all tools)\n        .route(\"/\", post(mcp_handler))\n        .route(\"/sse\", get(mcp_sse_handler))\n        .route(\"/message\", post(mcp_message_handler))\n        // Configuration\n        .route(\"/_config\", get(config_handler))\n}\n\n/// Standard Handler (all tools)\nasync fn mcp_handler(\n    Extension(state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,\n    Json(request): Json<McpRequest>,\n) -> Json<McpResponse> {\n    let response = process_request(&state, request).await;\n    Json(response)\n}\n\n/// JSON-RPC compatibility handler (1:1 mirror of MCP)\npub async fn jsonrpc_handler(\n    Extension(state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,\n    Json(request): Json<McpRequest>,\n) -> Json<McpResponse> {\n    let response = process_request(&state, request).await;\n    Json(response)\n}\n\n/// SSE endpoint for MCP connections\nasync fn mcp_sse_handler(\n    headers: axum::http::HeaderMap,\n) -> Sse<impl Stream<Item = Result<Event, Infallible>>> {\n    let rx = GLOBAL_BROADCASTER.subscribe();\n\n    info!(\"SSE client connected\");\n\n    let host = headers\n        .get(\"host\")\n        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())\n        .unwrap_or(\"localhost\");\n\n    let scheme = headers\n        .get(\"x-forwarded-proto\")\n        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())\n        .unwrap_or(\"http\");\n\n    let post_url = format!(\"{}://{}/mcp/message\", scheme, host);\n\n    // Initial endpoint event\n    let endpoint_event = Event::default().event(\"endpoint\").data(&post_url);\n\n    let stream = BroadcastStream::new(rx).filter_map(|result| {\n        match result {\n            Ok(data) => Some(Ok(Event::default().data(data))),\n            Err(_) => None, // Skip lagged messages\n        }\n    });\n\n    // Combine initial event with broadcast stream\n    let combined_stream = stream::once(async move { Ok(endpoint_event) }).chain(stream);\n\n    Sse::new(combined_stream).keep_alive(\n        axum::response::sse::KeepAlive::new()\n            .interval(std::time::Duration::from_secs(15))\n            .text(\"ping\"),\n    )\n}\n\n/// Message handler for MCP requests (with SSE broadcasting)\nasync fn mcp_message_handler(\n    Extension(state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,\n    Json(request): Json<McpRequest>,\n) -> Json<McpResponse> {\n    info!(\"MCP message received (method: {})\", request.method);\n\n    let response = process_request(&state, request).await;\n\n    // Broadcast to SSE clients\n    if let Ok(json) = simd_json::to_string(&response) {\n        GLOBAL_BROADCASTER.broadcast(&json);\n    }\n\n    Json(response)\n}\n\n/// Process a single MCP request\nasync fn process_request(state: &AppState, request: McpRequest) -> McpResponse {\n    debug!(\"MCP request: {} (id: {:?})\", request.method, request.id);\n\n    // Validate JSON-RPC version\n    if request.jsonrpc != \"2.0\" {\n        return McpResponse::error(request.id, -32600, \"Invalid JSON-RPC version\");\n    }\n\n    match request.method.as_str() {\n        \"initialize\" => handle_initialize(request.id).await,\n        \"initialized\" => handle_initialized(request.id).await,\n        \"tools/list\" => handle_tools_list(state, request.id, request.params).await,\n        \"tools/call\" => handle_tools_call(state, request.id, request.params).await,\n        \"resources/list\" => handle_resources_list(request.id).await,\n        \"resources/read\" => handle_resources_read(request.id, request.params).await,\n        \"prompts/list\" => handle_prompts_list(request.id).await,\n        \"ping\" => handle_ping(request.id).await,\n        _ => McpResponse::error(\n            request.id,\n            -32601,\n            format!(\"Method not found: {}\", request.method),\n        ),\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn handle_initialize(id: Option<Value>) -> McpResponse {\n    McpResponse::success(\n        id,\n        json!({\n            \"protocolVersion\": \"2024-11-05\",\n            \"capabilities\": {\n                \"tools\": {\n                    \"listChanged\": true\n                },\n                \"resources\": {\n                    \"subscribe\": false,\n                    \"listChanged\": false\n                },\n                \"prompts\": {\n                    \"listChanged\": false\n                }\n            },\n            \"serverInfo\": {\n                \"name\": \"op-dbus-mcp\",\n                \"version\": env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\"),\n            }\n        }),\n    )\n}\n\nasync fn handle_initialized(id: Option<Value>) -> McpResponse {\n    McpResponse::success(id, json!({}))\n}\n"}}

MCP Server Management Handlers\n\nuse axum::{\n    extract::{Extension, Path},\n    response::Json,\n};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse simd_json::{json, OwnedValue as Value};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse crate::mcp_agents;\nuse crate::state::AppState;\n\n#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct McpServer {\n    pub id: String,\n    pub name: String,\n    pub server_type: String, // \"compact\" or \"cognitive\"\n    pub status: String,      // \"running\", \"stopped\", \"error\"\n    pub url: String,\n    pub tools_count: usize,\n    pub agents: Option<Vec<String>>, // Only for cognitive server\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Agent {\n    pub id: String,\n    pub name: String,\n    pub description: String,\n    pub enabled: bool,\n    pub active: bool,\n    pub running: bool,\n    pub capabilities: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]\npub struct SetAgentsRequest {\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub agent_ids: Vec<String>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub enabled_agent_ids: Option<Vec<String>>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub active_agent_ids: Option<Vec<String>>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct MemoryQuery {\n    pub key_pattern: Option<String>,\n    pub memory_type: Option<String>,\n    pub tags: Option<Vec<String>>,\n    pub limit: Option<usize>,\n}\n\n/// GET /api/mcp/servers - List all MCP servers\npub async fn list_servers_handler(\n    Extension(_state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,\n) -> Json<Vec<McpServer>> {\n    let cognitive = mcp_agents::cognitive_runtime_snapshot().await;\n    let servers = vec![\n        McpServer {\n            id: \"compact\".to_string(),\n            name: \"Compact MCP Server\".to_string(),\n            server_type: \"compact\".to_string(),\n            status: \"running\".to_string(),\n            url: \"http://localhost:3001\".to_string(),\n            tools_count: 15,\n            agents: None,\n        },\n        McpServer {\n            id: \"cognitive\".to_string(),\n            name: \"Cognitive MCP Server\".to_string(),\n            server_type: \"cognitive\".to_string(),\n            status: \"running\".to_string(),\n            url: \"http://localhost:3002\".to_string(),\n            tools_count: cognitive.tools_count,\n            agents: Some(cognitive.active_agents),\n        },\n    ];\n\n    Json(servers)\n}\n\n/// GET /api/mcp/servers/:id - Get server details\npub async fn get_server_handler(\n    Extension(_state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,\n    Path(server_id): Path<String>,\n) -> Json<Value> {\n    let cognitive = mcp_agents::cognitive_runtime_snapshot().await;\n\n    if server_id == \"cognitive\" {\n        return Json(json!({\n            \"id\": \"cognitive\",\n            \"name\": \"Cognitive MCP Server\",\n            \"status\": \"running\",\n            \"tools_count\": cognitive.tools_count,\n            \"total_agents\": cognitive.total_agents,\n            \"enabled_agents\": cognitive.enabled_agents,\n            \"active_agents\": cognitive.active_agents,\n            \"running_agents\": cognitive.running_agents\n        }));\n    }\n\n    Json(json!({\n        \"id\": server_id,\n        \"name\": format!(\"{} MCP Server\", server_id),\n        \"status\": \"running\",\n        \"tools_count\": 15\n    }))\n}\n\n/// GET /api/mcp/cognitive/agents - List available agents for cognitive server\npub async fn list_agents_handler(Extension(_state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>) -> Json<Vec<Agent>> {\n    let agents = mcp_agents::list_cognitive_agents()\n        .await\n        .into_iter()\n        .map(|agent| Agent {\n            id: agent.id,\n            name: agent.name,\n            description: agent.description,\n            enabled: agent.enabled,\n            active: agent.active,\n            running: agent.running,\n            capabilities: agent.capabilities,\n        })\n        .collect();\n\n    Json(agents)\n}\n\n/// POST /api/mcp/cognitive/agents - Set enabled agents for cognitive server\npub async fn set_agents_handler(\n    Extension(_state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,\n    Json(request): Json<SetAgentsRequest>,\n) -> Json<Value> {\n    let enabled = if let Some(explicit) = request.enabled_agent_ids {\n        Some(explicit)\n    } else if !request.agent_ids.is_empty() || request.active_agent_ids.is_none() {\n        Some(request.agent_ids)\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n\n    match mcp_agents::set_cognitive_agents(enabled, request.active_agent_ids).await {\n        Ok(snapshot) => Json(json!({\n            \"success\": true,\n            \"enabled_agents\": snapshot.enabled_agents,\n            \"active_agents\": snapshot.active_agents,\n            \"running_agents\": snapshot.running_agents,\n            \"tools_count\": snapshot.tools_count,\n            \"message\": \"Cognitive MCP agent configuration updated\"\n        })),\n        Err(err) => Json(json!({\n            \"success\": false,\n            \"error\": err\n        })),\n    }\n}\n\n/// GET /api/mcp/cognitive/memory - Query cognitive memory\npub async fn query_memory_handler(\n    Extension(_state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,\n    Json(query): Json<MemoryQuery>,\n) -> Json<Value> {\n    // TODO: Query actual memory store\n    Json(json!({\n        \"entries\": [\n            {\n                \"id\": \"mem_123\",\n                \"key\": \"user_preference\",\n                \"value\": {\"theme\": \"dark\", \"language\": \"en\"},\n                \"memory_type\": \"persistent\",\n                \"tags\": [\"user\", \"settings\"],\n                \"created_at\": \"2026-03-03T08:00:00Z\",\n                \"access_count\": 42\n            },\n            {\n                \"id\": \"mem_456\",\n                \"key\": \"session_context\",\n                \"value\": {\"last_topic\": \"MCP servers\", \"mood\": \"helpful\"},\n                \"memory_type\": \"ephemeral\",\n                \"tags\": [\"session\", \"context\"],\n                \"created_at\": \"2026-03-03T08:30:00Z\",\n                \"access_count\": 5\n            }\n        ],\n        \"total\": 2,\n        \"query\": query\n    }))\n}\n\n/// DELETE /api/mcp/cognitive/memory/:key - Delete memory entry\npub async fn delete_memory_handler(\n    Extension(_state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,\n    Path(key): Path<String>,\n) -> Json<Value> {\n    // TODO: Delete from actual memory store\n    Json(json!({\n        \"success\": true,\n        \"deleted_key\": key,\n        \"message\": \"Memory entry deleted\"\n    }))\n}\n\n/// GET /api/mcp/cognitive/memory/stats - Get memory statistics\npub async fn memory_stats_handler(Extension(_state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>) -> Json<Value> {\n    // TODO: Get actual stats\n    Json(json!({\n        \"total_entries\": 127,\n        \"ephemeral\": 45,\n        \"persistent\": 72,\n        \"shared\": 10,\n        \"total_memory_bytes\": 1024000,\n        \"max_entries\": 10000,\n        \"oldest_entry\": \"2026-02-01T00:00:00Z\",\n        \"most_accessed_key\": \"user_preference\"\n    }))\n}\n"}}

You and the user share one workspace, and your job is to collaborate with them until their goal is genuinely handled.\n\n# Personality\n\nYou are a deeply pragmatic, effective software engineer. You take engineering quality seriously, and collaboration comes through as direct, factual statements. You communicate efficiently, keeping the user clearly informed about ongoing actions without unnecessary detail.\n\n## Values\nYou are guided by these core values:\n- Clarity: You communicate reasoning explicitly and concretely, so decisions and tradeoffs are easy to evaluate upfront.\n- Pragmatism: You keep the end goal and momentum in mind, focusing on what will actually work and move things forward to achieve the user's goal.\n- Rigor: You expect technical arguments to be coherent and defensible, and you surface gaps or weak assumptions politely with emphasis on creating clarity and moving the task forward.\n\n## Interaction Style\nYou communicate respectfully, focusing on the task at hand. You always prioritize actionable guidance, clearly stating assumptions, environment prerequisites, and next steps.\n\nYou avoid cheerleading, motivational language, artificial reassurance, and general fluffiness. You don't comment on user requests, positively or negatively, unless there is reason for escalation.\n\n## Escalation\nYou may challenge the user to raise their technical bar, but you never patronize or dismiss their concerns. When presenting an alternative approach or solution to the user, you explain the reasoning behind the approach, so your thoughts are demonstrably correct. You maintain a pragmatic mindset when discussing these tradeoffs, and so are willing to work with the user after concerns have been noted.\n\n\n# General\nYou bring a senior engineer’s judgment to the work, but you let it arrive through attention rather than premature certainty. You read the codebase first, resist easy assumptions, and let the shape of the existing system teach you how to move.\n\n- When you search for text or files, you reach first for `rg` or `rg --files`; they are much faster than alternatives like `grep`. If `rg` is unavailable, you use the next best tool without fuss.\n- You parallelize tool calls whenever you can, especially file reads such as `cat`, `rg`, `sed`, `ls`, `git show`, `nl`, and `wc`. You use `multi_tool_use.parallel` for that parallelism, and only that. Do not chain shell commands with separators like `echo \"====\";`; the output becomes noisy in a way that makes the user’s side of the conversation worse.\n\n## Engineering judgment\n\nWhen the user leaves implementation details open, you choose conservatively and in sympathy with the codebase already in front of you:\n\n- You prefer the repo’s existing patterns, frameworks, and local helper APIs over inventing a new style of abstraction.\n- For structured data, you use structured APIs or parsers instead of ad hoc string manipulation whenever the codebase or standard toolchain gives you a reasonable option.\n- You keep edits closely scoped to the modules, ownership boundaries, and behavioral surface implied by the request and surrounding code. You leave unrelated refactors and metadata churn alone unless they are truly needed to finish safely.\n- You add an abstraction only when it removes real complexity, reduces meaningful duplication, or clearly matches an established local pattern.\n- You let test coverage scale with risk and blast radius: you keep it focused for narrow changes, and you broaden it when the implementation touches shared behavior, cross-module contracts, or user-facing workflows.\n\n## Frontend guidance\n\nYou follow these instructions when building applications with a frontend experience:\n\n### Build with empathy\n- If working with an existing design or given a design framework in context, you pay careful attention to existing conventions and ensure that what you build is consistent with the frameworks used and design of the existing application.\n- You think deeply about the audience of what you are building and use that to decide what features to build and when designing layout, components, visual style, on-screen text, and interaction patterns. Using your application should feel rich and sophisticated.\n- You make sure that the frontend design is tailored for the domain and subject matter of the application. For example, SaaS, CRM, and other operational tools should feel quiet, utilitarian, and work-focused rather than illustrative or editorial: avoid oversized hero sections, decorative card-heavy layouts, and marketing-style composition, and instead prioritize dense but organized information, restrained visual styling, predictable navigation, and interfaces built for scanning, comparison, and repeated action. A game can be more illustrative, expressive, animated, and playful.\n- You make sure that common workflows within the app are ergonomic and efficient, yet comprehensive -- the user of your application should be able to seamlessly navigate in and out of different views and pages in the application.\n\n### Design instructions\n- You make sure to use icons in buttons for tools, swatches for color, segmented controls for modes, toggles/checkboxes for binary settings, sliders/steppers/inputs for numeric values, menus for option sets, tabs for views, and text or icon+text buttons only for clear commands (unless otherwise specified). Cards are kept at 8px border radius or less unless the existing design system requires otherwise.\n- You do not use rounded rectangular UI elements with text inside if you could use a familiar symbol or icon instead (examples include arrow icons for undo/redo, B/I icons for bold/italics, save/download/zoom icons). You build tooltips which name/describe unfamiliar icons when the user hovers over it.\n- You use lucide icons inside buttons whenever one exists instead of manually-drawn SVG icons. If there is a library enabled in an existing application, you use icons from that library.\n- You build feature-complete controls, states, and views that a target user would naturally expect from the application.\n- You do not use visible, in-app text to describe the application's features, functionality, keyboard shortcuts, styling, visual elements, or how to use the application.\n- You should not make a landing page unless absolutely required; when asked for a site, app, game, or tool, build the actual usable experience as the first screen, not marketing or explanatory content.\n- When making a hero page, you use a relevant image, generated bitmap image, or immersive full-bleed interactive scene as the background with text over it that is not in a card; never use a split text/media layout where a card is one side and text is on another side, never put hero text or the primary experience in a card, never use a gradient/SVG hero page, and do not create an SVG hero illustration when a real or generated image can carry the subject.\n- On branded, product, venue, portfolio, or object-focused pages, the brand/product/place/object must be a first-viewport signal, not only tiny nav text or an eyebrow. Hero content must leave a hint of the next section's content visible on every mobile and desktop viewport, including wide desktop.\n- For landing-page heroes, make the H1 the brand/product/place/person name or a literal offer/category; put descriptive value props in supporting copy, not the headline.\n- Websites and games must use visual assets. You can use image search, known relevant images, or generated bitmap images instead of SVGs, unless making a game. Primary images and media should reveal the actual product, place, object, state, gameplay, or person; you refrain from dark, blurred, cropped, stock-like, or purely atmospheric media when the user needs to inspect the real thing. For highly specific game assets you use custom SVG/Three.js/etc.\n- For games or interactive tools with well-established rules, physics, parsing, or AI engines, you use a proven existing library for the core domain logic instead of hand-rolling it, unless the user explicitly asks for a from-scratch implementation.\n- You use Three.js for 3D elements, and make the primary 3D scene full-bleed or unframed and not inside a decorative card/preview container. Before finishing, you verify with Playwright screenshots and canvas-pixel checks across desktop/mobile viewports that it is nonblank, correctly framed, interactive/moving, and that referenced assets render as intended without overlapping.\n- You do not put UI cards inside other cards. Do not style page sections as floating cards. Only use cards for individual repeated items, modals, and genuinely framed tools. Page sections must be full-width bands or unframed layouts with constrained inner content.\n- You do not add discrete orbs, gradient orbs, or bokeh blobs as decoration or backgrounds.\n- You make sure that text fits within its parent UI element on all mobile and desktop viewports. Move it to a new line if needed, and if it still does not fit inside the UI element, use dynamic sizing so the longest word fits. Text must also not occlude preceding or subsequent content. Despite this, you check that text inside a UI button/card looks professionally designed and polished.\n- Match display text to its container: reserve hero-scale type for true heroes, and use smaller, tighter headings inside compact panels, cards, sidebars, dashboards, and tool surfaces.\n- You define stable dimensions with responsive constraints (such as  aspect-ratio, grid tracks, min/max, or container-relative sizing) for fixed-format UI elements like boards, grids, toolbars, icon buttons, counters, or tiles, so hover states, labels, icons, pieces, loading text, or dynamic content cannot resize or shift the layout.\n- You do not scale font size with viewport width. Letter spacing must be 0, not negative.\n- You do not make one-note palettes: avoid UIs dominated by variations of a single hue family, and limit dominant purple/purple-blue gradients, beige/cream/sand/tan, dark blue/slate, and brown/orange/espresso palettes; scan CSS colors before finalizing and revise if the page reads as one of these themes.\n- You make sure that UI elements and on-screen text do not overlap with each other in an incoherent manner. This is extremely important as it leads to a jarring user experience.\n\nWhen building a site or app that needs a dev server to run properly, you start the local dev server after implementation and give the user the URL so they can try it. If there's already a server on that port, you use another one. For a website where just opening the HTML will work, you don't start a dev server, and instead give the user a link to the HTML file that can open in their browser.\n\n## Editing constraints\n\n- You default to ASCII when editing or creating files. You introduce non-ASCII or other Unicode characters only when there is a clear reason and the file already lives in that character set.\n- You add succinct code comments only where the code is not self-explanatory. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. {"timestamp":"2026-06-08T11:43:29.816Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_kxRmjEGrqvI2tAOSslumc1Jo","output":"Chunk ID: e76aba\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1565\nOutput:\n//! Cognitive MCP Server Binary\n//!\n//! Transports started in parallel:\n//! - HTTP/SSE  (MCP protocol, port 3003)\n//! - gRPC      (CognitiveToolService, port 50052)\n//! - D-Bus     (org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp / /org/opdbus/v1/cognitive)\n//!\n//! On startup the server reads the local WireGuard public key (from the\n//! interface named by $WG_INTERFACE, defaulting to \"netmaker\") and writes the\n//! canonical IdentitySled to /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat so the Ghostbridge\n//! interceptor and Qdrant shuttle can authenticate outbound gRPC calls.\n//!\n//! Bind address resolution order (highest priority first):\n//!   1. COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND / COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND env vars\n//!   2. --http / --grpc CLI flags\n//!   3. WireGuard interface IP detected at startup (if interface is up)\n//!   4. 0.0.0.0 fallback\n\nuse clap::Parser;\nuse op_cognitive_mcp::CognitiveMcpServer;\nuse op_identity::{write_sled_from_wg, WireGuardIdentity};\nuse tracing::{info, warn, Level};\nuse tracing_subscriber::FmtSubscriber;\n\n#[derive(Parser)]\n#[command(name = \"cognitive-mcp-server\")]\n#[command(about = \"Cognitive MCP Server with memory, NotebookLM bridge, gRPC, and D-Bus\")]\nstruct Cli {\n    /// HTTP/SSE server address (MCP protocol).\n    /// If left at 0.0.0.0 the WireGuard interface IP is used when available.\n    /// Override with COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND env var or this flag.\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND\", default_value = \"0.0.0.0:3003\")]\n    http: String,\n\n    /// gRPC server address (CognitiveToolService).\n    /// If left at 0.0.0.0 the WireGuard interface IP is used when available.\n    /// Override with COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND env var or this flag.\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND\", default_value = \"0.0.0.0:50052\")]\n    grpc: String,\n\n    /// CozoDB database path\n    #[arg(\n        long,\n        env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_DB_PATH\",\n        default_value = \"/var/lib/op-cognitive-mcp/memory.db\"\n    )]\n    db: String,\n\n    /// WireGuard interface to read identity from\n    #[arg(long, env = \"WG_INTERFACE\", default_value = \"netmaker\")]\n    wg_interface: String,\n\n    /// Log level\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_LOG_LEVEL\", default_value = \"info\")]\n    log_level: String,\n\n    /// Disable gRPC server\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_DISABLED\")]\n    no_grpc: bool,\n\n    /// Disable HTTP/SSE server\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_HTTP_DISABLED\")]\n    no_http: bool,\n\n    /// Disable D-Bus registration\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_DBUS_DISABLED\")]\n    no_dbus: bool,\n}\n\n/// Promote an `0.0.0.0:PORT` default address to `<wg_ip>:PORT` when the WG\n/// interface is up.  Explicit addresses (not starting with `0.0.0.0:`) are\n/// returned unchanged so env-var or flag overrides always win.\nfn resolve_bind(addr: &str, wg_ip: Option<&str>) -> String {\n    if let Some(rest) = addr.strip_prefix(\"0.0.0.0:\") {\n        if let Some(ip) = wg_ip {\n            return format!(\"{ip}:{rest}\");\n        }\n    }\n    addr.to_string()\n}\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let cli = Cli::parse();\n\n    let level = match cli.log_level.as_str() {\n        \"trace\" => Level::TRACE,\n        \"debug\" => Level::DEBUG,\n        \"warn\" => Level::WARN,\n        \"error\" => Level::ERROR,\n        _ => Level::INFO,\n    };\n\n    let subscriber = FmtSubscriber::builder()\n        .with_max_level(level)\n        .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n        .finish();\n    tracing::subscriber::set_global_default(subscriber)?;\n\n    // ── WireGuard identity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    // 1. Detect local WG IP for bind address resolution.\n    // 2. Write canonical IdentitySled to /dev/shm for Ghostbridge auth.\n    let wg_id = WireGuardIdentity::with_interface(&cli.wg_interface);\n    let wg_ip = wg_id.get_local_ip();\n\n    match wg_id.get_local_pubkey() {\n        Ok(pubkey) => {\n            info!(\n                interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n                pubkey = %pubkey,\n                wg_ip = ?wg_ip,\n                \"Writing WireGuard identity sled to /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat\"\n            );\n            if let Err(e) = write_sled_from_wg(&pubkey) {\n                warn!(\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"Failed to write identity sled — gRPC Ghostbridge auth will not work\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            warn!(\n                interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n                error = %e,\n                \"Could not read WireGuard public key — identity sled not written; \\\n                 set WG_PUBKEY env var to override\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Resolve bind addresses: promote 0.0.0.0 defaults to WG interface IP.\n    let http_addr = resolve_bind(&cli.http, wg_ip.as_deref());\n    let grpc_addr = resolve_bind(&cli.grpc, wg_ip.as_deref());\n\n    info!(\n        http = %http_addr,\n        grpc = %grpc_addr,\n        db = %cli.db,\n        wg_interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n        \"Starting Cognitive MCP Server\"\n    );\n\n    let server = CognitiveMcpServer::new(&cli.db).await?;\n\n    // D-Bus: start first, keep connection alive for the process lifetime.\n    let _dbus_conn = if !cli.no_dbus {\n        match server.start_dbus().await {\n            Ok(conn) => {\n                info!(\"D-Bus registered: org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp\");\n                Some(conn)\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                warn!(\"D-Bus registration failed (continuing without it): {e}\");\n                None\n            }\n        }\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n\n    match (cli.no_grpc, cli.no_http) {\n        (true, true) => {\n            eprintln!(\"Error: both --no-grpc and --no-http specified. Nothing to run.\");\n            std::process::exit(1);\n        }\n        (true, false) => {\n            info!(\"Running HTTP/SSE only\");\n            server.start_http_server(&http_addr).await?;\n        }\n        (false, true) => {\n            info!(\"Running gRPC only\");\n            server.start_grpc_server(&grpc_addr).await?;\n        }\n        (false, false) => {\n            info!(\"Running HTTP/SSE + gRPC\");\n            server.start_dual(&http_addr, &grpc_addr).await?;\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n"}}

Cognitive MCP Client Configuration & Optimization\n//!\n//! Provides connection pooling, caching, retry logic, and optimized transport\n//! patterns for external MCP clients connecting to the cognitive-mcp gateway.\n//!\n//! ## Architecture\n//!\n//! - **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WG IP `100.90.37.254`):\n//!   Universal gateway for ALL external clients: NotebookLM, Droid, Cursor,\n//!   Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. External clients MUST use this endpoint.\n//!\n//! - **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`):\n//!   Loopback/chatbot only. NEVER expose externally.\n//!\n//! ## Client Optimization Strategies\n//!\n//! 1. **Connection Pooling**: Reuse HTTP/SSE connections to reduce latency\n//! 2. **Capability Caching**: Cache tool/resource discovery to reduce round-trips\n//! 3. **Batched Operations**: Parallelize independent tool calls\n//! 4. **Circuit Breaker**: Fail-fast on degraded service\n//! 5. **Exponential Backoff**: Graceful retry with jitter\n//!\n//! ## Usage\n//!\n//! ```rust\n//! use op_cognitive_mcp::client_config::{CognitiveMcpClient, ClientConfig};\n//!\n//! let config = ClientConfig::for_external_client(\"droid-instance-1\");\n//! let client = CognitiveMcpClient::connect(config).await?;\n//!\n//! // Cached tool discovery\n//! let tools = client.list_tools_cached().await?;\n//!\n//! // Batched execution\n//! let results = client.call_tools_batch([\n//!     (\"memory/store\", json!({\"key\": \"ctx\", \"value\": \"data\"})),\n//!     (\"rag/search\", json!({\"query\": \"architecture\"})),\n//! ]).await?;\n//! ```\n\nuse crate::quota::{QuotaManager, QuotaTier};\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse reqwest::{Client as HttpClient, ClientBuilder};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse serde_json::Value;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::time::{Duration, Instant};\nuse tokio::sync::RwLock;\nuse tracing::{debug, info, warn};\n\n/// Default cognitive-mcp endpoint for external clients.\n/// Per AGENTS.md: cognitive-mcp (`:3003`, Netmaker WG IP `100.90.37.254`)\n/// is the universal gateway for ALL external clients.\npub const COGNITIVE_MCP_DEFAULT_ENDPOINT: &str = \"http://100.90.37.254:3003\";\n\n/// Default compact-mcp endpoint (loopback only, chatbot only).\npub const COMPACT_MCP_DEFAULT_ENDPOINT: &str = \"http://127.0.0.1:11436\";\n\n/// Connection pool configuration.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct PoolConfig {\n    /// Maximum idle connections per host.\n    pub max_idle: usize,\n    /// Connection idle timeout before closing.\n    pub idle_timeout_secs: u64,\n    /// Maximum connections in the pool.\n    pub max_connections: usize,\n    /// Enable HTTP/2 if server supports it.\n    pub use_http2: bool,\n}\n\nimpl Default for PoolConfig {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            max_idle: 10,\n            idle_timeout_secs: 90,\n            max_connections: 100,\n            use_http2: true,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Retry configuration with exponential backoff.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct RetryConfig {\n    /// Maximum retry attempts.\n    pub max_retries: u32,\n    /// Base delay in milliseconds.\n    pub base_delay_ms: u64,\n    /// Maximum delay in milliseconds.\n    pub max_delay_ms: u64,\n    /// Backoff multiplier.\n    pub backoff_multiplier: f64,\n    /// Enable jitter to prevent thundering herd.\n    pub use_jitter: bool,\n}\n\nimpl Default for RetryConfig {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            max_retries: 3,\n            base_delay_ms: 100,\n            max_delay_ms: 5000,\n            backoff_multiplier: 2.0,\n            use_jitter: true,\n        }\n         path,\n            layout: \"compact\",\n            size: COMPACT_SLED_SIZE,\n            is_valid,\n            wireguard_pubkey_hex: hex::encode(wg),\n            wireguard_pubkey_b64: {"timestamp":"2026-06-08T11:50:30.653Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"identity detaches fro wg protocol :'ve launched an exploration agent to map the codebase. I'll have a detailed breakdown ready once it completes — including the WireGuard session derivation, NextDNS header injection, gRPC forwarding logic, and how that maps to the concert/wristband/valet analogy.\n\nHere's the full breakdown of the zero-trust identity pipeline, mapped to the concert analogy throughout.\n\nThe Concert Analogy\nYou arrive at a venue. You hand your keys to the valet (WireGuard). The valet parks your car and gives you a claim ticket (session ID). At the door, you exchange the ticket for an all-access wristband (the Ghostbridge identity sled). Every backstage door checks the wristband — not your car, not your ticket — just the wristband. Your car (the WireGuard tunnel) never enters the venue.\n\nStage 1 — The Valet: WireGuard Handshake & Session ID Derivation\nFiles: crates/op-gateway/src/wireguard_auth.rs:529-633\n\nWhen a peer connects over WireGuard, the gateway derives three cryptographic artifacts:\n\nSession ID (the claim ticket)\n// wireguard_auth.rs:529-540\nlet input = format!(\"WG-SESSION-{}-{}\", peer_pubkey, Self::current_timestamp());\nlet session_ids = self.crypto_engine.generate_session_ids_batch(&[input.as_bytes()]);\n// → BLAKE2s hash → 128-bit hex string\nInput: Curve25519 peer public key + current timestamp\nAlgorithm: SIMD-accelerated BLAKE2s\nOutput: 16-byte hex session ID — the peer's claim ticket\nPSK (stable parking spot number)\n// wireguard_auth.rs:542-593\nlet salt = b\"WG-STABLE-PSK-2024\";  // fixed — no timestamp\n// Argon2 KDF over peer pubkey\nDeliberately does not rotate — rotating it would lock peers out mid-session, like changing the valet lot number while cars are still parked.\n\nSession Key (per-visit ephemeral)\n// wireguard_auth.rs:595-633\nlet server_nonce = self.generate_server_nonce().await?;\n// Argon2 + nonce → ephemeral key, rotated per connection\nThe Session Record (the claim stub kept by the valet)\n// wireguard_auth.rs:200-215\npub struct WireGuardSession {\n    pub session_id: String,        // BLAKE2s(pubkey + timestamp)\n    pub peer_pubkey: String,\n    pub psk: String,               // stable Argon2\n    pub expires_at: u64,           // 1 hour TTL\n    pub auth_method: String,       // \"wireguard\"\n    pub key_rotation_count: u32,\n    // ...\n}\nPersisted to SQLite (wireguard_sessions table) and cached in DashMap (no SQL in the hot path).\n\nStage 2 — The Wristband Printer: IdentitySled\nFiles: crates/op-mcp-proxy/src/sled.rs, crates/op-identity/src/schema_bridge.rs\n\nOnce the WireGuard session is established, a 152-byte shared-memory struct (/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat) is stamped — the all-access wristband:\n\nIdentitySled layout (repr(C), 152 bytes):\n  [ 0.. 32]  wireguard_pubkey    — who you are\n  [32.. 40]  mutation_index      — which version of the schema you authenticated against\n  [40.. 72]  hashed_footprint    — Blake3(current schema state) — the hologram on the wristband\n  [72.. 88]  trace_id            — UUID v4 — your unique wristband serial number\n  [88.. 92]  schema_version\n  [92..152]  reserved\n  [192..208] nextdns_profile     — e.g., \"689ec7\" — your VIP section access\nThe footprint (Blake3 hash of the live schema state) is the hologram — it proves the wristband was issued by tonight's venue, not a forgery from last week's show.\n\nThe trace_id is the serial number stamped on your wrist — immutable, linked to a Qdrant vector record for full accountability.\n\nNextDNS Profile (the VIP section pass)\n# deploy/nextdns/upsert-rewrite.py\n# Profile ID: 689ec7\n# Upserts DNS rewrites: dashboard.3tched.com → 10.0.0.1\nThe NextDNS profile ID travels with the identity sled. It tells the DNS layer which routing rules apply to this peer — their section of the venue.\n\nStage 3 — The Door Scanner: xray Header Injection\nFile: deploy/incus/privacy-xray-ingress/etc/xray/config.json:47-50\n\nxray sits at the venue entrance. It reads the wristband (sled) and stamps the metadata onto every gRPC call:\n\n\"grpcSettings\": {\n  \"serviceName\": \"Ghostbridge.StateSync\",\n  \"multiMode\": true,\n  \"metadata\": {\n    \"X-Ghostbridge-Footprint\": \"<Blake3 footprint hex>\",\n    \"X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID\":  \"<UUID v4 hex>\"\n  }\n}\nAt this point, WireGuard is dropped. The tunnel delivered the peer to the door; the tunnel itself does not go backstage. xray strips the WireGuard framing and forwards a plain gRPC call carrying only the two header stamps. The car stays in the lot.\n\nThe NextDNS profile influences DNS resolution at this layer — selector_ip routing directs packets to the correct Incus container before they ever reach the gRPC endpoint.\n\nStage 4 — The Backstage Guard: GhostbridgeInterceptor\nFile: crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/interceptor.rs:34-84\n\nEvery gRPC call hits this Tonic middleware on port 18789 before any handler sees it:\n\npub fn ghostbridge_interceptor(mut req: Request<()>) -> Result<Request<()>, Status> {\n    // 1. Wristband must be present\n    let footprint_value = req.metadata().get(\"x-ghostbridge-footprint\").cloned();\n    let trace_value    = req.metadata().get(\"x-ghostbridge-trace-id\").cloned();\n\n    if footprint_value.is_none() || trace_value.is_none() {\n        return Err(Status::unauthenticated(\n            \"A.N.N.A. Scribe: Missing Ghostbridge Identity Sled. Connection Dropped.\",\n        ));\n    }\n\n    // 2. Zero-copy mmap read of the live sled (no DB hit, no network hop)\n    let (sled_ptr, _mmap) = op_identity::read_sled()?;\n    let sled = unsafe { &*sled_ptr };\n\n    // 3. Hologram check — footprint must match tonight's schema state exactly\n    let expected_footprint = hex::encode(sled.hashed_footprint);\n    if request_footprint != expected_footprint {\n        return Err(Status::permission_denied(\n            \"A.N.N.A. Scribe: Temporal Hash Mismatch. Session footprint out of sync.\",\n        ));\n    }\n\n    // 4. Embed trace ID into gRPC extensions for downstream accountability\n    req.extensions_mut().insert(trace_val);\n    Ok(req)\n}\nValidity rule: the sled is live only if hashed_footprint != [0u8;32] AND trace_id != [0u8;16]. A zero field means the wristband was never properly stamped — instant ejection.\n\nThe check is zero-copy — the sled lives in tmpfs (/dev/shm), mmap'd directly into the process. No SQL, no network, no disk. The guard glances at your wrist under UV light in milliseconds.\n\nStage 5 — Backstage: gRPC Routing to op-dbus\nFile: crates/op-mcp-proxy/src/main.rs:94-105\n\nOnce the interceptor passes the call, it routes to the internal gRPC service:\n\nDefault: http://10.200.0.2:50051  (op-dbus, inside the privacy network)\nSubnet assignments per peer come from schemas/plugin/privacy_routes.json:\n\n{\n  \"wireguard_public_key\": \"P8c9Kjnv4B3r6C4+...\",\n  \"assigned_ip\":  \"10.100.0.2/32\",    // WireGuard tunnel allocation\n  \"selector_ip\":  \"10.100.0.2\",       // OpenFlow packet-match label\n  \"container_name\": \"privacy-route-550e8400\"\n}\nOpenFlow matches selector_ip and routes to the correct Incus container. The WireGuard subnet (10.100.0.0/24) exists only to give each peer a unique identity label — it is never forwarded as a WireGuard packet beyond the gateway.\n\nA Linux user session (wg-{first12ofpubkey}) is created via loginctl enable-linger, giving the peer a D-Bus session and $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR — the backstage room with their name on the door.\n\nComplete Flow, Annotated\n[Peer]\n  │  WireGuard UDP (Curve25519 handshake)\n  ▼\n[op-gateway / WireGuard endpoint]\n  │  BLAKE2s(pubkey + timestamp) → session_id        ← claim ticket issued\n  │  Argon2(pubkey, stable-salt) → PSK               ← stable parking spot\n  │  Argon2(pubkey, nonce)       → session_key        ← tonight's coat check\n  │  Write IdentitySled → /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat  ← wristband stamped\n  │\n  │  WireGuard framing DROPPED here ──────────────────← car stays with valet\n  ▼\n[xray ingress]\n  │  Reads sled: footprint + trace_id + nextdns_profile\n  │  Injects gRPC metadata headers:\n  │    X-Ghostbridge-Footprint: <blake3-hex>\n  │    X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID:  <uuid4-hex>\n  │  NextDNS profile → DNS rewrites applied (VIP section routing)\n  ▼\n[GhostbridgeInterceptor — port 18789]\n  │  Header present?    No  → 401 \"Connection Dropped\"\n  │  Footprint matches?
