          context_engine.clone(),\n                DEFAULT_COLLECTION.to_string(),\n            )\n            .await?;\n            tracing::info!(registered = n, \"Registered code-context tools\");\n        }\n\n        Ok(Self {\n            memory_store,\n            cozo_shuttle,\n            qdrant_shuttle,\n            tool_registry,\n            session_manager,\n            quota_manager,\n            gemini_fallback,\n            rag_pipeline,\n            context_engine,\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub async fn start_http_server(self, addr: &str) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n        use crate::context_server::build_context_router;\n        use op_mcp::{HttpSseTransport, McpServer, McpServerConfig, Transport};\n\n        let config = McpServerConfig {\n            name: Some(\"cognitive-mcp\".to_string()),\n            compact_mode: false,\n            ..Default::default()\n        };\n\n        let executor = Arc::new(RegistryExecutor::new(self.tool_registry.clone()));\n        let mcp_server = Arc::new(McpServer::with_executor(config, executor));\n\n        // Mount the context-awareness SSE endpoints on the same HTTP server\n        // so they share auth, CORS, and the port with the MCP protocol routes.\n        let context_router = build_context_router(\n            self.context_engine.clone(),\n            self.memory_store.clone(),\n            self.session_manager.clone(),\n        );\n\n        let transport = HttpSseTransport::new(addr.to_string())\n            .with_extra_router(context_router);\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            addr = %addr,\n            \"Cognitive MCP Server listening (MCP + context-awareness endpoints)\"\n        );\n        transport.serve(mcp_server).await?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub async fn start_grpc_server(&self, addr: &str) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n        let grpc_service = CognitiveGrpcService::new(\n            self.memory_store.clone(),\n            self.session_manager.clone(),\n            self.quota_manager.clone(),\n            self.gemini_fallback.clone(),\n        );\n\n        let reflection = tonic_reflection::server::Builder::configure()\n            .register_encoded_file_descriptor_set(crate::proto::FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SET)\n            .build_v1()\n            .expect(\"failed to build cognitive reflection service\");\n\n        let (mut health_reporter, health_service) = tonic_health::server::health_reporter();\n        health_reporter\n            .set_serving::<CognitiveToolServiceServer<CognitiveGrpcService>>()\n            .await;\n\n        let socket_addr: std::net::SocketAddr = addr.parse()?;\n        tracing::info!(addr = %socket_addr, \"Cognitive gRPC Server listening\");\n\n        tonic::transport::Server::builder()\n            .accept_http1(true)\n            .add_service(tonic_web::enable(\n                CognitiveToolServiceServer::with_interceptor(\n                    grpc_service,\n                    crate::interceptor::ghostbridge_interceptor,\n                ),\n            ))\n            .add_service(tonic_web::enable(reflection))\n            .add_service(tonic_web::enable(health_service))\n            .serve(socket_addr)\n            .await?;\n"}}

I'll have a detailed breakdown ready once it completes — including the WireGuard session derivation, NextDNS header injection, gRPC forwarding logic, and how that maps to the concert/wristband/valet analogy.\n\nHere's the full breakdown of the zero-trust identity pipeline, mapped to the concert analogy throughout.\n\nThe Concert Analogy\nYou arrive at a venue. You hand your keys to the valet (WireGuard). The valet parks your car and gives you a claim ticket (session ID). At the door, you exchange the ticket for an all-access wristband (the Ghostbridge identity sled). Every backstage door checks the wristband — not your car, not your ticket — just the wristband. Your car (the WireGuard tunnel) never enters the venue.\n\nStage 1 — The Valet: WireGuard Handshake & Session ID Derivation\nFiles: crates/op-gateway/src/wireguard_auth.rs:529-633\n\nWhen a peer connects over WireGuard, the gateway derives three cryptographic artifacts:\n\nSession ID (the claim ticket)\n// wireguard_auth.rs:529-540\nlet input = format!(\"WG-SESSION-{}-{}\", peer_pubkey, Self::current_timestamp());\nlet session_ids = self.crypto_engine.generate_session_ids_batch(&[input.as_bytes()]);\n// → BLAKE2s hash → 128-bit hex string\nInput: Curve25519 peer public key + current timestamp\nAlgorithm: SIMD-accelerated BLAKE2s\nOutput: 16-byte hex session ID — the peer's claim ticket\nPSK (stable parking spot number)\n// wireguard_auth.rs:542-593\nlet salt = b\"WG-STABLE-PSK-2024\";  // fixed — no timestamp\n// Argon2 KDF over peer pubkey\nDeliberately does not rotate — rotating it would lock peers out mid-session, like changing the valet lot number while cars are still parked.\n\nSession Key (per-visit ephemeral)\n// wireguard_auth.rs:595-633\nlet server_nonce = self.generate_server_nonce().await?;\n// Argon2 + nonce → ephemeral key, rotated per connection\nThe Session Record (the claim stub kept by the valet)\n// wireguard_auth.rs:200-215\npub struct WireGuardSession {\n    pub session_id: String,        // BLAKE2s(pubkey + timestamp)\n    pub peer_pubkey: String,\n    pub psk: String,               // stable Argon2\n    pub expires_at: u64,           // 1 hour TTL\n    pub auth_method: String,       // \"wireguard\"\n    pub key_rotation_count: u32,\n    // ...\n}\nPersisted to SQLite (wireguard_sessions table) and cached in DashMap (no SQL in the hot path).\n\nStage 2 — The Wristband Printer: IdentitySled\nFiles: crates/op-mcp-proxy/src/sled.rs, crates/op-identity/src/schema_bridge.rs\n\nOnce the WireGuard session is established, a 152-byte shared-memory struct (/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat) is stamped — the all-access wristband:\n\nIdentitySled layout (repr(C), 152 bytes):\n  [ 0.. 32]  wireguard_pubkey    — who you are\n  [32.. 40]  mutation_index      — which version of the schema you authenticated against\n  [40.. 72]  hashed_footprint    — Blake3(current schema state) — the hologram on the wristband\n  [72.. 88]  trace_id            — UUID v4 — your unique wristband serial number\n  [88.. 92]  schema_version\n  [92..152]  reserved\n  [192..208] nextdns_profile     — e.g., \"689ec7\" — your VIP section access\nThe footprint (Blake3 hash of the live schema state) is the hologram — it proves the wristband was issued by tonight's venue, not a forgery from last week's show.\n\nThe trace_id is the serial number stamped on your wrist — immutable, linked to a Qdrant vector record for full accountability.\n\nNextDNS Profile (the VIP section pass)\n# deploy/nextdns/upsert-rewrite.py\n# Profile ID: 689ec7\n# Upserts DNS rewrites: dashboard.3tched.com → 10.0.0.1\nThe NextDNS profile ID travels with the identity sled. It tells the DNS layer which routing rules apply to this peer — their section of the venue.\n\nStage 3 — The Door Scanner: xray Header Injection\nFile: deploy/incus/privacy-xray-ingress/etc/xray/config.json:47-50\n\nxray sits at the venue entrance. It reads the wristband (sled) and stamps the metadata onto every gRPC call:\n\n\"grpcSettings\": {\n  \"serviceName\": \"Ghostbridge.StateSync\",\n  \"multiMode\": true,\n  \"metadata\": {\n    \"X-Ghostbridge-Footprint\": \"<Blake3 footprint hex>\",\n    \"X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID\":  \"<UUID v4 hex>\"\n  }\n}\nAt this point, WireGuard is dropped. The tunnel delivered the peer to the door; the tunnel itself does not go backstage. xray strips the WireGuard framing and forwards a plain gRPC call carrying only the two header stamps. The car stays in the lot.\n\nThe NextDNS profile influences DNS resolution at this layer — selector_ip routing directs packets to the correct Incus container before they ever reach the gRPC endpoint.\n\nStage 4 — The Backstage Guard: GhostbridgeInterceptor\nFile: crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/interceptor.rs:34-84\n\nEvery gRPC call hits this Tonic middleware on port 18789 before any handler sees it:\n\npub fn ghostbridge_interceptor(mut req: Request<()>) -> Result<Request<()>, Status> {\n    // 1. Wristband must be present\n    let footprint_value = req.metadata().get(\"x-ghostbridge-footprint\").cloned();\n    let trace_value    = req.metadata().get(\"x-ghostbridge-trace-id\").cloned();\n\n    if footprint_value.is_none() || trace_value.is_none() {\n        return Err(Status::unauthenticated(\n            \"A.N.N.A. Scribe: Missing Ghostbridge Identity Sled. Connection Dropped.\",\n        ));\n    }\n\n    // 2. Zero-copy mmap read of the live sled (no DB hit, no network hop)\n    let (sled_ptr, _mmap) = op_identity::read_sled()?;\n    let sled = unsafe { &*sled_ptr };\n\n    // 3. Hologram check — footprint must match tonight's schema state exactly\n    let expected_footprint = hex::encode(sled.hashed_footprint);\n    if request_footprint != expected_footprint {\n        return Err(Status::permission_denied(\n            \"A.N.N.A. Scribe: Temporal Hash Mismatch. Session footprint out of sync.\",\n        ));\n    }\n\n    // 4. Embed trace ID into gRPC extensions for downstream accountability\n    req.extensions_mut().insert(trace_val);\n    Ok(req)\n}\nValidity rule: the sled is live only if hashed_footprint != [0u8;32] AND trace_id != [0u8;16]. A zero field means the wristband was never properly stamped — instant ejection.\n\nThe check is zero-copy — the sled lives in tmpfs (/dev/shm), mmap'd directly into the process. No SQL, no network, no disk. The guard glances at your wrist under UV light in milliseconds.\n\nStage 5 — Backstage: gRPC Routing to op-dbus\nFile: crates/op-mcp-proxy/src/main.rs:94-105\n\nOnce the interceptor passes the call, it routes to the internal gRPC service:\n\nDefault: http://10.200.0.2:50051  (op-dbus, inside the privacy network)\nSubnet assignments per peer come from schemas/plugin/privacy_routes.json:\n\n{\n  \"wireguard_public_key\": \"P8c9Kjnv4B3r6C4+...\",\n  \"assigned_ip\":  \"10.100.0.2/32\",    // WireGuard tunnel allocation\n  \"selector_ip\":  \"10.100.0.2\",       // OpenFlow packet-match label\n  \"container_name\": \"privacy-route-550e8400\"\n}\nOpenFlow matches selector_ip and routes to the correct Incus container. The WireGuard subnet (10.100.0.0/24) exists only to give each peer a unique identity label — it is never forwarded as a WireGuard packet beyond the gateway.\n\nA Linux user session (wg-{first12ofpubkey}) is created via loginctl enable-linger, giving the peer a D-Bus session and $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR — the backstage room with their name on the door.\n\nComplete Flow, Annotated\n[Peer]\n  │  WireGuard UDP (Curve25519 handshake)\n  ▼\n[op-gateway / WireGuard endpoint]\n  │  BLAKE2s(pubkey + timestamp) → session_id        ← claim ticket issued\n  │  Argon2(pubkey, stable-salt) → PSK               ← stable parking spot\n  │  Argon2(pubkey, nonce)       → session_key        ← tonight's coat check\n  │  Write IdentitySled → /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat  ← wristband stamped\n  │\n  │  WireGuard framing DROPPED here ──────────────────← car stays with valet\n  ▼\n[xray ingress]\n  │  Reads sled: footprint + trace_id + nextdns_profile\n  │  Injects gRPC metadata headers:\n  │    X-Ghostbridge-Footprint: <blake3-hex>\n  │    X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID:  <uuid4-hex>\n  │  NextDNS profile → DNS rewrites applied (VIP section routing)\n  ▼\n[GhostbridgeInterceptor — port 18789]\n  │  Header present?    No  → 401 \"Connection Dropped\"\n  │  Footprint matches? No  → 403 \"Temporal Hash Mismatch\"\n  │  Zero-copy mmap sled read (tmpfs, no DB)\n  │  Inject trace_id into gRPC extensions\n  ▼\n[op-dbus gRPC — 10.200.0.2:50051]\n  │  Full access to internal services\n  │  Trace ID rides every call → Qdrant vector linkage for audit\n  ▼\n[Incus container — privacy-route-{user_id}]\n  └─ Linux user session, D-Bus activated, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR alive\nWhy This Is Genuinely Zero-Trust\nZero-Trust Principle\tImplementation\nNever trust, always verify\tEvery gRPC call re-validates the live sled footprint — no cached \"logged in\" state\nVerify cryptographic state, not identity claims\tFootprint is Blake3 of current schema — a stale wristband from an old schema is invalid\nLeast privilege\tNextDNS profile scopes DNS; assigned_ip/32 scopes the subnet to exactly one peer\nFull audit trail\tTrace ID links every call to a Qdrant vector record — immutable, append-only\nNo implicit trust from network location\tBeing inside 10.100.0.0/24 grants nothing — the wristband check happens regardless\nThe WireGuard subnet is purely a cryptographic identity label — it gets the peer through the front door and into the valet system. The moment they're inside, the car (the tunnel) stays parked. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking Optionally `select_notebook` to make it the default.\\n3. `ask_question` — start asking. Save the returned `session_id` and\\n   reuse it for follow-up questions to keep context.\\n\\n## Notebook ID flow\\n\\n`list_notebooks` / `search_notebooks` / `get_notebook` all return\\nnotebook objects with an `id` field. That `id` feeds\\n`select_notebook`, `update_notebook`, `remove_notebook`, and the\\noptional `notebook_id` argument on `ask_question` / `add_source` /\\naudio tools.\\n\\n## Session ID flow\\n\\n`ask_question` returns `session_id` on every call. Pass that same id\\nback as `session_id` on later `ask_question` calls to maintain a\\nconversational context (NotebookLM uses session-RAG so follow-ups get\\nsharper). `list_sessions` enumerates live sessions; `reset_session`\\nclears chat history (same id), `close_session` ends a session.\\n\\n## Source ingestion (multi-source)\\n\\nCall `add_source` once per source — text snippets and URLs are supported.\\nNotebookLM crawls/indexes each source asynchronously; new sources are\\ntypically queryable within 5–30 seconds after `add_source` succeeds.\\n\\n## Audio Overview (async chain — important)\\n\\n`generate_audio` is **non-blocking** by default: it triggers the render\\nand returns immediately with `status: \\\"started\\\"` (or `\\\"in_progress\\\"` if\\na generation was already running, or `\\\"ready\\\"` if one already existed).\\nGeneration typically takes 2–10 minutes.\\n\\nTo complete the workflow, poll `get_audio_status` every ~30 s. When it\\nreturns `status: \\\"ready\\\"`, call `download_audio` with an absolute\\n`destination_dir` to save the file. Calling `download_audio` before\\n`ready` will surface a clear error.\\n\\nFor synchronous behaviour pass `wait_for_completion: true` to\\n`generate_audio` (legacy mode — blocks for up to `timeout_ms`).\\n\\n## Constraints\\n\\n- Free Google accounts: 50 NotebookLM queries/day. `re_auth` rotates\\n  accounts.\\n- Session timeout: ~15 min idle (see `get_health.session_timeout`).\\n- File / YouTube / Drive source uploads are not yet implemented in v2.0.\\n- Audio Overview is the only Studio output exposed in v2.0; Video,\\n  Presentation, Mindmap, Flashcards, Quiz, Infographic, and Datatable are\\n  generated by NotebookLM but not yet wrapped by this server.\\n\"},\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":1}\r\n\r\n\u001b[2m2026-06-08T12:27:45.404694Z\u001b[0m \u001b[34mDEBUG\u001b[0m \u001b[2mop_mcp::external_client\u001b[0m\u001b[2m:\u001b[0m MCP server initialized: notebooklm\r\n\u001b[2m2026-06-08T12:27:45.404784Z\u001b[0m \u001b[32m INFO\u001b[0m \u001b[2mop_mcp::external_client\u001b[0m\u001b[2m:\u001b[0m External MCP server initialized in 2.22s\r\n\u001b[2m2026-06-08T12:27:45.405032Z\u001b[0m \u001b[34mDEBUG\u001b[0m \u001b[2mop_mcp::external_client\u001b[0m\u001b[2m:\u001b[0m Sent request to notebooklm: {\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":2,\"method\":\"tools/list\",\"params\":{}}\r\n\u001b[36mℹ️  [12:27:45] 📋 [MCP] list_tools request received\u001b[0m\r\n\u001b[2m2026-06-08T12:27:45.406873Z\u001b[0m \u001b[34mDEBUG\u001b[0m \u001b[2mop_mcp::external_client\u001b[0m\u001b[2m:\u001b[0m Received response from notebooklm: {\"result\":{\"tools\":[{\"name\":\"ask_question\",\"description\":\"# Conversational Research Partner (NotebookLM • Gemini 2.5 • Session RAG)\\n\\n## No Active Notebook\\n- Visit https://notebooklm.google to create a notebook and get a share link\\n- Use **add_notebook** to add it to your library (explains how to get the link)\\n- Use **list_notebooks** to show available sources\\n- Use **select_notebook** to set one active\\n\\n> Auth tip: If login is required, use the prompt 'notebooklm.auth-setup' and then verify with the 'get_health' tool. 102\t    /// `bridge` is the bridge name, `args_json` is a JSON array of extra CLI args.\n   103\t    async fn ofctl(&self, bridge: &str, args_json: &str) -> zbus::Result<String>;\n   104\t\n   105\t  async fn barrier(&self) -> zbus::Result<String>;\n   110\t\n   111\t    /// Dump all flows. {"timestamp":"2026-06-08T12:38:38.653Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"I want `rovs` to be the schema-backed D-Bus authority for the Rust Open vSwitch transport/control surface.\n\nConcretely:\n\n`rovs` plugin:\n- Owns `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/rovs`\n- Declares that the ROVS subsystem exists and is schema-valid\n- Exposes the contract for its child surfaces:\n  - `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/rovs/jsonrpc`\n  - `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/rovs/openflow`\n  - `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/rovs/proxy`\n- Carries state like:\n  - OVSDB socket path\n  - connected/not connected\n  - supported transports: `unix`, `tcp`, maybe `ssl`\n  - supported surfaces: `jsonrpc`, `openflow`, `proxy`\n  - bridge/controller status\n  - endpoint mappings like Qdrant transport if we add that later\n\nWhat it should do:\n- Be the parent plugin that validates the Open vSwitch daemon’s D-Bus objects.\n- Make `op-openvswitch-daemon` legal under your rule: “if it does not have a plugin, it does not exist.”\n- Let other plugins call ROVS through D-Bus without using raw paths that are outside the plugin tree.\n- Replace the invalid legacy paths:\n  - `/org/opdbus/rovs/jsonrpc`\n  - `/org/opdbus/rovs/openflow`\n  - `/org/opdbus/rovs/proxy`\n\nWhat it should not do:\n- It should not be a second network plugin.\n- It should not replace `net`, `openflow`, or `ovsdb_bridge`.\n- It should not become business logic for every bridge/flow. Those plugins can still own their domain behavior.\n- It should not bypass D-Bus or `PluginSchema`.\n\nHow it relates to existing plugins:\n- `rovs_commands`: read-only command vocabulary/schema. Keep it as reference/docs/tool schema if useful.\n- `ovsdb_daemon`: currently represents the daemon binary. This could either remain as daemon status, or be folded into `rovs`.\n- `openflow`: owns flow policy/state.\n- `ovsdb_bridge`: owns bridge state.\n- `rovs`: owns the transport/control-plane endpoint contract for the Rust Open vSwitch daemon.\n\nFor Qdrant, this means the transport repair should eventually go through a validated path like:\n\n`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/rovs/proxy.AttachPort(...)`\n\nor a more specific method under `rovs` if we add endpoint proxy methods, instead of unmanaged Incus `forkproxy` state.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-08T12:40:59.566Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes. For this case, Qdrant does not necessarily need its own top-level plugin if it is modeled as part of the existing `cognitive_mcp` plugin schema.\n\nThat is probably the right fit here:\n\n- `cognitive_mcp` is the service that uses Qdrant for code RAG/context retrieval.\n- Its schema already has Qdrant fields, including `qdrant_collection`.\n- The failing thing is the Qdrant backing store/transport for `cognitive_mcp`, not a general system-wide OVS object.\n- So the projected object should likely live under something like:\n\n`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/cognitive_mcp/qdrant`\n\nor another projection-derived child path from the `cognitive_mcp` schema.\n\nThat keeps the rule intact:\n\n“If it does not have a plugin, it does not exist.”\n\nHere, Qdrant exists because it is a schema-backed object inside the `cognitive_mcp` plugin contract.\n\nThe practical fix path is:\n\n1. Inspect `cognitive_mcp_plugin_schema()` and its current state for Qdrant fields.\n2. Ensure Qdrant endpoint/transport state is represented there.\n3. Use projection to expose that Qdrant object under `cognitive_mcp`.\n4. Repair runtime: start Qdrant in the Incus container and make cognitive MCP’s configured endpoint healthy.\n5. Only use `op-openvswitch-daemon` if the projected `cognitive_mcp.qdrant` object declares that its transport is OVS/ROVS-managed.\n\nSo I would not make a standalone `rovs` plugin or standalone `qdrant` plugin unless the schema wants Qdrant as a global vector-store resource. For this bug, it belongs under `cognitive_mcp`.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-08T12:40:59.572Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"Yes. For this case, Qdrant does not necessarily need its own top-level plugin if it is modeled as part of the existing `cognitive_mcp` plugin schema.\n\nThat is probably the right fit here:\n\n- `cognitive_mcp` is the service that uses Qdrant for code RAG/context retrieval.\n- Its schema already has Qdrant fields, including `qdrant_collection`.\n- The failing thing is the Qdrant backing store/transport for `cognitive_mcp`, not a general system-wide OVS object.\n- So the projected object should likely live under something like:\n\n`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/cognitive_mcp/qdrant`\n\nor another projection-derived child path from the `cognitive_mcp` schema.\n\nThat keeps the rule intact:\n\n“If it does not have a plugin, it does not exist.”\n\nHere, Qdrant exists because it is a schema-backed object inside the `cognitive_mcp` plugin contract.\n\nThe practical fix path is:\n\n1. Inspect `cognitive_mcp_plugin_schema()` and its current state for Qdrant fields.\n2. Ensure Qdrant endpoint/transport state is represented there.\n3. Use projection to expose that Qdrant object under `cognitive_mcp`.\n4. Repair runtime: start Qdrant in the Incus container and make cognitive MCP’s configured endpoint healthy.\n5. Only use `op-openvswitch-daemon` if the projected `cognitive_mcp.qdrant` object declares that its transport is OVS/ROVS-managed.\n\nSo I would not make a standalone `rovs` plugin or standalone `qdrant` plugin unless the schema wants Qdrant as a global vector-store resource. For this bug, it belongs under `cognitive_mcp`."}],"phase":"final_answer"}}

You hand your keys to the valet (WireGuard). The valet parks your car and gives you a claim ticket (session ID). At the door, you exchange the ticket for an all-access wristband (the Ghostbridge identity sled). Every backstage door checks the wristband — not your car, not your ticket — just the wristband. Your car (the WireGuard tunnel) never enters the venue.\n\nStage 1 — The Valet: WireGuard Handshake & Session ID Derivation\nFiles: crates/op-gateway/src/wireguard_auth.rs:529-633\n\nWhen a peer connects over WireGuard, the gateway derives three cryptographic artifacts:\n\nSession ID (the claim ticket)\n// wireguard_auth.rs:529-540\nlet input = format!(\"WG-SESSION-{}-{}\", peer_pubkey, Self::current_timestamp());\nlet session_ids = self.crypto_engine.generate_session_ids_batch(&[input.as_bytes()]);\n// → BLAKE2s hash → 128-bit hex string\nInput: Curve25519 peer public key + current timestamp\nAlgorithm: SIMD-accelerated BLAKE2s\nOutput: 16-byte hex session ID — the peer's claim ticket\nPSK (stable parking spot number)\n// wireguard_auth.rs:542-593\nlet salt = b\"WG-STABLE-PSK-2024\";  // fixed — no timestamp\n// Argon2 KDF over peer pubkey\nDeliberately does not rotate — rotating it would lock peers out mid-session, like changing the valet lot number while cars are still parked.\n\nSession Key (per-visit ephemeral)\n// wireguard_auth.rs:595-633\nlet server_nonce = self.generate_server_nonce().await?;\n// Argon2 + nonce → ephemeral key, rotated per connection\nThe Session Record (the claim stub kept by the valet)\n// wireguard_auth.rs:200-215\npub struct WireGuardSession {\n    pub session_id: String,        // BLAKE2s(pubkey + timestamp)\n Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking canonical convention\npub fn is_canonical_plugin_path(path: &str) -> bool {\n    path.starts_with(PLUGIN_BASE_PATH)\n}\n\n/// Normalize a plugin path to canonical form\n///\n/// Converts legacy paths to canonical paths\n///\n/// # Examples\n/// - `/opdbus/v1/plugins/net` → `/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/net`\n/// - `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/net` → `/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/net`\n/// - `/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/net` → `/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/net` (already canonical)\npub fn normalize_plugin_path(path: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let trimmed = path.trim().trim_matches('/');\n\n    // Already canonical\n    if trimmed.starts_with(\"org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/\") {\n        return Some(format!(\"/{}\", trimmed));\n    }\n\n    // Legacy: /opdbus/v1/plugins/{name}\n    if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_prefix(\"opdbus/v1/plugins/\") {\n        let name = rest.split('/').next()?;\n        return Some(plugin_path(name));\n    }\n\n    // Some(plugin_path(name));\n    }\n\n    // Just a plugin name\n    if !trimmed.contains('/') {\n        return Some(plugin_path(trimmed));\n    }\n\n    None\n}\n\n/// Extract plugin name from a path (canonical or legacy)\n///\n/// # Examples\n/// - `/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/net` → `Some(\"net\")`\n/// - `/opdbus/v1/plugins/net` → `Some(\"net\")` (legacy)\n/// - `/other/path` → `None`\npub fn extract_plugin_name(path: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let normalized = normalize_plugin_path(path)?;\n    normalized\n        .strip_prefix(PLUGIN_BASE_PATH)?\n        .trim_start_matches('/')\n        .split('/')\n        .next()\n        .map(|s| s.to_string())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_plugin_path() {\n        assert_eq!(plugin_path(\"incus\"), \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/incus\");\n        assert_eq!(\n            plugin_path(\"my-plugin\"),\n            \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/my_plugin\"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            plugin_path(\"123invalid\"),\n            \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/plugin_123invalid\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_plugin_interface() {\n        assert_eq!(\n            plugin_interface(\"incus\"),\n            \"org.opdbus.v1.Plugin.Plugins.Incus\"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            plugin_interface(\"my-plugin\"),\n            \"org.opdbus.v1.Plugin.Plugins.MyPlugin\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_plugin_schema_path() {\n        assert_eq!(plugin_schema_path(\"incus\"), \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/incus/instance-1\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_sanitize_plugin_name() {\n        assert_eq!(sanitize_plugin_name(\"incus\"), \"incus\");\n        assert_eq!(sanitize_plugin_name(\"My-Plugin\"), \"my_plugin\");\n        assert_eq!(sanitize_plugin_name(\"/incus/\"), \"incus\");\n        assert_eq!(sanitize_plugin_name(\"123test\"), normalize_plugin_path(\"/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/net\"),\n            Some(\"/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/net\".to_string())\n        );\n\n        // Legacy paths\n        assert_eq!(\n            normalize_plugin_path(\"/opdbus/v1/plugins/net\"),\n            Some(\"/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/net\".to_string())\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            normalize_plugin_path(\"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/net\"),\n            Some(\"/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/net\".to_string())\n        );\n\n        // Just plugin name\n        assert_eq!(\n            normalize_plugin_path(\"net\"),\n            Some(\"/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/net\".to_string())\n        );\n\n        // Invalid\n        assert_eq!(normalize_plugin_path(\"/other/path\"), None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_extract_plugin_name() {\n        assert_eq!(\n            extract_plugin_name(\"/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/net\"),\n            Some(\"net\".to_string())\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            extract_plugin_name(\"/opdbus/v1/plugins/net\"),\n            Some(\"net\".to_string())\n        );\n        assert_eq!(extract_plugin_name(\"/other/path\"), None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_is_canonical_plugin_path() {\n        assert!(is_canonical_plugin_path(\n            \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/net\"\n        ));\n        assert!(!is_canonical_plugin_path(\"/opdbus/v1/plugins/net\"));\n        assert!(!is_canonical_plugin_path(\"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/net\"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_constants() {\n        assert_eq!(DBUS_ROOT_PATH, \"/org/opdbus/v1\");\n        assert_eq!(PLUGIN_BASE_PATH, \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins\");\n        assert_eq!(PLUGINS_INTERFACE, \"org.opdbus.v1.Plugin.Plugins\");\n        assert_eq!(BASE_SERVICE_NAME, \"org.opdbus.v1\");\n    }\n}\n"}}

Normalize aliases first, then extract the top-level plugin name.\n        let normalized = crate::canonical::normalize_plugin_path(requested)?;\n        normalized\n plugin_name in &self.config.auto_load {\n            match self.load_plugin(plugin_name).await {\n                Ok(plugin) => {\n                    if !plugin.is_available() {\n            );\n                        continue;\n                    }\n                    tracing::info!(\"✅ Loaded plugin: {}\", plugin_name);\n                    plugins.push(plugin);\n {"timestamp":"2026-06-08T12:48:24.757Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes, with one correction: the thing that should reflect is the schema and plugin state, not the transport itself.\n\nThe intended chain is:\n- Netmaker/WireGuard establishes identity\n- the identity is stamped into The Sled\n- the schema-backed plugin object is projected under `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>`\n- gRPC and UI read that projected plugin state through reflection\n- footprints are part of the reflected state and headers, not a separate ad hoc source\n\nSo the alias fix matters because reflection should resolve both path spellings to the same canonical plugin object before UI/gRPC consume it. I’m letting the test finish now.","phase":"commentary","memory_citation":null}}

\"_\");\n                Some(format!(\"/org/opdbus/v1/registry/{}\", safe))\n            }\n            MirrorEvent::ProcMem { .. } => Some(\"/org/opdbus/v1/host/meminfo\".to_string()),\n            MirrorEvent::ProcLoad { .. } => Some(\"/org/opdbus/v1/host/loadavg\".to_string()),\n            MirrorEvent::ProcStatic { section, .. } => {\n                Some(format!(\"/org/opdbus/v1/host/{}\", section))\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get the sequence number for this event\n    pub fn sequence(&self) -> u64 {\n        match self {\n            MirrorEvent::OvsdbRow { sequence, .. }\n            | MirrorEvent::NonNet { sequence, .. }\n            | MirrorEvent::Plugin { sequence, .. }\n            | MirrorEvent::Registry { sequence, .. }\n            | MirrorEvent::ProcMem { sequence, .. }\n            | MirrorEvent::ProcLoad { sequence, .. }\n            | MirrorEvent::ProcStatic { sequence, .. } => *sequence,\n        }\n    }\n}\n"}}

pipefail\n\nCONTAINER=\"qdrant\"\nQDRANT_VERSION=\"v1.18.1\"\nQDRANT_URL=\"https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/releases/download/${QDRANT_VERSION}/qdrant-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz\"\nSTORAGE_POOL=\"default\"\n# }\n\n# ─── preflight ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n[[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die \"Run as root: sudo bash $0\"\ncommand -v incus &>/dev/null || die \"incus not found\"\n\n# Initialise Incus storage if this is a fresh system\nif ! incus storage list --format csv 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then\n    log \"Initialising Incus with default storage pool (dir backend)\"\n    incus admin init --preseed <<'PRESEED'\nconfig: {}\nnetworks: []\nstorage_pools:\n- config: {}\n  description: \"\"\n  name: default\n  driver: dir\nprofiles:\n- config: {}\n  description: \"\"\n  devices:\n    root:\n      path: /\n      pool: default\n      type: disk\n  name: default\nPRESEED\nfi\n\n# ─── download Qdrant on the host ──────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nQDRANT_TMP=$(mktemp -d)\ntrap \"rm -rf $QDRANT_TMP\" EXIT\n\nif [[ ! -f \"$QDRANT_TMP/qdrant\" ]]; then\n    log \"Downloading Qdrant ${QDRANT_VERSION} ...\"\n    curl -fL \"$QDRANT_URL\" | tar -xz -C \"$QDRANT_TMP\"\nfi\n\nlog \"Qdrant binary: $(file $QDRANT_TMP/qdrant | cut -d: -f2 | xargs)\"\n\n# ─── create container (no NIC) ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nif incus info \"$CONTAINER\" &>/dev/null; then\n    log \"Container '$CONTAINER' already exists — stopping and recreating\"\n    incus stop \"$CONTAINER\" --force 2>/dev/null || true\n    incus delete \"$CONTAINER\"\nfi\n\nlog \"Creating container '$CONTAINER' (Alpine 3.20, no NIC)\"\n\n# Launch with default profile to get storage, then strip the NIC\nincus launch images:alpine/3.20 \"$CONTAINER\" \\\n    --storage \"$STORAGE_POOL\" \\\n    --no-profiles \\\n    -d root,path=/,pool=\"$STORAGE_POOL\",size=4GiB\n\n# Give Alpine a moment to boot\nsleep 3\n\n# ─── add Unix socket proxy BEFORE removing NIC ────────────────────────────────\n# Incus proxy: host listens on /run/qdrant.sock, bridges to container TCP 6334.\n# Xray's ds outbound then proxies 127.0.0.1:$QDRANT_PORT → /run/qdrant.sock\n# via UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS=qdrant:/run/qdrant.sock:$QDRANT_PORT.\n\nSOCKET_PATH=\"/run/qdrant.sock\"\n\nincus config device add \"$CONTAINER\" qdrant proxy \\\n    listen=unix:\"$SOCKET_PATH\" \\\n    connect=tcp:127.0.0.1:6334 \\\n    bind=host\n\nlog \"Proxy device: $SOCKET_PATH -> container:6334 (xray ds outbound will use this)\"\n\n# ─── install Qdrant inside the container ──────────────────────────────────────\n\nlog \"Pushing Qdrant binary into container\"\nincus file push \"$QDRANT_TMP/qdrant\" \"$CONTAINER/usr/local/bin/qdrant\" --mode 0755\n\nlog \"Configuring Qdrant\"\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER\" -- mkdir -p /var/lib/qdrant /etc/qdrant\n\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER\" -- sh -c 'cat > /etc/qdrant/config.yaml' <<'CONF'\nstorage:\n  storage_path: /var/lib/qdrant\n\nservice:\n  host: 127.0.0.1\n  http_port: 6333\n  grpc_port: 6334\n  enable_cors: false\n\ncluster:\n  enabled: false\n\ntelemetry_disabled: true\nCONF\n\n# ─── OpenRC service ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER\" -- sh -c 'cat > /etc/init.d/qdrant' <<'INIT'\n#!/sbin/openrc-run\n\nname=\"qdrant\"\ndescription=\"Qdrant vector database\"\n\ncommand=\"/usr/local/bin/qdrant\"\ncommand_args=\"--config-path /etc/qdrant/config.yaml\"\ncommand_background=\"yes\"\npidfile=\"/run/qdrant.pid\"\noutput_log=\"/var/log/qdrant.log\"\nerror_log=\"/var/log/qdrant.log\"\n\ndepend() {\n    need localmount\n    after bootmisc\n}\nINIT\n\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER\" -- chmod +x /etc/init.d/qdrant\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER\" -- rc-update add qdrant default\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER\" -- rc-service qdrant start\n\n# ─── verify Qdrant is up inside the container ─────────────────────────────────\n\nlog \"Waiting for Qdrant to start...\"\nfor i in $(seq 1 15); do\n    if incus exec \"$CONTAINER\" -- wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:6333/healthz 2>/dev/null | grep -q ok; then\n        log \"Qdrant is healthy inside the container\"\n        break\n    fi\n    sleep 1\ndone\n\n# ─── remove NIC (container is now sealed, no network) ────────────────────────\n\nlog \"Removing container NIC (sealing network)\"\n# Alpine has eth0 added by default profile; remove any NIC devices\nfor dev in eth0 eth1 enp0 enp1; do\n    incus config device remove \"$CONTAINER\" \"$dev\" 2>/dev/null && \\\n        log \"  Removed NIC: $dev\" || true\ndone\n\n# ─── set socket permissions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n# The proxy device creates the socket as root; make it group-accessible\nSOCKET_GID=$(id -g jeremy 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\nchown root:\"$SOCKET_GID\" \"$SOCKET_PATH\" 2>/dev/null || true\nchmod 660 \"$SOCKET_PATH\" 2>/dev/null || true\n\n# ─── test connectivity from host via Unix socket ──────────────────────────────\n\nlog \"Testing gRPC health via Unix socket...\"\nif command -v grpc_health_probe &>/dev/null; then\n    grpc_health_probe -addr unix:\"$SOCKET_PATH\" && log \"gRPC health OK\" || true\nelse\n    # Fall back to socat + HTTP check\n    if command -v socat &>/dev/null; then\n        result=$(echo -e \"GET /healthz HTTP/1.0\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\n\\r\\n\" \\\n            | socat - UNIX-CONNECT:\"$SOCKET_PATH\" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 || true)\n        log \"Socket check: ${result:-no HTTP response (gRPC-only socket is normal)}\"\n    fi\nfi\n\n# ─── summary {"timestamp":"2026-06-08T13:01:54.848Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_umDwoaFC9zgUUINiYY1l0W4N","output":"Chunk ID: e457b2\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 3910\nOutput:\n//! Code-Context MCP Tools\n//!\n//! Coding-aware retrieval and indexing surfaces backed by the [`RagPipeline`]\n//! (Voyage embeddings + Qdrant) and the [`ContextAwarenessEngine`]. These are\n//! the tools an external coding client (Droid, Cursor, Codex) calls to pull\n//! repository context.\n//!\n//! Tools:\n//! - `code_search`  — filtered semantic search over indexed repos.\n//!   subid: `obs.service.code-rag.search@v1`\n//! - `code_context` — session-aware fused retrieval + awareness signals.\n//!   subid: `exp.service.code-context.render@v1`\n//! - `code_index`   — live indexing of a source file / repomix entry.\n//!   subid: `src.software.workspace.index@v1`\n\nuse crate::context_awareness::{ActivityType, ContextAwarenessEngine};\nuse crate::rag_pipeline::{CodeFilter, RagPipeline, RagResult};\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse async_trait::async_trait;\nuse op_mcp::tool_registry::{BoxedTool, Tool, ToolRegistry};\nuse simd_json::prelude::*;\nuse simd_json::{json, OwnedValue as Value};\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tracing::warn;\n\n/// Register all code-context tools against the shared registry.\n/// Returns the number of tools registered.\npub async fn register_code_tools(\n    registry: &ToolRegistry,\n    rag: Arc<RagPipeline>,\n    engine: Arc<ContextAwarenessEngine>,\n    collection: String,\n) -> Result<usize> {\n    registry\n        .register(Arc::new(CodeSearchTool {\n            rag: rag.clone(),\n            collection: collection.clone(),\n        }) as BoxedTool)\n        .await?;\n    registry\n        .register(Arc::new(CodeContextTool {\n            rag: rag.clone(),\n            engine,\n            collection: collection.clone(),\n        }) as BoxedTool)\n        .await?;\n    registry\n        .register(Arc::new(CodeIndexTool { rag, collection }) as BoxedTool)\n        .await?;\n    Ok(3)\n}\n\n// ─── code_search ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\npub struct CodeSearchTool {\n    rag: Arc<RagPipeline>,\n    collection: String,\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl Tool for CodeSearchTool {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"code_search\"\n    }\n\n    fn description(&self) -> &str {\n        \"Semantic code search over indexed repositories. Filter by repo, language, file_type, \\\n         path substring, or symbol. Returns ranked code chunks with symbols, imports, and line spans.\"\n    }\n\n    fn category(&self) -> &str {\n        \"code\"\n    }\n\n    fn tags(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        vec![\"code\".into(), \"search\".into(), \"rag\".into()]\n    }\n\n    fn input_schema(&self) -> Value {\n        tool_input_schema(\"code_search\")\n    }\n\n    async fn execute(&self, input: Value) -> Result<Value> {\n        let query = input\n            .get(\"query\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"missing query\"))?;\n        let limit = input\n            .get(\"limit\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_u64)\n            .unwrap_or(8)\n            .clamp(1, 50);\n        let filter = filter_from(&input, false);\n\n        let results = if input.get(\"fused\").and_then(Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(true) {\n            self.rag\n                .query_fused(&self.collection, query, limit, &filter)\n                .await?\n        } else {\n            self.rag\n                .query_filtered(&self.collection, query, limit, &filter)\n                .await?\n        };\n\n        Ok(json!({\n            \"count\": results.len(),\n            \"collection\": self.collection,\n            \"results\": results_to_simd(&results),\n        }))\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── code_context ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\npub struct CodeContextTool {\n    rag: Arc<RagPipeline>,\n    engine: Arc<ContextAwarenessEngine>,\n    collection: String,\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl Tool for CodeContextTool {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"code_context\"\n    }\n\n    fn description(&self) -> &str {\n        \"Session-aware coding context. Records the current activity (query, edit, build_error, \\\n         test_failure, etc.) into the awareness engine, runs fused retrieval, and returns relevant \\\n         code plus session signals (stuck, recent errors, topics).\"\n    }\n\n    fn category(&self) -> &str {\n        \"code\"\n    }\n\n    fn tags(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        vec![\"code\".into(), \"context\".into(), \"session\".into()]\n    }\n\n    fn input_schema(&self) -> Value {\n        tool_input_schema(\"code_context\")\n    }\n\n    async fn execute(&self, input: Value) -> Result<Value> {\n        let query = input\n            .get(\"query\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"missing query\"))?;\n        let session_id = input\n            .get(\"session_id\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .unwrap_or(\"default\");\n        let activity_type = input\n            .get(\"activity_type\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .map(ActivityType::parse)\n            .unwrap_or(ActivityType::Query);\n        let limit = input\n            .get(\"limit\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_u64)\n            .unwrap_or(6)\n            .clamp(1, 50);\n\n        // Record the activity so stuck/error/topic detection stays current.\n        self.engine\n            .record_activity(\n                session_id,\n                activity_type,\n                query.to_string(),\n                serde_json::json!({ \"source\": \"code_context\" }),\n            )\n            .await;\n\n        let filter = filter_from(&input, false);\n        let (results, retrieval_error) = match self\n            .rag\n            .query_fused(&self.collection, query, limit, &filter)\n            .await\n        {\n            Ok(results) => (results, None),\n            Err(err) => {\n                warn!(\n                    error = %err,\n                    \"Code-context vector retrieval unavailable; returning awareness signals only\"\n                );\n                (Vec::new(), Some(err.to_string()))\n            }\n        };\n\n        let signals = self\n            .engine\n            .get_session_signals(session_id)\n            .await\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| serde_json::json!({ \"session_id\": session_id }));\n\n        Ok(json!({\n            \"count\": results.len(),\n            \"session_id\": session_id,\n            \"signals\": serde_to_simd(&signals),\n            \"results\": results_to_simd(&results),\n            \"retrieval_error\": retrieval_error,\n        }))\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── code_index ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\npub struct CodeIndexTool {\n    rag: Arc<RagPipeline>,\n    collection: String,\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl Tool for CodeIndexTool {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"code_index\"\n    }\n\n    fn description(&self) -> &str {\n        \"Index code into the semantic store. mode='source' indexes a single in-memory file \\\n         (repo, file_path, content) for live workspace updates; mode='repomix_zip' ingests an \\\n         entry from a repomix zip (zip_path, entry).\"\n    }\n\n    fn category(&self) -> &str {\n        \"code\"\n    }\n\n    fn tags(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        vec![\"code\".into(), \"index\".into(), \"ingest\".into()]\n    }\n\n    fn input_schema(&self) -> Value {\n        tool_input_schema(\"code_index\")\n    }\n\n    async fn execute(&self, input: Value) -> Result<Value> {\n        let collection = input\n            .get(\"collection\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .unwrap_or(&self.collection);\n        let mode = input\n            .get(\"mode\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .unwrap_or(\"source\");\n\n        let stats = match mode {\n            \"source\" => {\n                let repo = input\n                    .get(\"repo\")\n                    .and_then(Value::as_str)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"source mode requires 'repo'\"))?;\n                let file_path = input\n                    .get(\"file_path\")\n                    .and_then(Value::as_str)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"source mode requires 'file_path'\"))?;\n                let content = input\n                    .get(\"content\")\n\n---CTX---\n//! Context-Aware HTTP Server with Proactive SSE Pushes\n//!\n//! Extended HTTP server that adds:\n//! - `/context/stream` - SSE endpoint for proactive knowledge pushes\n//! - `/context/status/:session_id` - Get session context status\n//! - `/context/request_push` - On-demand knowledge push\n//!\n//! Integrates with the ContextAwarenessEngine to provide real-time\n//! context-aware assistance to connected clients.\n\nuse crate::context_awareness::{\n    ActivityEvent, ActivityType, ContextAwarenessConfig, ContextAwarenessEngine,\n};\nuse crate::memory_store::CognitiveMemoryStore;\nuse crate::rag_pipeline::RagPipeline;\nuse crate::session::SessionManager;\nuse axum::{\n    extract::{Path, State},\n    response::sse::{Event, Sse},\n    routing::{get, post},\n    Json, Router,\n};\nuse serde::Deserialize;\nuse std::convert::Infallible;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::time::Duration;\nuse tracing::{debug, info, warn};\n\n/// Server state shared across request handlers\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct ContextServerState {\n    /// Context awareness engine\n    pub context_engine: Arc<ContextAwarenessEngine>,\n    /// Activity event sender\n    pub activity_tx: tokio::sync::mpsc::Sender<ActivityEvent>,\n    /// Memory store reference\n    pub memory_store: Arc<CognitiveMemoryStore>,\n    /// Session manager reference\n    pub session_manager: Arc<SessionManager>,\n}\n\n/// Create a context-aware server with proactive SSE pushes.\n/// **Deprecated in favour of [`build_context_router`]**: this function\n/// instantiates its own `ContextAwarenessEngine`.  In the main server the\n/// engine is already created in `CognitiveMcpServer::new`, so use\n/// `build_context_router` to avoid duplicate engines.\npub async fn create_context_aware_server(\n    memory_store: Arc<CognitiveMemoryStore>,\n    session_manager: Arc<SessionManager>,\n    rag_pipeline: Option<Arc<RagPipeline>>,\n) -> anyhow::Result<(Router, Arc<ContextAwarenessEngine>)> {\n    let config = ContextAwarenessConfig::default();\n    let engine = Arc::new(ContextAwarenessEngine::new(\n        config,\n        memory_store.clone(),\n        rag_pipeline,\n    ));\n\n    let router = build_context_router(engine.clone(), memory_store, session_manager);\n\n    // Start background monitoring\n    let engine_clone = engine.clone();\n    tokio::spawn(async move {\n        engine_clone.start_monitoring();\n    });\n\n    Ok((router, engine))\n}\n\n/// Build an Axum router for the context-awareness endpoints using an\n/// *existing* `ContextAwarenessEngine`.\n///\n/// Call this from `CognitiveMcpServer::start_http_server` so the engine\n/// created in `CognitiveMcpServer::new` is reused rather than duplicated.\npub fn build_context_router(\n    engine: Arc<ContextAwarenessEngine>,\n    memory_store: Arc<CognitiveMemoryStore>,\n    session_manager: Arc<SessionManager>,\n) -> Router {\n    let activity_tx = engine.activity_sender();\n\n    let state = ContextServerState {\n        context_engine: engine,\n        activity_tx,\n        memory_store,\n        session_manager,\n    };\n\n    let router = Router::new()\n        .route(\"/stream/:session_id\", get(sse_push_stream))\n        .route(\"/status/:session_id\", get(get_session_status))\n        .route(\"/record\", post(record_activity))\n        .route(\"/request_push\", post(request_knowledge_push))\n        .route(\"/health\", get(context_health))\n        .with_state(state);\n\n    info!(\"Context-aware server endpoints registered\");\n    router\n}\n\n/// SSE stream handler for proactive knowledge pushes\nasync fn sse_push_stream(\n    State(state): State<ContextServerState>,\n    Path(session_id): Path<String>,\n) -> Sse<impl tokio_stream::Stream<Item = Result<Event, Infallible>>> {\n    info!(session_id = %session_id, \"Client subscribed to context push stream\");\n\n    // Record the subscription activity\n    let _ = state\n        .activity_tx\n        .send(ActivityEvent {\n            session_id: session_id.clone(),\n            activity_type: ActivityType::ToolCall,\n            content: \"Subscribed to context push stream\".to_string(),\n            metadata: serde_json::json!({ \"endpoint\": \"/context/stream\" }),\n        })\n        .await;\n\n    // Subscribe to push notifications\n    let mut push_rx = state.context_engine.subscribe_pushes();\n\n    // Create filtered stream for this session only\n    let stream = async_stream::stream! {\n        // Send initial connection event\n        yield Ok(Event::default()\n            .event(\"connected\")\n            .data(serde_json::json!({\n                \"session_id\": &session_id,\n                \"message\": \"Connected to context push stream\",\n                \"timestamp\": chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339()\n            }).to_string()));\n\n        // Forward relevant pushes to this client\n        while let Ok(push) = push_rx.recv().await {\n            if push.session_id == session_id {\n                let event = Event::default()\n                    .event(\"knowledge_push\")\n                    .id(&push.id)\n                    .data(serde_json::to_string(&push).unwrap_or_default());\n\n                yield Ok(event);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stream ended\n        yield Ok(Event::default()\n            .event(\"disconnected\")\n            .data(serde_json::json!({\n                \"session_id\": &session_id,\n                \"message\": \"Context stream ended\",\n                \"timestamp\": chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339()\n            }).to_string()));\n    };\n\n    Sse::new(stream).keep_alive(\n        axum::response::sse::KeepAlive::new()\n            .interval(Duration::from_secs(30))\n            .text(\"keep-alive\"),\n    )\n}\n\n/// Get session context status\nasync fn get_session_status(\n    State(state): State<ContextServerState>,\n    Path(session_id): Path<String>,\n) -> Json<serde_json::Value> {\n    debug!(session_id = %session_id, \"Getting session context status\");\n\n    let stats = state\n        .context_engine\n        .get_session_stats(&session_id)\n        .await\n        .unwrap_or(serde_json::json!({ \"error\": \"Session not found\" }));\n\n    Json(stats)\n}\n\n/// Request on-demand knowledge push\n#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]\nstruct RequestPushInput {\n    session_id: String,\n    query: String,\n    context: Option<serde_json::Value>,\n}\n\nasync fn request_knowledge_push(\n    State(state): State<ContextServerState>,\n    Json(input): Json<RequestPushInput>,\n) -> Json<serde_json::Value> {\n    info!(\n        session_id = %input.session_id,\n        query = %input.query,\n        \"On-demand knowledge push requested\"\n    );\n\n    // Record the request activity\n    let _ = state\n        .activity_tx\n        .send(ActivityEvent {\n            session_id: input.session_id.clone(),\n            activity_type: ActivityType::Query,\n            content: input.query.clone(),\n            metadata: input.context.clone().unwrap_or(serde_json::json!({})),\n        })\n        .await;\n\n    // Generate and send the push\n    match state\n        .context_engine\n        .request_push(&input.session_id, &input.query)\n        .await\n    {\n        Ok(push) => Json(serde_json::json!({\n            \"success\": true,\n            \"push\": push,\n            \"message\": \"Knowledge push generated and sent via SSE stream\"\n        })),\n        Err(e) => {\n            warn!(error = %e, \"Failed to generate on-demand push\");\n            Json(serde_json::json!({\n"}}

 }\n            Err(e) => {\n                warn!(error = %e, \"SSE error\");\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nasync fn handle_sse_event(event_type: &str, data: &str) {\n    match event_type {\n        \"connected\" => {\n            info!(\"✅ Connected to context push stream\");\n        }\n        \"knowledge_push\" => {\n            match serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(data) {\n                Ok(push) => {\n                    let trigger = push\n                        .get(\"trigger\")\n                        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                        .unwrap_or(\"unknown\");\n                    let relevance = push\n                        .get(\"relevance_score\")\n                        .and_then(|v| v.as_f64())\n                        .unwrap_or(0.0);\n                    let reason = push\n                        .get(\"trigger_reason\")\n                        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                        .unwrap_or(\"\");\n\n                    info!(\n                        trigger = trigger,\n                        relevance = relevance,\n                        \"🧠 PROACTIVE KNOWLEDGE PUSH RECEIVED\"\n                    );\n                    info!(reason = reason, \"   Reason\");\n\n                    // Display content based on type\n                    if let Some(content) = push.get(\"content\") {\n                        match content.get(\"type\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n                            Some(\"rag_results\") => {\n                                if let Some(results) = content.get(\"results\") {\n                                    info!(results = %results, \"   RAG Results\");\n                                }\n                            }\n                            Some(\"memory_entries\") => {\n                                if let Some(namespace) = content.get(\"namespace\") {\n                                    info!(namespace = %namespace, \"   Memory Namespace\");\n                                }\n                            }\n                            Some(\"error_assistance\") => {\n                                if let Some(steps) = content.get(\"resolution_steps\") {\n                                    info!(steps = %steps, \"   Resolution Steps\");\n                                }\n                            }\n                            _ => {\n                                info!(content = %content, \"   Content\");\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n\n                    if let Some(action) = push.get(\"suggested_action\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n                        info!(action = action, \"   Suggested Action\");\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    warn!(error = %e, data = data, \"Failed to parse knowledge push\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        \"disconnected\" => {\n            info!(\"⚠️  SSE stream disconnected\");\n        }\n        _ => {\n            tracing::debug!(event_type = event_type, data = data, \"SSE event\");\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn simulate_activities(client: &Client, cli: &Cli) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let base_url = COGNITIVE_MCP_URL;\n\n    info!(\"Starting activity simulation...\");\n\n    // Record initial session start\n    record_activity(\n        client,\n        base_url,\n        &cli.session_id,\n        \"tool_call\",\n        \"Session started - exploring cognitive-mcp features\",\n        json!({ \"demo\": true }),\n    )\n    .await?;\n\n    info!(\"Activity 1: Tool call recorded\");\n    sleep(Duration::from_secs(2)).await;\n\n    // Simulate queries with different topics (to trigger new_topic detection)\n    let topics = [\n        \"How does database connection pooling work?\",\n        \"Configure PostgreSQL with connection limits\",\n        \"What are the best practices for async database access?\",\n        \"React component state management patterns\",\n        \"Implementing React hooks with TypeScript\",\n        \"Frontend performance optimization techniques\",\n    ];\n\n    for (i, query) in topics.iter().enumerate() {\n        record_activity(\n            client,\n            base_url,\n            &cli.session_id,\n            \"query\",\n            query,\n            json!({ \"sequence\": i + 1 }),\n        )\n        .await?;\n\n        info!(query = query, \"Activity: Query recorded\");\n\n        // Wait between queries\n        sleep(Duration::from_secs(3)).await;\n    }\n\n    // Simulate stuck session if requested\n    if cli.simulate_stuck {\n        info!(\"Simulating stuck session pattern (repeated similar queries)...\");\n\n        for i in 0..4 {\n            record_activity(\n                client,\n                base_url,\n                &cli.session_id,\n                \"query\",\n                \"How to fix the database connection error\", // Repeated query\n                json!({ \"stuck_simulation\": true, \"attempt\": i }),\n            )\n            .await?;\n\n            sleep(Duration::from_secs(2)).await;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Simulate errors if requested\n    if cli.simulate_errors {\n        info!(\"Simulating error pattern...\");\n\n        for i in 0..3 {\n            record_activity(\n                client,\n                base_url,\n                &cli.session_id,\n                \"error\",\n                \"Database connection timeout\",\n                json!({\n                    \"error_type\": \"timeout\",\n                    \"error_simulation\": true,\n                    \"attempt\": i\n                }),\n            )\n            .await?;\n\n            sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)).await;\n        }\n    }\n"}}
