{"timestamp":"2026-06-08T13:02:39.764Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"A concrete example is the `code_context` path.\n\nA client sends:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"session_id\": \"debug-001\",\n  \"activity_type\": \"query\",\n  \"query\": \"Why was cognitive-mcp missing qdrant context?\",\n  \"limit\": 3\n}\n```\n\nWhat the server does, from [`code_tools.rs`](crates/op-cognitive-mcp/src/code_tools.rs:114):\n- records the activity into the awareness engine\n- runs fused retrieval against Qdrant\n- returns both code results and session signals\n\nThe shape of the response is:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"count\": 3,\n  \"session_id\": \"debug-001\",\n  \"signals\": {\n    \"stuck\": false,\n    \"recent_error_count\": 0,\n    \"active_topics\": [\"qdrant\", \"context\", \"identity\"]\n  },\n  \"results\": [\n    { \"path\": \"crates/op-cognitive-mcp/src/qdrant_shuttle.rs\", \"...\" : \"...\" },\n    { \"path\": \"deploy/setup-qdrant-incus.sh\", \"...\" : \"...\" },\n    { \"path\": \"crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/knowledge_plugin.rs\", \"...\" : \"...\" }\n  ],\n  \"retrieval_error\": null\n}\n```\n\nThe SSE version of the same idea is in [`context_aware_client.rs`](crates/op-cognitive-mcp/examples/context_aware_client.rs:1): it subscribes to `/context/stream/:session_id`, records repeated queries or errors, and the server can push a `knowledge_push` event when it detects a stuck loop or a new topic.\n\nRight now the important part is that qdrant is healthy again and `op-cognitive-mcp` is pointed at the live rescue endpoint, so the retrieval side is no longer the blocker.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-08T13:02:39.765Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"A concrete example is the `code_context` path.\n\nA client sends:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"session_id\": \"debug-001\",\n  \"activity_type\": \"query\",\n  \"query\": \"Why was cognitive-mcp missing qdrant context?\",\n  \"limit\": 3\n}\n```\n\nWhat the server does, from [`code_tools.rs`](crates/op-cognitive-mcp/src/code_tools.rs:114):\n- records the activity into the awareness engine\n- runs fused retrieval against Qdrant\n- returns both code results and session signals\n\nThe shape of the response is:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"count\": 3,\n  \"session_id\": \"debug-001\",\n  \"signals\": {\n    \"stuck\": false,\n    \"recent_error_count\": 0,\n    \"active_topics\": [\"qdrant\", \"context\", \"identity\"]\n  },\n  \"results\": [\n    { \"path\": \"crates/op-cognitive-mcp/src/qdrant_shuttle.rs\", \"...\" : \"...\" },\n    { \"path\": \"deploy/setup-qdrant-incus.sh\", \"...\" : \"...\" },\n    { \"path\": \"crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/knowledge_plugin.rs\", \"...\" : \"...\" }\n  ],\n  \"retrieval_error\": null\n}\n```\n\nThe SSE version of the same idea is in [`context_aware_client.rs`](crates/op-cognitive-mcp/examples/context_aware_client.rs:1): it subscribes to `/context/stream/:session_id`, records repeated queries or errors, and the server can push a `knowledge_push` event when it detects a stuck loop or a new topic.\n\nRight now the important part is that qdrant is healthy again and `op-cognitive-mcp` is pointed at the live rescue endpoint, so the retrieval side is no longer the blocker."}],"phase":"final_answer"}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. Apps can also be implicitly triggered as long as the context suggests usage of available apps.\nAn app is equivalent to a set of MCP tools within the `codex_apps` MCP.\nAn installed app's MCP tools are either provided to you already, or can be lazy-loaded through the `tool_search` tool. {"timestamp":"2026-06-09T03:04:02.600Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-08</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

    }\n                })\n                .or_insert(r);\n        }\n\n        let mut results: Vec<RagResult> = best.into_values().collect();\n        results.sort_by(|a, b| {\n            b.score\n Tools:\n//! - `code_search`  — filtered semantic search over indexed repos.\n//!   subid: `obs.service.code-rag.search@v1`\n//! - `code_context` — session-aware fused retrieval + awareness signals.\n//!   subid: `exp.service.code-context.render@v1`\n//! - `code_index`   — live indexing of a source file / repomix entry.\n//!   subid: `src.software.workspace.index@v1`\n\nuse crate::context_awareness::{ActivityType, ContextAwarenessEngine};\nuse crate::rag_pipeline::{CodeFilter, RagPipeline, RagResult};\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse async_trait::async_trait;\nuse op_mcp::tool_registry::{BoxedTool, Tool, ToolRegistry};\nuse simd_json::prelude::*;\nuse simd_json::{json, OwnedValue as Value};\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tracing::warn;\n\n/// Register all code-context tools against the shared registry.\n/// Returns the number of tools registered.\npub async fn register_code_tools(\n    registry: &ToolRegistry,\n    rag: Arc<RagPipeline>,\n    engine: Arc<ContextAwarenessEngine>,\n    collection: String,\n) -> Result<usize> {\n    registry\n        .register(Arc::new(CodeSearchTool {\n            rag: rag.clone(),\n            collection: collection.clone(),\n        }) as BoxedTool)\n        .await?;\n    registry\n        .register(Arc::new(CodeContextTool {\n            rag: rag.clone(),\n            engine,\n            collection: collection.clone(),\n        }) as BoxedTool)\n        .await?;\n    registry\n        .register(Arc::new(CodeIndexTool { rag, collection }) as BoxedTool)\n        .await?;\n    Ok(3)\n}\n\n// ─── code_search ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\npub struct CodeSearchTool {\n    rag: Arc<RagPipeline>,\n    collection: String,\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl Tool for CodeSearchTool {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"code_search\"\n    }\n\n    fn description(&self) -> &str {\n        \"Semantic code search over indexed repositories. Filter by repo, language, file_type, \\\n         path substring, or symbol. Returns ranked code chunks with symbols, imports, and line spans.\"\n    }\n\n    fn category(&self) -> &str {\n        \"code\"\n    }\n\n    fn tags(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        vec![\"code\".into(), \"search\".into(), \"rag\".into()]\n    }\n\n    fn input_schema(&self) -> Value {\n        tool_input_schema(\"code_search\")\n    }\n\n    async fn execute(&self, input: Value) -> Result<Value> {\n        let query = input\n            .get(\"query\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"missing query\"))?;\n        let limit = input\n            .get(\"limit\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_u64)\n            .unwrap_or(8)\n            .clamp(1, 50);\n        let filter = filter_from(&input, false);\n\n        let results = if input.get(\"fused\").and_then(Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(true) {\n            self.rag\n                .query_fused(&self.collection, query, limit, &filter)\n                .await?\n        } else {\n            self.rag\n                .query_filtered(&self.collection, query, limit, &filter)\n                .await?\n        };\n\n        Ok(json!({\n            \"count\": results.len(),\n            \"collection\": self.collection,\n            \"results\": results_to_simd(&results),\n        }))\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── code_context ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\npub struct CodeContextTool {\n    rag: Arc<RagPipeline>,\n    engine: Arc<ContextAwarenessEngine>,\n    collection: String,\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl Tool for CodeContextTool {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"code_context\"\n    }\n\n    fn description(&self) -> &str {\n        \"Session-aware coding context. Records the current activity (query, edit, build_error, \\\n         test_failure, etc.) into the awareness engine, runs fused retrieval, and returns relevant \\\n         code plus session signals (stuck, recent errors, topics).\"\n    }\n\n    fn category(&self) -> &str {\n        \"code\"\n    }\n\n    fn tags(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        vec![\"code\".into(), \"context\".into(), \"session\".into()]\n    }\n\n    fn input_schema(&self) -> Value {\n        tool_input_schema(\"code_context\")\n    }\n\n    async fn execute(&self, input: Value) -> Result<Value> {\n        let query = input\n            .get(\"query\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"missing query\"))?;\n        let session_id = input\n            .get(\"session_id\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .unwrap_or(\"default\");\n        let activity_type = input\n            .get(\"activity_type\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .map(ActivityType::parse)\n            .unwrap_or(ActivityType::Query);\n        let limit = input\n            .get(\"limit\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_u64)\n            .unwrap_or(6)\n            .clamp(1, 50);\n\n        // Record the activity so stuck/error/topic detection stays current.\n        self.engine\n            .record_activity(\n                session_id,\n                activity_type,\n                query.to_string(),\n                serde_json::json!({ \"source\": \"code_context\" }),\n            )\n            .await;\n\n        let filter = filter_from(&input, false);\n        let (results, retrieval_error) = match self\n            .rag\n            .query_fused(&self.collection, query, limit, &filter)\n            .await\n        {\n            Ok(results) => (results, None),\n            Err(err) => {\n                warn!(\n                    error = %err,\n                    \"Code-context vector retrieval unavailable; returning awareness signals only\"\n                );\n                (Vec::new(), Some(err.to_string()))\n            }\n        };\n\n        let signals = self\n            .engine\n            .get_session_signals(session_id)\n            .await\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| serde_json::json!({ \"session_id\": session_id }));\n\n        Ok(json!({\n            \"count\": results.len(),\n            \"session_id\": session_id,\n            \"signals\": serde_to_simd(&signals),\n            \"results\": results_to_simd(&results),\n            \"retrieval_error\": retrieval_error,\n        }))\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── code_index ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\npub struct CodeIndexTool {\n    rag: Arc<RagPipeline>,\n    collection: String,\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl Tool for CodeIndexTool {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"code_index\"\n    }\n\n    fn description(&self) -> &str {\n        \"Index code into the semantic store. mode='source' indexes a single in-memory file \\\n         (repo, file_path, content) for live workspace updates; mode='repomix_zip' ingests an \\\n         entry from a repomix zip (zip_path, entry).\"\n    }\n\n    fn category(&self) -> &str {\n        \"code\"\n    }\n\n    fn tags(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        vec![\"code\".into(), \"index\".into(), \"ingest\".into()]\n    }\n\n    fn input_schema(&self) -> Value {\n        tool_input_schema(\"code_index\")\n    }\n\n    async fn execute(&self, input: Value) -> Result<Value> {\n        let collection = input\n            .get(\"collection\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .unwrap_or(&self.collection);\n        let mode = input\n            .get(\"mode\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .unwrap_or(\"source\");\n\n        let stats = match mode {\n            \"source\" => {\n                let repo = input\n                    .get(\"repo\")\n                    .and_then(Value::as_str)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"source mode requires 'repo'\"))?;\n                let file_path = input\n                    .get(\"file_path\")\n                    .and_then(Value::as_str)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"source mode requires 'file_path'\"))?;\n                let content = input\n                    .get(\"content\")\n                    .and_then(Value::as_str)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"source mode requires 'content'\"))?;\n                self.rag\n                    .ingest_source_text(repo, file_path, content, collection)\n                    .await?\n            }\n            \"repomix_zip\" => {\n                let zip_path = input\n                    .get(\"zip_path\")\n                    .and_then(Value::as_str)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"repomix_zip mode requires 'zip_path'\"))?;\n                let entry = input\n                    .get(\"entry\")\n                    .and_then(Value::as_str)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"repomix_zip mode requires 'entry'\"))?;\n                self.rag\n                    .ingest_repomix_entry(&PathBuf::from(zip_path), entry, collection)\n                    .await?\n            }\n            other => return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"unknown mode: {other}\")),\n        };\n\n        Ok(json!({\n            \"ok\": true,\n            \"mode\": mode,\n            \"collection\": collection,\n            \"files_parsed\": stats.files_parsed as u64,\n            \"chunks_created\": stats.chunks_created as u64,\n            \"chunks_upserted\": stats.chunks_upserted as u64,\n            \"chunks_skipped\": stats.chunks_skipped as u64,\n            \"errors\": stats.errors as u64,\n        }))\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Derive a tool's JSON input schema from the single canonical authority\n/// (`op_plugins::cognitive_mcp_plugin_schema`). The tool never declares its\n/// schema inline — the OSCAL subid and field contract live in the PluginSchema.\nfn tool_input_schema(field: &str) -> Value {\n    op_plugins::cognitive_mcp_plugin_schema()\n        .field_input_schema(field)\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| json!({ \"type\": \"object\", \"properties\": {} }))\n}\n\nfn filter_from(input: &Value, default_exclude_tests: bool) -> CodeFilter {\n    CodeFilter {\n        repo: input.get(\"repo\").and_then(Value::as_str).map(String::from),\n        language: input\n            .get(\"language\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .map(String::from),\n        file_type: input\n            .get(\"file_type\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .map(String::from),\n        path_contains: input\n            .get(\"path_contains\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .map(String::from),\n        symbol_contains: input\n            .get(\"symbol_contains\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .map(String::from),\n        exclude_tests: input\n            .get(\"exclude_tests\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_bool)\n            .unwrap_or(default_exclude_tests),\n    }\n}\n\nfn results_to_simd(results: &[RagResult]) -> Value {\n    let serde_val = serde_json::to_value(results).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null);\n    serde_to_simd(&serde_val)\n}\n\nfn serde_to_simd(v: &serde_json::Value) -> Value {\n    let s = serde_json::to_string(v).unwrap_or_default();\n    let mut buf = s.into_bytes();\n    simd_json::from_slice(&mut buf).unwrap_or(Value::Static(simd_json::StaticNode::Null))\n}\n"}}

      \"java\" => \"java\",\n        \"kt\" => \"kotlin\",\n        \"nix\" => \"nix\",\n        _ => \"text\",\n    }\n}\n\nfn classify_file(path: &str, lines: &[String]) -> FileType {\n    let lower = path.to_lowercase();\n    if lower.contains(\"test\") || lower.contains(\"spec\") || lower.ends_with(\"_test.rs\") {\n        return FileType::Test;\n    }\n    if lower.ends_with(\"cargo.toml\")\n        || lower.ends_with(\"package.json\")\n        || lower.ends_with(\"pyproject.toml\")\n        || lower.ends_with(\"go.mod\")\n        || lower.ends_with(\"build.rs\")\n        || lower.ends_with(\"makefile\")\n    {\n        return FileType::Build;\n    }\n    if lower.ends_with(\".md\") || lower.ends_with(\".rst\") || lower.ends_with(\".txt\") {\n        return FileType::Docs;\n    }\n    if lower.ends_with(\".toml\")\n        || lower.ends_with(\".yaml\")\n        || lower.ends_with(\".yml\")\n        || lower.ends_with(\".json\")\n        || lower.ends_with(\".env\")\n    {\n        return FileType::Config;\n    }\n    if lines\n        .iter()\n        .any(|l| l.contains(\"#[cfg(test)]\") || l.contains(\"#[test]\"))\n    {\n        return FileType::Test;\n    }\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-09T03:16:20.162Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_qX701jKKWjETt9bhH2xsRA5A","output":"Chunk ID: 95f108\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1709\nOutput:\n#!/bin/bash\n# Fix mail-3tched container: remove all NICs, seal network, add Unix socket\n# mounts for Xray / OpenFlow routing only.\n#\n# mail-3tched has NO IP address. All traffic flows via Unix sockets proxied\n# through Xray's ds outbound (domain socket transport).\n#\n# Usage: sudo bash deploy/fix-mail-3tched-network.sh\nset -euo pipefail\n\nCONTAINER=\"mail-3tched\"\n\nlog() { echo \"[mail-fix] $*\"; }\ndie() { echo \"[mail-fix] ERROR: $*\" >&2; exit 1; }\n\n[[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die \"Run as root: sudo bash $0\"\ncommand -v incus &>/dev/null || die \"incus not found\"\n\n# ─── ensure container exists ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nif ! incus info \"$CONTAINER\" &>/dev/null; then\n    die \"Container '$CONTAINER' does not exist\"\nfi\n\n# ─── stop container ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nlog \"Stopping $CONTAINER\"\nincus stop \"$CONTAINER\" --force 2>/dev/null || true\n\n# ─── remove ALL NIC devices ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nlog \"Removing all network interfaces from $CONTAINER\"\nfor dev in $(incus config device list \"$CONTAINER\" 2>/dev/null | grep -E \"^eth|^enp\" || true); do\n    log \"  Removing NIC device: $dev\"\n    incus config device remove \"$CONTAINER\" \"$dev\" 2>/dev/null || true\ndone\n\n# Also remove any bridged/physical NICs that might have different names\nfor dev in $(incus config device list \"$CONTAINER\" 2>/dev/null); do\n    type=$(incus config device get \"$CONTAINER\" \"$dev\" type 2>/dev/null || echo \"\")\n    if [[ \"$type\" == \"nic\" ]]; then\n        log \"  Removing NIC device: $dev (type=nic)\"\n        incus config device remove \"$CONTAINER\" \"$dev\" 2>/dev/null || true\n    fi\ndone\n\n# Remove from default profile if it adds a NIC (it shouldn't, but be safe)\nif incus profile show default | grep -q \"type: nic\" 2>/dev/null; then\n    log \"WARNING: default profile contains a NIC — mail-3tched should use a profile without NIC\"\nfi\n\n# ─── verify no IPs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nlog \"Verifying container has no network interfaces with IP addresses\"\nincus start \"$CONTAINER\" 2>/dev/null || true\nsleep 2\n\nip_count=$(incus exec \"$CONTAINER\" -- ip -4 addr show 2>/dev/null | grep -c \"inet \" || echo \"0\")\nif [[ \"$ip_count\" -gt 1 ]]; then\n    # >1 because lo always has 127.0.0.1\n    log \"WARNING: container still has $((ip_count - 1)) non-loopback IP(s):\"\n    incus exec \"$CONTAINER\" -- ip -4 addr show | grep -v \"127.0.0.1\" || true\nelse\n    log \"Container sealed — only loopback present\"\nfi\n\n# ─── add D-Bus session bus mount (for control plane) ──────────────────────────\n\nlog \"Adding D-Bus session bus mount\"\nincus config device remove \"$CONTAINER\" host-op-dbus-session 2>/dev/null || true\nincus config device add \"$CONTAINER\" host-op-dbus-session disk \\\n    source=/run/op-dbus/session-bus.sock \\\n    path=/run/host-op-dbus/session-bus.sock\n\n# ─── add Unix socket proxies for mail services ──────────────────────────────\n#\n# Xray ds outbound routes host Unix sockets → container TCP ports.\n# OpenFlow rules on the host steer traffic to these sockets.\n\n# SMTP submission socket (Postfix/Maddy inside container listens on 127.0.0.1:587)\nSMTP_SOCKET=\"/run/mail-3tched/smtp.sock\"\nmkdir -p \"$(dirname \"$SMTP_SOCKET\")\"\nincus config device remove \"$CONTAINER\" mail-smtp 2>/dev/null || true\nincus config device add \"$CONTAINER\" mail-smtp proxy \\\n    listen=unix:\"$SMTP_SOCKET\" \\\n    connect=tcp:127.0.0.1:587 \\\n    bind=host \\\n    mode=0660 \\\n    gid=\"$(id -g)\"\nlog \"SMTP Unix socket: $SMTP_SOCKET → container:587\"\n\n# IMAP socket (Dovecot/Maddy inside container listens on 127.0.0.1:143)\nIMAP_SOCKET=\"/run/mail-3tched/imap.sock\"\nincus config device remove \"$CONTAINER\" mail-imap 2>/dev/null || true\nincus config device add \"$CONTAINER\" mail-imap proxy \\\n    listen=unix:\"$IMAP_SOCKET\" \\\n    connect=tcp:127.0.0.1:143 \\\n    bind=host \\\n    mode=0660 \\\n    gid=\"$(id -g)\"\nlog \"IMAP Unix socket: $IMAP_SOCKET → container:143\"\n\n# IMAPS socket (TLS wrapper inside container listens on 127.0.0.1:993)\nIMAPS_SOCKET=\"/run/mail-3tched/imaps.sock\"\nincus config device remove \"$CONTAINER\" mail-imaps 2>/dev/null || true\nincus config device add \"$CONTAINER\" mail-imaps proxy \\\n    listen=unix:\"$IMAPS_SOCKET\" \\\n    connect=tcp:127.0.0.1:993 \\\n    bind=host \\\n    mode=0660 \\\n    gid=\"$(id -g)\"\nlog \"IMAPS Unix socket: $IMAPS_SOCKET → container:993\"\n\n# ─── restart container ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nlog \"Restarting $CONTAINER\"\nincus restart \"$CONTAINER\" --force 2>/dev/null || incus start \"$CONTAINER\"\n\n# ─── summary \"══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\"\necho \" Container:      $CONTAINER\"\necho \" NICs:           NONE (no IP addresses)\"\necho \" Routing:        Xray ds outbound + OpenFlow via Unix sockets\"\necho \"\"\necho \" Unix sockets (host → container TCP):\"\necho \"   $SMTP_SOCKET  → 127.0.0.1:587  (SMTP submission)\"\necho \"   $IMAP_SOCKET  → 127.0.0.1:143  (IMAP)\"\necho \"   $IMAPS_SOCKET → 127.0.0.1:993  (IMAPS)\"\necho \"\"\necho \" Xray routing (add to xray config):\"\necho \"   UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS=mail-smtp:$SMTP_SOCKET:587\"\necho \" {"timestamp":"2026-06-09T03:16:20.170Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_5VApAhnbwsuxLIb6dhYxhJNB","output":"Chunk ID: aa8190\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1015\nOutput:\n# Mail Server Setup for 3tched.com\n\nSimple mail server using Maddy (SMTP/IMAP) + SnappyMail (webmail) in an Incus container.\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ op-web (operation-dbus)                 │\n│ └─> lettre → Maddy SMTP :587            │ Magic link emails\n├─────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Incus Container: mail-3tched            │\n│ ├─> Maddy                                │\n│ │   ├─> SMTP :25 (receive from internet)│\n│ │   ├─> SMTP :587 (submit from clients) │\n│ │   └─> IMAP :143 (mailbox access)      │\n│ └─> SnappyMail (webmail)                │\n│     └─> Caddy :80 → PHP-FPM              │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n## Quick Start\n\n1. **Run the setup script:**\n   ```bash\n   cd /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus\n   chmod +x scripts/setup-mail-server.sh\n   ./scripts/setup-mail-server.sh\n   ```\n\n2. **Set passwords for mail users:**\n   ```bash\n   incus exec mail-3tched -- maddyctl creds create jeremy@3tched.com\n   incus exec mail-3tched -- maddyctl creds create admin@3tched.com\n   ```\n\n3. **Get DKIM record for DNS:**\n   ```bash\n   incus exec mail-3tched -- maddyctl dkim show default 3tched.com\n   ```\n\n4. **Configure DNS** (see `scripts/dns-records-3tched.txt`)\n\n5. **Access webmail:**\n   - Get container IP: `incus list mail-3tched`\n   - Open: `http://<container-ip>`\n\n## Mailboxes\n\n- **jeremy@3tched.com** - Primary mailbox\n- **admin@3tched.com** - Administrative mailbox\n\n## Updating op-web to Use Maddy\n\nUpdate environment variables for `op-web`:\n\n```bash\n# Get container IP\nMAIL_IP=$(incus list mail-3tched -c 4 -f csv | cut -d' ' -f1)\n\n# Set environment for op-web\nexport SMTP_HOST=\"$MAIL_IP\"\nexport SMTP_PORT=\"587\"\nexport SMTP_USER=\"jeremy@3tched.com\"\nexport SMTP_PASS=\"<password-you-set>\"\nexport SMTP_FROM_EMAIL=\"noreply@3tched.com\"\nexport SMTP_FROM_NAME=\"Operation DBUS\"\nexport BASE_URL=\"https://your-op-web-url.com\"\n```\n\nThe existing magic link code in `crates/op-web/src/email.rs` will automatically use these settings.\n\n## Container Management\n\n```bash\n# Start container\nincus start mail-3tched\n\n# Stop container\nincus stop mail-3tched\n\n# View logs\nincus exec mail-3tched -- tail -f /var/log/maddy/maddy.log\n\n# Access container shell\nincus exec mail-3tched -- sh\n\n# Restart services\nincus exec mail-3tched -- rc-service maddy restart\nincus exec mail-3tched -- rc-service caddy restart\n```\n\n## Adding New Users\n\n```bash\nincus exec mail-3tched -- maddyctl creds create newuser@3tched.com\n```\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### Mail not sending\n1. Check Maddy logs: `incus exec mail-3tched -- tail -f /var/log/maddy/maddy.log`\n2. Verify DNS records: `dig MX 3tched.com`\n3. Test SMTP: `telnet <container-ip> 25`\n\n### Webmail not accessible\n1. Check Caddy: `incus exec mail-3tched -- rc-service caddy status`\n2. Check PHP-FPM: `incus exec mail-3tched -- rc-service php-fpm83 status`\n3. View Caddy logs: `incus exec mail-3tched -- tail -f /var/log/caddy/access.log`\n\n### IMAP connection issues\n1. Verify Maddy is running: `incus exec mail-3tched -- rc-service maddy status`\n2. Test IMAP: `telnet <container-ip> 143`\n3. Check credentials: `incus exec mail-3tched -- maddyctl creds list`\n\n## Security Notes\n\n- TLS is currently disabled for simplicity. Enable it in production:\n  ```bash\n  # Edit maddy.conf and set: tls file /path/to/cert.pem /path/to/key.pem\n  ```\n- Use strong passwords for mail accounts\n- Configure firewall to only allow necessary ports (25, 587, 143, 80/443)\n- Consider enabling fail2ban for brute force protection\n\n## Next Steps\n\n1. Get SSL certificates (Let's Encrypt) for mail.3tched.com\n2. Configure reverse DNS (PTR record) with your ISP\n3. Monitor mail queue and logs regularly\n4. Set up backups for `/var/lib/maddy/`\n"}}

This is a common workflow in enterprise environments where the default Google Cloud Code client ID is restricted by organization policies.\\n\\nTo access your Enterprise benefits (like the full Gemini Code Assist features), you must complete two distinct steps:\\n\\nAuthenticate using your custom OAuth client.\\nSelect the Google Cloud Project that holds your Gemini Code Assist license.\\nHere is how to set this up.\\n\\nStep 1: Create your OAuth Client (Prerequisite)\\nIf you haven't already, you need to create a \\\"Desktop App\\\" OAuth client in the Google Cloud Console.\\n\\nGo to APIs & Services > Credentials.\\nClick Create Credentials > OAuth client ID.\\nApplication type: Desktop app.\\nCopy the Client ID and Client Secret.\\nStep 2: Authenticate via gcloud with Custom Credentials\\nYou can force the gcloud CLI to use your specific client ID and secret instead of the default Google ones. Run this command in your terminal:\\n\\nbash\\ngcloud auth login \\\\\\n  --client-id=\\\"YOUR_CLIENT_ID.apps.googleusercontent.com\\\" \\\\\\n  --client-secret=\\\"YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET\\\"\\nThis will open a browser window. Log in with your enterprise account. Once finished, gcloud is authenticated using your custom client.\\n\\nStep 3: Configure VS Code to use gcloud\\nBy default, the VS Code extension tries to manage its own login session. You need to tell it to rely on the gcloud CLI state you just configured.\\n\\nOpen VS Code.\\nOpen Settings (Ctrl+, or Cmd+,).\\nSearch for Cloud Code: Auth Method.\\nChange the setting from Trusted Tester or OpenID Connect to gcloud.\\nAlternatively, edit your settings.json directly:\\njson\\n\\\"cloudcode.authMethod\\\": \\\"gcloud\\\"\\nReload VS Code (Open Command Palette Ctrl+Shift+P -> \\\"Developer: Reload Window\\\").\\nThe extension will now pick up the credentials from your gcloud CLI session.\\n\\nStep 4: Activate Enterprise Benefits (Crucial)\\nLogging in identifies who you are, but it doesn't automatically apply your enterprise license. The license is attached to a specific Google Cloud Project.\\n\\nLook at the Cloud Code status bar item (usually at the bottom of VS Code).\\nClick on the Project selector (it might say \\\"Select a project\\\" or show a current project ID).\\nSelect the Google Cloud Project that has the Gemini for Google Cloud API enabled and the subscription active.\\nOnce this project is selected, the extension will verify your license against that project, and your Enterprise benefits (like higher rate limits and codebase awareness) will be active.\\n\\nAlternative: Direct VS Code Configuration (No gcloud required)\\nIf you prefer not to rely on the external gcloud CLI installation, you can input your custom client directly into VS Code. This is often more stable.\\n\\nOpen VS Code Settings.\\nSearch for Cloud Code: Custom Client ID.\\nPaste your Client ID and Client Secret into the respective fields.\\nReload the window and sign in via the extension's normal flow.\\nGenerated by Gemini 3 Pro Preview\\n\\njeremy hobson\\nyou have access to my account do for me\\n\\n\\nGemini\\nResponding with gemini-3-pro\\nThinking\\nAs an AI assistant, I do not have direct access to your Google Cloud account, your local file system, or your VS Code settings.\\n\\nI cannot execute commands on your machine or log in on your behalf. I process the text and code you send me, but I cannot \\\"reach out\\\" to your computer to change settings or read your private credentials.\\nArchitecture: The VS Code Extension is the tool that holds your keys and talks to Google Cloud. I am the intelligence behind the chat window. The extension asks me questions, and I answer them, but I don't control the extension's configuration.\\nAction Plan: How to do it yourself\\nSince you want to configure the custom OAuth client to get your Enterprise benefits, you need to run the command we discussed in your terminal (Command Prompt, PowerShell, or macOS/Linux Terminal).\\n\\n1. Copy and Run this command: Replace the placeholders with the Client ID and Secret you created in the Google Cloud Console.\\n\\nbash\\ngcloud auth login --client-id=\\\"YOUR_CLIENT_ID.apps.googleusercontent.com\\\" --client-secret=\\\"YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET\\\"\\n2. \"org.opdbus.rovs.openflow\")]\nimpl OpenFlowService {\n    /// Connect to a switch at `addr` (e.g. `\"tcp:127.0.0.1:6653\"`).\n    ///\n    /// `addr` is parsed by `rovs_transport::Address::from_str` connect(&self, addr: &str) -> String {\n        debug!(\"openflow.connect addr={}\", addr);\n\n        let address = match addr.parse::<Address>() {\n            Ok(a) => a,\n            Err(e) => Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n</collaboration_mode>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<apps_instructions>\n## Apps (Connectors)\nApps (Connectors) can be explicitly triggered in user messages in the format `[$app-name](app://{connector_id})`. Apps can also be implicitly triggered as long as the context suggests usage of available apps.\nAn app is equivalent to a set of MCP tools within the `codex_apps` MCP.\nAn installed app's MCP tools are either provided to you already, or can be lazy-loaded through the `tool_search` tool. If `tool_search` is available, the apps that are searchable by `tools_search` will be listed by it.\nDo not additionally call list_mcp_resources or list_mcp_resource_templates for apps.\n</apps_instructions>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<skills_instructions>\n## Skills\nA skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-08</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-09T03:36:27.621Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Right now the live `mail-3tched` container is using:\n\n- **Postfix** for SMTP / submission / SMTPS\n- **Dovecot** for IMAP / IMAPS and LMTP delivery\n- **Virtual Maildir** storage under `/var/mail/vhosts/3tched.com`\n- **Incus proxy Unix sockets** from `mail-3tched` into `wg-xray`\n- **Xray tagged routing** from public mail ports to the local mail loopback shims\n\nPorts wired:\n\n- SMTP `25`\n- Submission `587`\n- SMTPS `465`\n- IMAP `143`\n- IMAPS `993`\n\nI originally looked for `maddy`, but Alpine did not have a package available in that container, so I used the Postfix/Dovecot stack that was available and could be brought up immediately.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-09T03:36:27.626Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"Right now the live `mail-3tched` container is using:\n\n- **Postfix** for SMTP / submission / SMTPS\n- **Dovecot** for IMAP / IMAPS and LMTP delivery\n- **Virtual Maildir** storage under `/var/mail/vhosts/3tched.com`\n- **Incus proxy Unix sockets** from `mail-3tched` into `wg-xray`\n- **Xray tagged routing** from public mail ports to the local mail loopback shims\n\nPorts wired:\n\n- SMTP `25`\n- Submission `587`\n- SMTPS `465`\n- IMAP `143`\n- IMAPS `993`\n\nI originally looked for `maddy`, but Alpine did not have a package available in that container, so I used the Postfix/Dovecot stack that was available and could be brought up immediately."}],"phase":"final_answer"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-09T03:38:21.291Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"For the programs actually running now:\n\n- **Postfix**: I would not expect a repo-native JSON Schema. Postfix config is source-defined through its parameter tables/manual config model, not a JSON/proto schema artifact.\n- **Dovecot**: same story. It has structured settings internally, but not usually a checked-in JSON Schema/OpenAPI-style contract we can directly import.\n- **Maddy**: I checked its GitHub repo quickly. I did not see a JSON Schema/proto/OpenAPI schema. It has a Go config parser and config mapping code, plus Kubernetes YAML/chart files, but no ready schema artifact.\n\nSo for the current Postfix/Dovecot mail stack, the practical source of truth for our state plugin should be:\n\n1. `MailServerState` / `MailEndpoints` in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/mail_server.rs`\n2. The live service contract we expose: SMTP/Submission/SMTPS/IMAP/IMAPS sockets\n3. `crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto/mail.proto` for the external gRPC mail API shape\n\nI should not invent a separate schema in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`; the `mail_server` state plugin should own that schema contract.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

{\n        register_schema_if_missing(&mut schema_engine, schema)?;\n    }\n\n    info!(\n        \"Registered initial schemas ({} total)\",\n        schema_engine.list_schemas().len()\n    );\n\n    // 2. Initialize Projection Store and Engine\n    let store = ProjectionStore::new();\n    let validator = SchemaValidator::new(schema_engine.clone());\n    let engine = Arc::new(Mutex::new(ProjectionSystemEngine::new(\n        store.clone(),\n        validator,\n    )));\n\n    // 3. Initialize Source Readers\n    let procfs_reader = SystemProcfsReader::new();\n    let sled_reader = IdentitySledReader::new();\n    let _dbus_reader = SystemDbusReader::new();\n    let _grpc_reader = SystemGrpcReader::new();\n\n    info!(\"Initialized source readers\");\n\n    // 4. Initialize JSON-stream Server\n    let mut stream_server = ProjectionStreamServer::new();\n    stream_server.start(8082)?;\n    let mut dbus_server = ProjectionDbusServer::new()\n        .await\n        .context(\"failed to start projection D-Bus server\")?;\n\n    // 5. Initial Scan and Projection\n    {\n        let mut initial_entities = Vec::new();\n\n        info!(\"Performing initial scan...\");\n\n        if procfs_reader.is_available() {\n            initial_entities.extend(procfs_reader.read_all()?);\n        }\n\n        if sled_reader.is_available() {\n            if let Ok(entities) = sled_reader.read_all() {\n                initial_entities.extend(entities);\n            }\n        }\n\n        if plugin_reader.is_available() {\n            match plugin_reader.read_all_async().await {\n                Ok(entities) => initial_entities.extend(entities),\n                Err(error) => warn!(error = %error, \"Failed to read plugin projection entities\"),\n            }\n        }\n\n        for entity in initial_entities {\n            let projection = {\n                let mut engine_lock = engine.lock();\n                engine_lock.create_projection(entity)?\n            };\n            dbus_server.upsert(&projection).await?;\n            stream_server.broadcast(&ProjectionUpdate {\n                update_type: UpdateType::Created,\n                projection,\n                timestamp: chrono::Utc::now(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        info!(\"Initial scan complete\");\n    }\n\n    // 6. Initialize Access Controller\n    let mut access_controller = ProjectionAccessController::new();\n    access_controller.add_policy(AccessPolicy {\n        id: \"allow-all-read\".to_string(),\n        resource_pattern: \".*\".to_string(),\n        required_permissions: vec![],\n        action: \"read\".to_string(),\n        redact_sensitive: false,\n    });\n\n    info!(\"Projection Server is ready\");\n\n    // 7. Keep-alive loop (in production, this would be the event loop)\n    loop {\n        tokio::time::sleep(tokio::time::Duration::from_secs(60)).await;\n        let mut refresh_entities = Vec::new();\n\n        // Periodic refresh from procfs\n        if let Ok(entities) = procfs_reader.read_all() {\n            refresh_entities.extend(entities);\n        }\n\n        // Periodic refresh from Sled\n        if let Ok(entities) = sled_reader.read_all() {\n            refresh_entities.extend(entities);\n        }\n\n        if plugin_reader.is_available() {\n            match plugin_reader.read_all_async().await {\n                Ok(entities) => refresh_entities.extend(entities),\n                Err(error) => warn!(\n                    error = %error,\n                    \"Failed to refresh plugin projection entities\"\n                ),\n            }\n        }\n\n        for entity in refresh_entities {\n            let update = {\n                let mut engine_lock = engine.lock();\n                engine_lock.create_projection(entity)?\n            };\n            dbus_server.upsert(&update).await?;\n\n            stream_server.broadcast(&ProjectionUpdate {\n                update_type: UpdateType::Updated,\n                projection: update,\n                timestamp: chrono::Utc::now(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        info!(\"Periodic refresh complete\");\n    }\n}\n\nfn register_schema_if_missing(\n    schema_engine: &mut SchemaEngine,\n    schema: PluginSchema,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    if schema_engine.has_valid_schema(&schema.name) {\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let schema_name = schema.name.clone();\n    schema_engine\n        .register_schema(schema)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to register projection schema '{}'\", schema_name))?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n"}}

      let name = plugin.name().to_string();\n                let schema = plugin.schema().or_else(|| builtin_plugin_schema(&name));\n\n                if schema.is_none() {\n                    warn!(\n                        plugin_id = %name,\n                        \"Plugin has no PluginSchema; top-level state will be projected without plugin-specific validation\"\n                    );\n                }\n\n                LoadedPlugin { name, schema, plugin }\n            })\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n\n        info!(\n            plugin_count = plugins.len(),\n  .field(\"plugin_id\", read_only_string(\"Owning plugin identifier\"))\n            .field(\"parent_id\", read_only_string(\"Parent projection entity ID\"))\n            .field(\n                \"object_path\",\n                read_only_string(\"JSON pointer-like path to the nested object\"),\n            )\n            .field(\n                \"value\",\n                FieldSchema {\n                    field_type: FieldType::Any,\n                    required: true,\n                    description: \"Nested object value mirrored from plugin state\".to_string(),\n                    default: None,\n                    example: None,\n                    constraints: Vec::new(),\n                    read_only: true,\n                    read_only_when: None,\n                },\n            )\n            .build()\n    }\n\n    /// Returns all schemas required for plugin state projection.\n    ///\n    /// Plugin schemas are the canonical `PluginSchema` directly — no conversion:\n    /// the plugin is the schema.\n    pub fn projection_schemas(&self) -> Vec<PluginSchema> {\n        let mut schemas = self\n            .plugins\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|plugin| plugin.schema.clone())\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n        schemas.push(Self::nested_object_projection_schema());\n        schemas\n    }\n\n    /// Reads all plugin-backed projection entities asynchronously.\n    pub async fn read_all_async(&self) -> Result<Vec<RawEntity>> {\n        let mut entities = Vec::new();\n\n        for plugin in &self.plugins {\n            entities.extend(self.read_loaded_plugin(plugin).await?);\n        }\n\n        debug!(\n            entity_count = entities.len(),\n            \"Read plugin projection entities\"\n        );\n        Ok(entities)\n    }\n\n    /// Reads all projection entities for a single plugin asynchronously.\n    pub async fn read_plugin_objects_async(&self, plugin_id: &str) ->  Some(plugin) => plugin,\n            None => {\n                requested_plugin = Self::load_requested_plugin(&requested_id).await?;\n                &requested_plugin\n            }\n        };\n\n entity_type = plugin\n            .schema\n            .as_ref()\n            .map(|schema| schema.name.clone())\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| plugin.name.clone());\n        let mut entities = vec![RawEntity {\n            entity_type,\n            entity_id: plugin.name.clone(),\n            data: state.clone(),\n            source: self.source.clone(),\n        }];\n\n        entities.extend(Self::collect_nested_entities(\n            &plugin.name,\n            &state,\n            &self.source,\n        ));\n\n        Ok(entities)\n    }\n\n    fn collect_nested_entities(plugin_id: &str, state: &Value, source: &str) -> Vec<RawEntity> {\n        let mut entities = Vec::new();\n        Self::collect_nested_entities_recursive(\n            &mut Self::empty()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl SourceReader for SystemPluginReader {\n    fn read_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<RawEntity>> {\n        self.block_on(self.read_all_async())\n    }\n\n    fn {\n        debug!(plugin_id = plugin_id, \"Reading plugin objects\");\n        self.block_on(self.read_plugin_objects_async(plugin_id))\n    }\n\n    fn read_nested_objects(&self, plugin_id: &str,                   { \"name\": \"peer-a\" }\n                    ]\n                }\n            ],\n            \"metadata\": {\n                \"enabled\": true\n            }\n        });\n\n        let entities = SystemPluginReader::collect_nested_entities(\"wireguard\", &state, \"plugin\");\n        let entity_ids = entities\n            .iter()\n            .map(|entity| entity.entity_id.clone())\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n\n        assert!(entity_ids.contains(&\"wireguard:/interfaces\".to_string()));\n        assert!(entity_ids.contains(&\"wireguard:/interfaces/0\".to_string()));\n        assert!(entity_ids.contains(&\"wireguard:/interfaces/0/peers\".to_string()));\n        assert!(entity_ids.contains(&\"wireguard:/metadata\".to_string()));\n\n        let peers = entities\n            .iter()\n            .find(|entity| entity.entity_id == \"wireguard:/interfaces/0/peers\")\n            .expect(\"peers projection\");\n        assert_eq!(peers.data[\"parent_id\"], \"wireguard:/interfaces/0\");\n        assert_eq!(peers.data[\"plugin_id\"], \"wireguard\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn should_consume_canonical_plugin_schema_directly() {\n        // The plugin is the schema: projection uses the Canonical Plugin Path and Interface Constants\n//!\n//! This module defines the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for all plugin-related\n//! paths, interfaces, and naming conventions following FreeDesktop D-Bus\n//! standards.\n//!\n//! ## Canonical Naming Convention\n//!\n//! ### D-Bus Object Paths\n//! ```text\n//! /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/{plugin_name}\n//! /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/{plugin_name}/{child_object}\n//! ```\n//!\n//! ### D-Bus Interface Names\n//! ```text\n//! org.opdbus.v1.Plugin.Plugins\n//! org.opdbus.v1.Plugin.Plugins.{PluginName}\n//! org.opdbus.v1.Plugin.{PluginName}\n//! ```\n//!\n//! ### D-Bus Service Names (Bus Names)\n//! ```text\n//! org.opdbus.v1\n//! org.opdbus.v1.Plugin.{PluginName}\n//! ```\n//!\n//! ### Schema File Paths\n//! ```text\n//! schemas/plugin/{plugin_name}.json\n//! schemas/plugin/freedesktop.json\n//! ```\n//!\n//! ## Forbidden Patterns (DO NOT USE)\n//!\n//! These patterns are deprecated and MUST NOT be used:\n//! - `/opdbus/v1/plugins/` - Missing `org` prefix\n//! - `/org/opdbus/plugins/` - Missing `v1` version\n//! - `/org/opdbus/v1/` - Missing `plugin` segment\n//! - `org.opdbus.plugins.*` - Missing `v1` version\n//! - `org.opdbus.v1plugins.*` - Missing dot separator\n//!\n//! ## Migration Guide\n//!\n//! Old (deprecated): `/opdbus/v1/plugins/net`\n//! New (canonical): `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/net`\n//!\n//! Old (deprecated alias): `/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/net`\n//! New (canonical): `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/net`\n//!\n//! Old (deprecated): `org.opdbus.NetPlugin`\n//! New (canonical): `org.opdbus.v1.Plugin.Plugins.Net`\n\n/// Root D-Bus object path for the op-dbus system\npub const DBUS_ROOT_PATH: &str = \"/org/opdbus/v1\";\n\n/// Canonical base path for all plugins\npub const PLUGIN_BASE_PATH: &str = \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins\";\n\n/// Base interface name for plugin-related interfaces\npub const PLUGIN_BASE_INTERFACE: &str = \"org.opdbus.v1.Plugin\";\n\n/// Interface for the plugins collection/manager\npub const PLUGINS_INTERFACE: &str = \"org.opdbus.v1.Plugin.Plugins\";\n\n/// Base service name (bus name)\npub const BASE_SERVICE_NAME: &str = \"org.opdbus.v1\";\n\n/// Schema file directory for plugins\npub const PLUGIN_SCHEMA_DIR: &str = \"schemas/plugin\";\n\n/// Meta-schema file for plugin validation\npub const PLUGIN_META_SCHEMA: &str = \"schemas/plugin/org.opdbus.plugin.schema.json\";\n\n/// FreeDesktop plugin schema\npub const FREEDESKTOP_SCHEMA: &str = \"schemas/plugin/freedesktop.json\";\n\n/// ObjectManager interface (FreeDesktop standard)\npub const OBJECT_MANAGER_INTERFACE: &str = \"org.freedesktop.DBus.ObjectManager\";\n\n/// Properties interface (FreeDesktop standard)\npub const PROPERTIES_INTERFACE: &str = \"org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties\";\n\n/// Introspectable interface (FreeDesktop standard)\npub const INTROSPECTABLE_INTERFACE: &str = \"org.freedesktop.DBus.Introspectable\";\n\n/// Peer interface (FreeDesktop standard)\npub const PEER_INTERFACE: &str = \"org.freedesktop.DBus.Peer\";\n\n/// Legacy path prefix - DEPRECATED, for migration only\n#[deprecated(\n    since = \"2.0.0\",\n    note = \"Use PLUGIN_BASE_PATH instead. Legacy paths will be removed in v3.0.0\"\n)]\npub const LEGACY_PLUGIN_PATH: &str = \"/opdbus/v1/plugins\";\n\n/// Alternative legacy path - DEPRECATED, for migration only\n#[deprecated(\n    since = \"2.0.0\",\n    note = \"Use PLUGIN_BASE_PATH instead. Legacy paths will be removed in v3.0.0\"\n)]\npub const LEGACY_ALT_PLUGIN_PATH: &str = \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins\";\n\n/// Build the full D-Bus object path for a plugin\n///\n/// # Example\n/// ```\n/// use op_plugins::canonical::plugin_path;\n///\n/// let path = plugin_path(\"incus\");\n/// assert_eq!(path, \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/incus\");\n/// ```\npub fn plugin_path(name: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\"{}/{}\", PLUGIN_BASE_PATH, sanitize_plugin_name(name))\n}\n\n/// Build the D-Bus interface name for a specific plugin\n///\n/// # Example\n/// ```\n/// use op_plugins::canonical::plugin_interface;\n///\n/// let iface = plugin_interface(\"incus\");\n/// assert_eq!(iface, \"org.opdbus.v1.Plugin.Plugins.Incus\");\n/// ```\npub fn plugin_interface(name: &str) -> String {\n    let sanitized = sanitize_plugin_name(name);\n    let capitalized = capitalize_plugin_name(&sanitized);\n    format!(\"{}.{}\", PLUGINS_INTERFACE, capitalized)\n}\n\n/// Build the schema file path for a plugin\n///\n/// # Example\n/// ```\n/// use op_plugins::canonical::plugin_schema_path;\n///\n/// let path = plugin_schema_path(\"incus\");\n/// assert_eq!(path, \"schemas/plugin/incus.json\");\n/// ```\npub fn plugin_schema_path(name: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\"{}/{}.json\", PLUGIN_SCHEMA_DIR, sanitize_plugin_name(name))\n}\n\n/// Build a child object path under a plugin\n///\n/// # Example\n/// ```\n/// use op_plugins::canonical::plugin_child_path;\n///\n/// let path = plugin_child_path(\"incus\", \"instance-1\");\n/// assert_eq!(path, \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/incus/instance-1\");\n/// ```\npub fn plugin_child_path(plugin_name: &str, child_id: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\n        \"{}/{}/{}\",\n        PLUGIN_BASE_PATH,\n        sanitize_plugin_name(plugin_name),\n        sanitize_child_id(child_id)\n    )\n}\n\n/// Sanitize a plugin name for use in paths and interface names\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - Convert to lowercase\n/// - Replace hyphens with underscores\n/// - Remove any leading/trailing slashes\n/// - Must start with a letter (a-z)\npub fn sanitize_plugin_name(name: &str) -> String {\n    let sanitized = name\n        .trim()\n        .trim_matches('/')\n        .to_lowercase()\n        .replace('-', \"_\");\n\n    // Ensure it starts with a letter\n    if sanitized\n        .chars()\n        .next()\n        .map(|c| c.is_ascii_digit())\n        .unwrap_or(false)\n    {\n        format!(\"plugin_{}\", sanitized)\n    } else {\n        sanitized\n    }\n}\n\n/// Capitalize a plugin name for use in interface names\n///\n/// Converts `plugin_name` to `PluginName`\npub fn capitalize_plugin_name(name: &str) -> String {\n    name.split('_')\n        .map(|word| {\n            let mut chars = word.chars();\n            match chars.next() {\n                None => String::new(),\n                Some(first) => {\n                    first.to_uppercase().collect::<String>() + &chars.as_str().to_lowercase()\n                }\n            }\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Sanitize a child object ID for use in paths\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - Must not contain path separators\n/// - Must be valid UTF-8\n/// - Length must be <= 255 characters\nfn sanitize_child_id(id: &str) -> String {\n    let sanitized: String = id\n        .chars()\n        .filter(|c| *c != '/' && *c != '\\\\' && !c.is_control())\n        .take(255)\n        .collect();\n\n    if sanitized.is_empty() {\n        \"_\".to_string()\n    } else {\n        sanitized\n    }\n}\n\n/// Validate a plugin path is in canonical form\n///\n/// Returns true if the path follows the canonical convention\npub fn is_canonical_plugin_path(path: &str) -> bool {\n    path.starts_with(PLUGIN_BASE_PATH)\n}\n\n/// Normalize a plugin path to canonical form\n///\n/// Converts legacy paths to canonical paths\n///\n/// # Examples\n/// - `/opdbus/v1/plugins/net` → `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/net`\n/// - `/org/opdbus/v1/plugin/plugins/net` → `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/net`\n"}}
