{"timestamp":"2026-06-09T03:46:30.626Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_WyuDWvE95NObzmWetsyxvGSk","output":"Chunk ID: fdd12b\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1816\nOutput:\n//! D-Bus object server for projections.\n//!\n//! Serves every Projection as a D-Bus object under org.opdbus.projection at\n//! /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<category>/<id>, e.g. /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/system/memory\n//! or /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/system/process/1234. Nothing mounts outside the\n//! plugins root: no plugin means no schema means no object.\n\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tokio::sync::RwLock;\nuse tracing::{debug, info};\nuse zbus::{connection::Builder, interface, object_server::SignalEmitter, Connection};\n\nuse crate::data_models::Projection;\n\n/// A single projected object on the D-Bus object server.\npub struct ProjectedObject {\n    pub entity_type: String,\n    pub entity_id: String,\n    /// JSON-serialized projection data\n    pub data_json: Arc<RwLock<String>>,\n    pub state: Arc<RwLock<String>>,\n}\n\n#[interface(name = \"org.opdbus.projection.v1.Object\")]\nimpl ProjectedObject {\n    /// The schema/entity type for this object (e.g. \"system.memory\")\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn entity_type(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.entity_type\n    }\n\n    /// The unique entity ID within its type\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn entity_id(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.entity_id\n    }\n\n    /// Current projection state: Valid, Quarantined, Degraded, etc.\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn state(&self) -> String {\n        self.state.read().await.clone()\n    }\n\n    /// Full projection data as a JSON string\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn data(&self) -> String {\n        self.data_json.read().await.clone()\n    }\n\n    /// Signal emitted when this object's data changes\n    #[zbus(signal)]\n    async fn updated(emitter: &SignalEmitter<'_>, data_json: &str) -> zbus::Result<()>;\n}\n\n/// Derives the D-Bus object path from a projection's entity_type and entity_id.\n///\n/// Every projected object lives under the single plugins root. No plugin means\n/// no schema means no object — nothing is ever mounted outside this path.\n///\n/// entity_type \"system.memory\"    → /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/system/memory\n/// entity_type \"system.process\"   → /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/system/process/<entity_id>\n/// entity_type \"identity.sled\"    → /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/identity/sled\n/// entity_type \"ovsdb_bridge\"     → /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/ovsdb/bridge/<entity_id>\npub fn projection_path(entity_type: &str, entity_id: &str) -> String {\n    // The ONLY path projections are allowed to mount under.\n    const PLUGIN_ROOT: &str = \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins\";\n\n    // Replace dots and underscores in type with slashes for the path prefix\n    let type_path = entity_type.replace(['.', '_'], \"/\").to_lowercase();\n\n    // For singleton objects (memory, cpu, filesystems, network) the entity_id\n    // is typically the same as the type — omit it to avoid redundancy.\n    let is_singleton = entity_id == entity_type\n        || entity_id.is_empty()\n        || entity_id == \"memory\"\n        || entity_id == \"cpu\"\n        || entity_id == \"filesystems\"\n        || entity_id == \"network\"\n        || entity_id == \"sled\";\n\n    if is_singleton {\n        format!(\"{}/{}\", PLUGIN_ROOT, type_path)\n    } else {\n        // Sanitize entity_id for use in a path segment\n        let safe_id: String = entity_id\n            .chars()\n            .map(|c| {\n                if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_' {\n                    c\n                } else {\n                    '_'\n                }\n            })\n            .collect();\n        format!(\"{}/{}/{}\", PLUGIN_ROOT, type_path, safe_id)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Object state handles for updating in place\ntype ObjectHandles = (Arc<RwLock<String>>, Arc<RwLock<String>>);\n\n/// Manages the set of D-Bus objects served for all projections.\npub struct ProjectionDbusServer {\n    conn: Connection,\n    /// path → data/state handles so we can update in place\n    objects: HashMap<String, ObjectHandles>,\n}\n\nimpl ProjectionDbusServer {\n    pub async fn new() -> Result<Self> {\n        let conn = match std::env::var(\"OP_DBUS_PROJECTION_BUS\")\n            .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"system\".to_string())\n            .as_str()\n        {\n            \"session\" => {\n                Builder::session()?\n                    .name(\"org.opdbus.projection\")?\n                    .build()\n                    .await?\n            }\n            _ => {\n                Builder::system()?\n                    .name(\"org.opdbus.projection\")?\n                    .build()\n                    .await?\n            }\n        };\n\n        info!(\"D-Bus connection established for org.opdbus.projection\");\n\n        Ok(Self {\n            conn,\n            objects: HashMap::new(),\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub async fn new_session() -> Result<Self> {\n        let conn = Builder::session()?\n            .name(\"org.opdbus.projection\")?\n            .build()\n            .await?;\n\n        info!(\"D-Bus session bus connection established for org.opdbus.projection\");\n\n        Ok(Self {\n            conn,\n            objects: HashMap::new(),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Register a projection as a D-Bus object (or update it if already registered).\n    pub async fn upsert(&mut self, projection: &Projection) -> Result<()> {\n        let path = projection_path(&projection.entity_type, &projection.entity_id);\n        let data_json = simd_json::to_string(&projection.data).unwrap_or_else(|_| \"{}\".to_string());\n        let state_str = format!(\"{:?}\", projection.state);\n\n        if let Some((data_handle, state_handle)) = self.objects.get(&path) {\n            // Update existing object in place\n            *data_handle.write().await = data_json.clone();\n            *state_handle.write().await = state_str;\n\n            // Emit the updated signal\n            let iface_ref = self\n                .conn\n                .object_server()\n                .interface::<_, ProjectedObject>(path.as_str())\n                .await?;\n            ProjectedObject::updated(iface_ref.signal_emitter(), &data_json).await?;\n\n            debug!(path, \"updated D-Bus projection object\");\n        } else {\n            // Register new object\n            let data_arc = Arc::new(RwLock::new(data_json));\n            let state_arc = Arc::new(RwLock::new(state_str));\n\n            let obj = ProjectedObject {\n                entity_type: projection.entity_type.clone(),\n                entity_id: projection.entity_id.clone(),\n                data_json: data_arc.clone(),\n                state: state_arc.clone(),\n            };\n\n            self.conn.object_server().at(path.as_str(), obj).await?;\n\n            self.objects.insert(path.clone(), (data_arc, state_arc));\n            info!(path, entity_type = %projection.entity_type, \"registered D-Bus projection object\");\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Remove a projection's D-Bus object.\n    pub async fn remove(&mut self, entity_type: &str, entity_id: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        let path = projection_path(entity_type, entity_id);\n        if self.objects.remove(&path).is_some() {\n            self.conn\n                .object_server()\n                .remove::<ProjectedObject, _>(path.as_str())\n                .await?;\n            info!(path, \"removed D-Bus projection object\");\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn object_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.objects.len()\n    }\n}\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-09T03:51:11.785Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"You’re right: with the architecture you’re describing, “default plugins” is redundant and probably harmful.\n\nThe cleaner model is:\n\n- `state_plugins/` defines the plugin universe.\n- Every state plugin is discoverable.\n- Every discovered plugin has or auto-creates a schema.\n- Projection publishes all discovered plugin schemas to `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`.\n- Projection only creates D-Bus objects under `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>/...`.\n- Runtime availability belongs in plugin state, not in whether the plugin exists.\n\nSo “default plugins” should not decide schema existence. At most, it can become a separate runtime policy like “start these daemons by default,” but not “these are the plugins.”\n\nThe refactor direction should be:\n\n- remove `load_default_plugins()` from projection use,\n- replace `default_auto_load()` with discovery from `state_plugins`,\n- keep optional config only for enable/disable runtime behavior,\n- let unavailable plugins still publish schema with `available=false` or equivalent state.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-09T03:52:39.227Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"The registry’s useful job should not be “decide which plugins exist.” You’re right: if a state plugin exists in `state_plugins`, it should be registered.\n\nThe registry should only do these jobs:\n\n- discover plugins from `state_plugins`\n- instantiate the plugin object\n- normalize aliases like `mail` -> `mail_server` if needed\n- fall back to auto-create when something is referenced but missing\n- hand plugins to `StateManager` / projection\n- maybe apply runtime policy like disabled/quarantined, but not erase schema existence\n\nThe extra “default plugins” step is legacy baggage. It creates a second source of truth:\n\n```text\nstate_plugins says plugin exists\ndefault_auto_load says maybe it exists\n```\n\nThat conflicts with “plugin is the schema.” The correct flow should be:\n\n```text\nstate_plugins module exists\n  -> registry discovers it\n  -> registry instantiates/registers it\n  -> schema enters /dev/shm/live-schema.json\n  -> projection exposes /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>\n```\n\nSo the registry is still useful as the factory/discovery layer, but `default_auto_load` should go away or become only a runtime enablement policy, not plugin registration.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-09T03:53:40.403Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"The registry should remain, but only as a **discovery + construction + registration coordinator**. It should not carry a separate plugin list.\n\nUseful responsibilities:\n\n- discover state plugins from `state_plugins`\n- instantiate the matching Rust plugin\n- auto-create missing plugin implementations when a referenced plugin has no Rust implementation yet\n- register every plugin with `StateManager`\n- expose every plugin schema to projection\n- normalize paths/aliases\n- apply quarantine/disable policy without deleting schema existence\n\nNot useful responsibilities:\n\n- deciding “default” plugins\n- requiring a second list after a plugin file already exists\n- hiding unavailable plugins from schema publication\n- making `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` depend on an autoload list\n\nSo the registry is still the place where plugin objects are assembled and handed to the system, but the source of truth is `state_plugins`, not registry lists.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-09T03:53:40.411Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"The registry should remain, but only as a **discovery + construction + registration coordinator**. It should not carry a separate plugin list.\n\nUseful responsibilities:\n\n- discover state plugins from `state_plugins`\n- instantiate the matching Rust plugin\n- auto-create missing plugin implementations when a referenced plugin has no Rust implementation yet\n- register every plugin with `StateManager`\n- expose every plugin schema to projection\n- normalize paths/aliases\n- apply quarantine/disable policy without deleting schema existence\n\nNot useful responsibilities:\n\n- deciding “default” plugins\n- requiring a second list after a plugin file already exists\n- hiding unavailable plugins from schema publication\n- making `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` depend on an autoload list\n\nSo the registry is still the place where plugin objects are assembled and handed to the system, but the source of truth is `state_plugins`, not registry lists."}],"phase":"final_answer"}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. = std::fs::read(SHM_SCHEMA_PATH)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Cannot read schema SHM: {}\", e))?;\n        let hash = blake3::hash(&bytes);\n        Ok(hash.to_hex().to_string())\n    }\n\n    /// Generates a trace ID for audit trail\n    fn generate_trace_id(&self) -> String {\n        // In production, use a proper UUID or distributed tracing ID\n        let timestamp = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_nanos_opt().unwrap_or(0);\n        format!(\"trace-{}\", timestamp)\n    }\n\n    /// Records an audit entry for schema changes\n    fn record_audit(&mut self, schema_name: &str, change_type: SchemaChangeType, reason: &str) {\n        let footprint = self.generate_footprint(schema_name, 0);\n        let trace_id = self.generate_trace_id();\n        let change_type_clone = change_type.clone();\n\n        let entry = SchemaAuditEntry {\n            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now(),\n            actor: \"system\".to_string(),\n            schema_name: schema_name.to_string(),\n            change_type,\n            reason: reason.to_string(),\n            footprint,\n            trace_id,\n        };\n\n        self.audit_trail.push(entry);\n        debug!(\n            schema_name = schema_name,\n            change_type = ?change_type_clone,\n            \"Schema audit entry recorded\"\n        );\n    }\n}\n\nimpl SchemaRegistry for SchemaEngine {\n    /// Register a new schema version\n    ///\n    /// Returns the schema version number on success.\n    fn register_schema(&mut self, schema: PluginSchema) -> Result<u64> {\n        let schema_name = schema.name.clone();\n        let schema_version = schema.version.clone();\n\n        // Check if schema is quarantined\n        if let Some(reason) = self.quarantined.get(&schema_name) {\n            return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n                \"Cannot register schema '{}': it is quarantined: {}\",\n                schema_name,\n                reason\n            ));\n        }\n\n        // Get or initialize version counter\n        let version = self.version_counter.get(&schema_name).copied().unwrap_or(0) + 1;\n\n        // Update version counter\n        self.version_counter.insert(schema_name.clone(), version);\n\n        // Add schema to registry\n        self.schemas\n            .entry(schema_name.clone())\n            .or_default()\n            .push(schema.clone());\n\n        // Record audit entry\n        self.record_audit(\n            &schema_name,\n            SchemaChangeType::Registered,\n            &format!(\"Registered schema version {}\", schema_version),\n        );\n\n        // Write the updated canonical catalog to shared memory.\n        // This is the single source of truth for UI, blockchain, everything.\n        if let Err(e) = self.write_schemas_to_shm() {\n            warn!(error = %e, \"Failed to sync schema catalog to shared memory\");\n        }\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-09T04:26:05.081Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_phbCSGAHf84vw3RAVZ8xkry6","output":"Chunk ID: fb09c2\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1113\nOutput:\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse async_trait::async_trait;\nuse op_state::{ApplyResult, Checkpoint, DiffMetadata, PluginCapabilities, StateDiff, StatePlugin};\nuse parking_lot::Mutex;\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse simd_json::prelude::*;\nuse simd_json::OwnedValue as Value;\nuse std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};\nuse std::os::unix::net::UnixListener;\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tracing::{info, warn};\n\n/// The single active-schema catalog in shared memory. Every plugin reads its\n/// own slice by name from this one file — there is no per-plugin shm file and\n/// no diff loop. The schema's declared state IS the desired state.\nconst SHM_SCHEMA_PATH: &str = \"/dev/shm/live-schema.json\";\n\nfn default_protocol() -> String {\n    \"grpc\".to_string()\n}\n\n/// A configured unix-domain socket endpoint.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct SocketEndpoint {\n    /// Filesystem path to the socket (e.g. `/run/qdrant.sock`).\n    pub path: String,\n    /// Local TCP port xray listens on and proxies into this socket.\n    pub port: u16,\n    /// Transport protocol carried over the socket (`\"grpc\"`, `\"jsonrpc\"`, …).\n    #[serde(default = \"default_protocol\")]\n    pub protocol: String,\n    /// Human-readable service label used as the xray outbound tag.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub label: String,\n}\n\n/// Runtime state: all declared socket endpoints.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]\npub struct UnixSocketState {\n    /// Declared unix socket endpoints visible to internal services.\n    pub sockets: Vec<SocketEndpoint>,\n}\n\npub struct UnixSocketPlugin {\n    /// Live listeners keyed by socket path. Holding the `UnixListener` keeps the\n    /// socket bound for the lifetime of the plugin; dropping it tears it down.\n    active: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, UnixListener>>>,\n}\n\nimpl UnixSocketPlugin {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            active: Arc::new(Mutex::new(HashMap::new())),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Read this plugin's desired socket set straight from the single active\n    /// schema catalog in shared memory (zero-copy 1:1). The catalog is keyed by\n    /// plugin name and each entry carries the schema-declared state.\n    fn read_desired() -> UnixSocketState {\n        let Ok(mut bytes) = std::fs::read(SHM_SCHEMA_PATH) else {\n            return UnixSocketState::default();\n        };\n        let Ok(catalog) = simd_json::to_owned_value(&mut bytes) else {\n            return UnixSocketState::default();\n        };\n        let Some(state) = catalog\n            .get(\"unix_socket\")\n            .and_then(|versions| versions.as_array())\n            .and_then(|versions| versions.last())\n            .and_then(|schema| schema.get(\"example\"))\n        else {\n            return UnixSocketState::default();\n        };\n        simd_json::serde::from_owned_value::<UnixSocketState>(state.clone()).unwrap_or_default()\n    }\n\n    /// Bind a single endpoint, replacing any stale socket file. Returns `true`\n    /// when a new listener was created.\n    fn ensure_bound(\n        active: &mut HashMap<String, UnixListener>,\n        endpoint: &SocketEndpoint,\n    ) -> Result<bool> {\n        if active.contains_key(&endpoint.path) {\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n        if let Some(parent) = Path::new(&endpoint.path).parent() {\n            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;\n        }\n        if Path::new(&endpoint.path).exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&endpoint.path)?;\n        }\n        let listener = UnixListener::bind(&endpoint.path)?;\n        listener.set_nonblocking(true)?;\n        active.insert(endpoint.path.clone(), listener);\n        info!(\n            socket = %endpoint.path,\n            port = endpoint.port,\n            protocol = %endpoint.protocol,\n            \"bound unix socket endpoint\"\n        );\n        Ok(true)\n    }\n\n    /// Drop a listener and unlink its socket file. Returns `true` when removed.\n    fn unbind(active: &mut HashMap<String, UnixListener>, path: &str) -> bool {\n        if active.remove(path).is_some() {\n            if let Err(error) = std::fs::remove_file(path) {\n                warn!(socket = %path, %error, \"failed to unlink unix socket file\");\n            }\n            true\n        } else {\n            false\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Reconcile the live listeners to exactly the supplied desired set.\n    fn reconcile(&self, desired: &UnixSocketState) -> ApplyResult {\n        let mut active = self.active.lock();\n"}}

The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. arrays representing client capabilities over D-Bus.\ncrates/audits/op-gateway/15_15_License_Compliance.md:81:  Because peer public keys are transmitted in plaintext during handshakes and are publicly known, an attacker can easily brute-force or compute active session IDs by guessing recent timestamps (which have a low search space of 1 second intervals). Since session IDs are validated to grant API access (`mcp_gateway.rs:193`), this allows an attacker to hijack active client sessions and query restricted MCP tools.\ncrates/audits/op-introspection/11_11_Configuration_Feature_Flags.md:22:  Conditional compilation attributes `#[cfg(feature = \"mcp\")]` are used in the codebase. However, `mcp` is not declared as a feature in the `crates/op-introspection/Cargo.toml` file. Consequently, the conditional compilation paths will never evaluate to true under standard compilations of this crate.\ncrates/audits/op-workflows/01_01_Architecture_Module_Map.md:54:    Rust's `std::collections::HashMap` uses a randomized hash seed by default to prevent HashDoS attacks. This means the iteration order of the variables is non-deterministic between different program executions or even between different read lock acquisitions.\ncrates/audits/op-introspection/10_10_Documentation_Completeness.md:109:* **Impact**: These structures hold critical system reporting metrics (including active security mitigations and conversion configurations). Defining them as raw Rust representations limits reporting automation and prevents programmatic ingestion by compliance tools natively recognizing versioned schemas or OSCAL.\ncrates/audits/op-gateway/14_14_Build_CI_Workspace_Wiring.md:12:- **Contract Enforcement**: Data contracts within `op-gateway` are expressed as ad-hoc Rust structs annotated with Serde (e.g., `RoutingDecision`, `AccessLevel`, `McpClientInfo`, `McpSession` in `crates/op-gateway/src/mcp_gateway.rs:16-56`).\ncrates/audits/op-gateway/14_14_Build_CI_Workspace_Wiring.md:13:- **Schema-as-Code Flag**: There is a violation of the Schema-as-Code discipline. The D-Bus communication payloads are dynamically constructed and serialized as ad-hoc JSON objects via `simd_json::json!` (e.g., `crates/op-gateway/src/mcp_gateway.rs:341-356`) instead of referencing versioned, strictly typed Protobuf schemas or OSCAL templates.\ncrates/audits/op-gateway/14_14_Build_CI_Workspace_Wiring.md:123:- `crates/op-gateway/src/mcp_gateway.rs:341`: file has 337 lines\ncrates/audits/op-workflows/18_18_Schema_OSCAL_Compliance.md:61:  `simd_json::OwnedValue` holds JSON objects as unordered maps (e.g. `halfbrown::HashMap` or `std::collections::HashMap`). In Rust, hash map iteration order is randomized by default to prevent DoS attacks. Consequently, `simd_json::to_string` does **not** guarantee a deterministic key serialization order across different program runs, different instances, or even successive iterations.\ncrates/audits/op-workflows/18_18_Schema_OSCAL_Compliance.md:138:  In `CodeReviewNode::execute`, it performs calculations using both formats, returning `serde_json::Value` while interacting with traits or structures that may expect `simd_json` parameters. This introduces cognitive overhead for developers, increases compile times, and leads to unnecessary type conversions and allocation penalties as values are marshaled between `serde_json` and `simd_json`.\ncrates/audits/op-workflows/09_09_Test_Coverage_Examples.md:112:  Because `vars` is a standard `std::collections::HashMap`, its iteration order is randomized and non-deterministic per execution. If one variable's value contains a placeholder string matching another variable's pattern (for example, variable `X` has value `${Y}` and variable `Y` has value `target`), the output is highly sensitive to the random iteration order of the map. If `X` is processed first, the placeholder `${Y}` is written into `result` and subsequently replaced by `target` during the second iteration step. If `Y` is processed first, its placeholder `${Y}` is replaced, and the placeholder `${Y}` introduced later by `X` remains unresolved. This creates non-deterministic execution bugs and potential variable-injection vectors.\n"}}

Tools:\n//! - `code_search`  — filtered semantic search over indexed repos.\n//!   subid: `obs.service.code-rag.search@v1`\n//! - `code_context` — session-aware fused retrieval + awareness signals.\n//!   subid: `exp.service.code-context.render@v1`\n//! - `code_index`   — live indexing of a source file / repomix entry.\n//!   subid: `src.software.workspace.index@v1`\n\nuse crate::context_awareness::{ActivityType, ContextAwarenessEngine};\nuse crate::rag_pipeline::{CodeFilter, RagPipeline, RagResult};\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse async_trait::async_trait;\nuse op_mcp::tool_registry::{BoxedTool, Tool, ToolRegistry};\nuse simd_json::prelude::*;\nuse simd_json::{json, OwnedValue as Value};\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tracing::warn;\n\n/// Register all code-context tools against the shared registry.\n/// Returns the number of tools registered.\npub async fn register_code_tools(\n    registry: &ToolRegistry,\n    rag: Arc<RagPipeline>,\n    engine: Arc<ContextAwarenessEngine>,\n    collection: String,\n) -> Result<usize> {\n    registry\n        .register(Arc::new(CodeSearchTool {\n            rag: rag.clone(),\n            collection: collection.clone(),\n        }) as BoxedTool)\n        .await?;\n    registry\n        .register(Arc::new(CodeContextTool {\n            rag: rag.clone(),\n            engine,\n            collection: collection.clone(),\n        }) as BoxedTool)\n        .await?;\n    registry\n        .register(Arc::new(CodeIndexTool { rag, collection }) as BoxedTool)\n        .await?;\n    Ok(3)\n}\n\n// ─── code_search ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\npub struct CodeSearchTool {\n    rag: Arc<RagPipeline>,\n    collection: String,\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl Tool for CodeSearchTool {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"code_search\"\n    }\n\n    fn description(&self) -> &str {\n        \"Semantic code search over indexed repositories. query = input\n            .get(\"query\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"missing query\"))?;\n        let session_id = input\n )\n            .await;\n\n        let filter = filter_from(&input, false);\n        let (results, retrieval_error) = match self\n            .rag\n            .query_fused(&self.collection, query, Arc<RagPipeline>,\n    collection: String,\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl Tool for CodeIndexTool {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"code_index\"\n    }\n\n    fn description(&self) -> &str {\n        \"Index code into the semantic store. mode='source' indexes a single in-memory file \\\n         (repo, file_path, content) for live workspace updates; mode='repomix_zip' ingests an \\\n \"index\".into(), \"ingest\".into()]\n    }\n\n    fn input_schema(&self) -> Value {\n        tool_input_schema(\"code_index\")\n    }\n\n    async fn execute(&self, input: Value) -> Result<Value> {\n         .get(\"file_path\")\n                    .and_then(Value::as_str)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"source mode requires 'file_path'\"))?;\n                let content = input\n                    .get(\"content\")\n                    .and_then(Value::as_str)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"source mode requires 'content'\"))?;\n                self.rag\n                    .ingest_source_text(repo, file_path, content, collection)\n                    .await?\n            }\n            \"repomix_zip\" => {\n                let zip_path = input\n                    .get(\"zip_path\")\n                    .and_then(Value::as_str)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"repomix_zip mode requires 'zip_path'\"))?;\n                let entry = input\n                    .get(\"entry\")\n                    .and_then(Value::as_str)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"repomix_zip mode requires 'entry'\"))?;\n                self.rag\n                    .ingest_repomix_entry(&PathBuf::from(zip_path), entry, collection)\n                    .await?\n            }\n            other => return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"unknown mode: {other}\")),\n        };\n\n        Ok(json!({\n            \"ok\": true,\n            \"mode\": mode,\n            \"collection\": collection,\n            \"files_parsed\": stats.files_parsed as u64,\n            \"chunks_created\": stats.chunks_created as u64,\n            \"chunks_upserted\": stats.chunks_upserted as u64,\n            \"chunks_skipped\": stats.chunks_skipped as u64,\n            \"errors\": stats.errors as u64,\n        }))\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Derive a tool's JSON input schema from the single canonical authority\n/// (`op_plugins::cognitive_mcp_plugin_schema`). The tool never declares its\n/// schema inline — the OSCAL subid and field contract live in the PluginSchema.\nfn tool_input_schema(field: &str) -> Value {\n    op_plugins::cognitive_mcp_plugin_schema()\n        .field_input_schema(field)\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| json!({ \"type\": \"object\", \"properties\": {} }))\n}\n\nfn filter_from(input: &Value, default_exclude_tests: bool) -> CodeFilter {\n    CodeFilter {\n        repo: input.get(\"repo\").and_then(Value::as_str).map(String::from),\n        language: input\n            .get(\"language\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .map(String::from),\n        file_type: input\n            .get(\"file_type\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .map(String::from),\n        path_contains: input\n            .get(\"path_contains\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .map(String::from),\n        symbol_contains: input\n            .get(\"symbol_contains\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_str)\n            .map(String::from),\n        exclude_tests: input\n            .get(\"exclude_tests\")\n            .and_then(Value::as_bool)\n            .unwrap_or(default_exclude_tests),\n    }\n}\n\nfn results_to_simd(results: &[RagResult]) -> Value {\n    let serde_val = serde_json::to_value(results).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null);\n    serde_to_simd(&serde_val)\n}\n\nfn serde_to_simd(v: &serde_json::Value) -> Value {\n    let s = serde_json::to_string(v).unwrap_or_default();\n    let mut buf = s.into_bytes();\n    simd_json::from_slice(&mut buf).unwrap_or(Value::Static(simd_json::StaticNode::Null))\n}\n"}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-11T07:02:26.135Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_0EHUBbapS1XhN2AeHQvBG8fo","output":"Chunk ID: c794be\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1565\nOutput:\n//! Cognitive MCP Server Binary\n//!\n//! Transports started in parallel:\n//! - HTTP/SSE  (MCP protocol, port 3003)\n//! - gRPC      (CognitiveToolService, port 50052)\n//! - D-Bus     (org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp / /org/opdbus/v1/cognitive)\n//!\n//! On startup the server reads the local WireGuard public key (from the\n//! interface named by $WG_INTERFACE, defaulting to \"netmaker\") and writes the\n//! canonical IdentitySled to /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat so the Ghostbridge\n//! interceptor and Qdrant shuttle can authenticate outbound gRPC calls.\n//!\n//! Bind address resolution order (highest priority first):\n//!   1. COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND / COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND env vars\n//!   2. --http / --grpc CLI flags\n//!   3. WireGuard interface IP detected at startup (if interface is up)\n//!   4. 0.0.0.0 fallback\n\nuse clap::Parser;\nuse op_cognitive_mcp::CognitiveMcpServer;\nuse op_identity::{write_sled_from_wg, WireGuardIdentity};\nuse tracing::{info, warn, Level};\nuse tracing_subscriber::FmtSubscriber;\n\n#[derive(Parser)]\n#[command(name = \"cognitive-mcp-server\")]\n#[command(about = \"Cognitive MCP Server with memory, NotebookLM bridge, gRPC, and D-Bus\")]\nstruct Cli {\n    /// HTTP/SSE server address (MCP protocol).\n    /// If left at 0.0.0.0 the WireGuard interface IP is used when available.\n    /// Override with COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND env var or this flag.\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_BIND\", default_value = \"0.0.0.0:3003\")]\n    http: String,\n\n    /// gRPC server address (CognitiveToolService).\n    /// If left at 0.0.0.0 the WireGuard interface IP is used when available.\n    /// Override with COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND env var or this flag.\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_BIND\", default_value = \"0.0.0.0:50052\")]\n    grpc: String,\n\n    /// CozoDB database path\n    #[arg(\n        long,\n        env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_DB_PATH\",\n        default_value = \"/var/lib/op-cognitive-mcp/memory.db\"\n    )]\n    db: String,\n\n    /// WireGuard interface to read identity from\n    #[arg(long, env = \"WG_INTERFACE\", default_value = \"netmaker\")]\n    wg_interface: String,\n\n    /// Log level\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_LOG_LEVEL\", default_value = \"info\")]\n    log_level: String,\n\n    /// Disable gRPC server\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_GRPC_DISABLED\")]\n    no_grpc: bool,\n\n    /// Disable HTTP/SSE server\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_HTTP_DISABLED\")]\n    no_http: bool,\n\n    /// Disable D-Bus registration\n    #[arg(long, env = \"COGNITIVE_MCP_DBUS_DISABLED\")]\n    no_dbus: bool,\n}\n\n/// Promote an `0.0.0.0:PORT` default address to `<wg_ip>:PORT` when the WG\n/// interface is up.  Explicit addresses (not starting with `0.0.0.0:`) are\n/// returned unchanged so env-var or flag overrides always win.\nfn resolve_bind(addr: &str, wg_ip: Option<&str>) -> String {\n    if let Some(rest) = addr.strip_prefix(\"0.0.0.0:\") {\n        if let Some(ip) = wg_ip {\n            return format!(\"{ip}:{rest}\");\n        }\n    }\n    addr.to_string()\n}\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let cli = Cli::parse();\n\n    let level = match cli.log_level.as_str() {\n        \"trace\" => Level::TRACE,\n        \"debug\" => Level::DEBUG,\n        \"warn\" => Level::WARN,\n        \"error\" => Level::ERROR,\n        _ => Level::INFO,\n    };\n\n    let subscriber = FmtSubscriber::builder()\n        .with_max_level(level)\n        .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n        .finish();\n    tracing::subscriber::set_global_default(subscriber)?;\n\n    // ── WireGuard identity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    // 1. Detect local WG IP for bind address resolution.\n    // 2. Write canonical IdentitySled to /dev/shm for Ghostbridge auth.\n    let wg_id = WireGuardIdentity::with_interface(&cli.wg_interface);\n    let wg_ip = wg_id.get_local_ip();\n\n    match wg_id.get_local_pubkey() {\n        Ok(pubkey) => {\n            info!(\n                interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n                pubkey = %pubkey,\n                wg_ip = ?wg_ip,\n                \"Writing WireGuard identity sled to /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat\"\n            );\n            if let Err(e) = write_sled_from_wg(&pubkey) {\n                warn!(\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"Failed to write identity sled — gRPC Ghostbridge auth will not work\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            warn!(\n                interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n                error = %e,\n                \"Could not read WireGuard public key — identity sled not written; \\\n                 set WG_PUBKEY env var to override\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Resolve bind addresses: promote 0.0.0.0 defaults to WG interface IP.\n    let http_addr = resolve_bind(&cli.http, wg_ip.as_deref());\n    let grpc_addr = resolve_bind(&cli.grpc, wg_ip.as_deref());\n\n    info!(\n        http = %http_addr,\n        grpc = %grpc_addr,\n        db = %cli.db,\n        wg_interface = %cli.wg_interface,\n        \"Starting Cognitive MCP Server\"\n    );\n\n    let server = CognitiveMcpServer::new(&cli.db).await?;\n\n    // D-Bus: start first, keep connection alive for the process lifetime.\n    let _dbus_conn = if !cli.no_dbus {\n        match server.start_dbus().await {\n            Ok(conn) => {\n                info!(\"D-Bus registered: org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp\");\n                Some(conn)\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                warn!(\"D-Bus registration failed (continuing without it): {e}\");\n                None\n            }\n        }\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n\n    match (cli.no_grpc, cli.no_http) {\n        (true, true) => {\n            eprintln!(\"Error: both --no-grpc and --no-http specified. Nothing to run.\");\n            std::process::exit(1);\n        }\n        (true, false) => {\n            info!(\"Running HTTP/SSE only\");\n            server.start_http_server(&http_addr).await?;\n        }\n        (false, true) => {\n            info!(\"Running gRPC only\");\n            server.start_grpc_server(&grpc_addr).await?;\n        }\n        (false, false) => {\n            info!(\"Running HTTP/SSE + gRPC\");\n            server.start_dual(&http_addr, &grpc_addr).await?;\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-11T07:02:34.597Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_G22fBf2psJdCKUrhHCURuQ8y","output":"Chunk ID: 54d9b3\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 2285\nOutput:\n//! RAG ingest CLI — embed repomix zip content into Qdrant via Voyage.\n//!\n//! Usage:\n//!   rag-ingest --zip ~/repomix.zip --repo rust-analyzer\n//!   rag-ingest --zip ~/repomix.zip --all\n//!   rag-ingest --zip ~/repomix.zip --list\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse clap::Parser;\nuse op_cognitive_mcp::rag_pipeline::{RagPipeline, DEFAULT_COLLECTION};\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse tracing::{error, info};\n\n// voyage-code-3 pricing: $0.18 per million tokens (charged after free tier exhausted)\nconst VOYAGE_COST_PER_MILLION: f64 = 0.18;\n// Free tier per model per month (tokens) — overage is billed at VOYAGE_COST_PER_MILLION\nconst VOYAGE_FREE_TIER_TOKENS: usize = 200_000_000;\n// Rough average tokens per chunk (embed_text header + ~300 content tokens)\nconst AVG_TOKENS_PER_CHUNK: usize = 400;\n// Default hard cap: stop before $10 of paid overage (55M tokens beyond free tier)\nconst DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS: usize = VOYAGE_FREE_TIER_TOKENS + 55_000_000; // free + ~$10\n\n#[derive(Parser)]\n#[command(name = \"rag-ingest\")]\n#[command(about = \"Ingest repomix content into Qdrant with Voyage embeddings\")]\nstruct Cli {\n    /// Path to the repomix zip file\n    #[arg(long, default_value = \"~/repomix.zip\")]\n    zip: PathBuf,\n\n    /// Repo to ingest (e.g. \"rust-analyzer\"). Can be specified multiple times.\n    #[arg(long)]\n    repo: Vec<String>,\n\n    /// Ingest all repos in the zip (slow — hundreds of MB)\n    #[arg(long)]\n    all: bool,\n\n    /// List available repos in the zip and exit\n    #[arg(long)]\n    list: bool,\n\n    /// Qdrant collection name\n    #[arg(long, default_value = DEFAULT_COLLECTION)]\n    collection: String,\n\n    /// Skip repos whose names contain this substring\n    #[arg(long)]\n    skip: Vec<String>,\n\n    /// Estimate cost and chunk count, then exit without embedding\n    #[arg(long)]\n    dry_run: bool,\n\n    /// Maximum tokens to embed across the entire run (budget guard).\n    /// Ingest aborts once this limit is reached. Default: 27M (~$4.86).\n    #[arg(long, default_value_t = DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS)]\n    max_tokens: usize,\n\n    /// Skip the cost confirmation prompt (use in CI or when you know the cost)\n    #[arg(long)]\n    yes: bool,\n}\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<()> {\n    tracing_subscriber::fmt()\n        .with_env_filter(std::env::var(\"RUST_LOG\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \"info\".into()))\n        .init();\n\n    let mut cli = Cli::parse();\n\n    // Expand ~ in zip path\n    if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os(\"HOME\") {\n        let zip_str = cli.zip.to_string_lossy();\n        if zip_str.starts_with('~') {\n            cli.zip = PathBuf::from(home).join(zip_str.trim_start_matches(\"~/\"));\n        }\n    }\n\n    let zip_path = cli\n        .zip\n        .canonicalize()\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"zip not found: {}\", cli.zip.display()))?;\n\n    // List available entries\n    let entries = list_repomix_entries(&zip_path)?;\n\n    if cli.list {\n        println!(\"Repomix entries in {}:\", zip_path.display());\n        for (entry, repo) in &entries {\n            println!(\"  {repo:40} ({entry})\");\n        }\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    // Determine what to ingest\n    let targets: Vec<(String, String)> = if cli.all {\n        entries.clone()\n    } else if !cli.repo.is_empty() {\n        // Match by repo name substring\n        entries\n            .into_iter()\n            .filter(|(_, repo)| cli.repo.iter().any(|r| repo.contains(r.as_str())))\n            .collect()\n    } else {\n        anyhow::bail!(\"Specify --repo <name>, --all, or --list\");\n    };\n\n    // Apply skip filter\n    let targets: Vec<_> = targets\n        .into_iter()\n        .filter(|(_, repo)| !cli.skip.iter().any(|s| repo.contains(s.as_str())))\n        .collect();\n\n    if targets.is_empty() {\n        anyhow::bail!(\"No matching entries found. Use --list to see available repos.\");\n    }\n\n    // ── Cost estimate ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    // Count chunks per target by reading zip entry sizes (fast, no embedding).\n    let mut estimated_chunks = 0usize;\n    {\n        let file = std::fs::File::open(&zip_path)?;\n        let mut archive = zip::ZipArchive::new(file)?;\n        for (entry_name, _repo) in &targets {\n            if let Ok(entry) = archive.by_name(entry_name) {\n                // ~1 chunk per 1.5 KB of source (empirical from past runs)\n                estimated_chunks += (entry.size() as usize / 1500).max(1);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    let estimated_tokens = estimated_chunks * AVG_TOKENS_PER_CHUNK;\n    let estimated_cost = estimated_tokens as f64 / 1_000_000.0 * VOYAGE_COST_PER_MILLION;\n\n    println!(\"\\n=== Cost estimate ===\");\n    println!(\"  Repos          : {}\", targets.len());\n    println!(\"  Est. chunks    : ~{estimated_chunks}\");\n    println!(\"  Est. tokens    : ~{}M\", estimated_tokens / 1_000_000);\n    println!(\"  Est. cost      : ~${estimated_cost:.2}  (voyage-code-3 @ ${VOYAGE_COST_PER_MILLION}/M tokens)\");\n    println!(\n        \"  Token cap      : {}M  (--max-tokens)\",\n        cli.max_tokens / 1_000_000\n    );\n\n    if cli.dry_run {\n        println!(\"\\n[dry-run] Exiting without embedding.\");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    if estimated_tokens > cli.max_tokens {\n        anyhow::bail!(\n            \"Estimated tokens ({estimated_tokens}) exceed --max-tokens cap ({}). \\\n             Reduce scope with --repo, raise --max-tokens, or use --dry-run to preview.\",\n            cli.max_tokens\n        );\n    }\n\n    if !cli.yes {\n        print!(\"\\nProceed with ingest? [y/N] \");\n        std::io::Write::flush(&mut std::io::stdout())?;\n        let mut answer = String::new();\n        std::io::stdin().read_line(&mut answer)?;\n        if !answer.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"y\") {\n            println!(\"Aborted.\");\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── Ingest ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    info!(\n        count = targets.len(),\n        collection = %cli.collection,\n        \"Starting ingest\"\n    );\n\n    let pipeline =\n        RagPipeline::from_env().context(\"Failed to init pipeline — is VOYAGE_API_KEY set?\")?;\n\n    let mut total_files = 0usize;\n    let mut total_chunks = 0usize;\n    let mut total_errors = 0usize;\n    let mut total_tokens = 0usize;\n\n    'outer: for (entry_name, repo) in &targets {\n        info!(repo = %repo, \"Processing\");\n\n        match pipeline\n            .ingest_repomix_entry(&zip_path, entry_name, &cli.collection)\n            .await\n        {\n            Ok(stats) => {\n                info!(\n                    repo = %repo,\n                    files = stats.files_parsed,\n                    chunks = stats.chunks_upserted,\n                    errors = stats.errors,\n                    \"Done\"\n                );\n                total_files += stats.files_parsed;\n                total_chunks += stats.chunks_upserted;\n                total_errors += stats.errors;\n                total_tokens += stats.chunks_upserted * AVG_TOKENS_PER_CHUNK;\n\n                if total_tokens >= cli.max_tokens {\n                    println!(\n                        \"\\n⚠  Token cap reached ({} / {} tokens). Stopping early.\",\n                        total_tokens, cli.max_tokens\n                    );\n                    break 'outer;\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                error!(repo = %repo, error = %e, \"Ingest failed\");\n                total_errors += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    let actual_cost = total_tokens as f64 / 1_000_000.0 * VOYAGE_COST_PER_MILLION;\n    println!(\"\\n=== Ingest summary ===\");\n    println!(\"  Repos processed : {}\", targets.len());\n    println!(\"  Source files    : {total_files}\");\n    println!(\"  Chunks upserted : {total_chunks}\");\n    println!(\"  Errors          : {total_errors}\");\n    println!(\"  Est. tokens used: ~{}M\", total_tokens / 1_000_000);\n    println!(\"  Est. cost       : ~${actual_cost:.2}\");\n    println!(\"  Collection      : {}\", cli.collection);\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn list_repomix_entries(zip_path: &std::path::Path) -> Result<Vec<(String, String)>> {\n    // Open archive to list entries\n    let file = std::fs::File::open(zip_path)?;\n    let mut archive = zip::ZipArchive::new(file)?;\n\n    let mut entries: Vec<(String, String)> = (0..archive.len())\n        .filter_map(|i| {\n            let entry = archive.by_index(i).ok()?;\n            let name = entry.name().to_string();\n            if name.ends_with(\".md\") || name.ends_with(\".xml\") {\n                let repo = repo_name_from_entry(&name);\n                Some((name, repo))\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        })\n        .collect();\n\n    entries.sort_by(|a, b| a.1.cmp(&b.1));\n    Ok(entries)\n}\n\nfn repo_name_from_entry(entry_name: &str) -> String {\n    let base = entry_name.trim_end_matches(\".md\").trim_end_matches(\".xml\");\n    let base = if let Some(pos) = base.rfind(\"-repomix\") {\n        &base[..pos]\n    } else {\n        base\n    };\n    base.to_string()\n}\n"}}

push_rate_limit_secs: u64,\n    /// Idle threshold for context refresh\n    pub idle_threshold_secs: u64,\n    /// Maximum pushes per session per hour\n    pub max_pushes_per_hour: u32,\n}\n\nimpl Default for ContextAwarenessConfig {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            proactive_enabled: true,\n            pattern_detection_enabled: true,\n            min_relevance_score: MIN_RELEVANCE_SCORE,\n            push_rate_limit_secs: MIN_PUSH_INTERVAL_SECS,\n            idle_threshold_secs: IDLE_REFRESH_THRESHOLD_SECS,\n            max_pushes_per_hour: 20,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Context awareness engine with proactive knowledge pushing\npub struct ContextAwarenessEngine {\n    config: ContextAwarenessConfig,\n    /// Session context states\n    session_states: Arc<DashMap<String, RwLock<SessionContextState>>>,\n    /// Memory store for context retrieval\n    memory_store: Arc<CognitiveMemoryStore>,\n    /// RAG pipeline for semantic search\n    rag_pipeline: Option<Arc<RagPipeline>>,\n    /// Broadcast channel for knowledge pushes\n    push_tx: broadcast::Sender<KnowledgePush>,\n    /// Activity event receiver\n    activity_rx: Arc<RwLock<mpsc::Receiver<ActivityEvent>>>,\n    /// Activity event sender (cloneable)\n    activity_tx: mpsc::Sender<ActivityEvent>,\n}\n\n/// Activity event for the engine to process\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ActivityEvent {\n    pub session_id: String,\n    pub activity_type: ActivityType,\n    pub content: String,\n    pub metadata: serde_json::Value,\n}\n\n/// Result of trigger evaluation\n#[derive(Debug)]\nstruct TriggerEvaluation {\n    should_push: bool,\n    trigger: Option<PushTrigger>,\n    trigger_reason: String,\n    relevance_score: f32,\n    context_query: String,\n}\n\nimpl ContextAwarenessEngine {\n    /// Create new context awareness engine\n    pub fn new(\n        config: ContextAwarenessConfig,\n        memory_store: Arc<CognitiveMemoryStore>,\n        rag_pipeline: Option<Arc<RagPipeline>>,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let (push_tx, _push_rx) = broadcast::channel(100);\n        let (activity_tx, activity_rx) = mpsc::channel(1000);\n\n        Self {\n            config,\n            session_states: Arc::new(DashMap::new()),\n            memory_store,\n            rag_pipeline,\n            push_tx,\n            activity_rx: Arc::new(RwLock::new(activity_rx)),\n            activity_tx,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get a sender for activity events\n    pub fn activity_sender(&self) -> mpsc::Sender<ActivityEvent> {\n        self.activity_tx.clone()\n    }\n\n    /// Subscribe to knowledge pushes\n    pub fn subscribe_pushes(&self) -> broadcast::Receiver<KnowledgePush> {\n        self.push_tx.subscribe()\n    }\n"}}

When the qdrant container socket is\n/// declared via `UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS` (e.g. `qdrant:/run/qdrant.sock:6334`),\n/// xray transparently proxies `127.0.0.1:6334` → container unix socket using\n/// its native domain-socket (`\"network\": \"ds\"`) outbound — no custom tonic\n/// connector needed here.\n///\n/// Override the URL with `COGNITIVE_MCP_QDRANT_URL`.\npub fn qdrant_client_from_env() -> Result<Qdrant> {\n    let url = std::env::var(\"COGNITIVE_MCP_QDRANT_URL\")\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"http://127.0.0.1:6334\".into());\n    Qdrant::from_url(&url)\n        .build()\n        .context(\"Failed to build Qdrant client\")\n}\n\n/// Load the Voyage API key from a secret file when env vars are unset.\n///\n/// Defaults to `~/.ssh/mongo-voyage`; override with the\n/// `COGNITIVE_MCP_VOYAGE_KEY_FILE` env var. The first non-empty line is used\n/// (so a key file with a trailing newline or comment lines works).\nfn voyage_key_from_file() -> Option<String> {\n    let path = std::env::var(\"COGNITIVE_MCP_VOYAGE_KEY_FILE\")\n        .ok()\n        .map(std::path::PathBuf::from)\n        .or_else(|| std::env::var_os(\"HOME\").map(|h| Path::new(&h).join(\".ssh/mongo-voyage\")))?;\n\n    let contents = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).ok()?;\n    // The creds file may contain multiple credential types (Atlas service\n    // account ID/secret, plus a Voyage API key).  We must skip service\n    // account lines and pick the actual API key.\n    let key = contents\n        .lines()\n        .map(str::trim)\n        .find(|l| {\n            !l.is_empty()\n                && !l.starts_with('#')\n                // skip Atlas service-account tokens\n                && !l.starts_with(\"mdb_sa_id_\")\n                && !l.starts_with(\"mdb_sa_sk_\")\n                // line should look like a Voyage key (MongoDB-hosted or public)\n                && (l.starts_with(\"al-\") || l.starts_with(\"pa-\"))\n        })?\n        .to_string();\n\n    if key.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        info!(path = %path.display(), \"Loaded Voyage API key from file\");\n        Some(key)\n"}}

ds outbound then proxies 127.0.0.1:$QDRANT_PORT → /run/qdrant.sock\n# via UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS=qdrant:/run/qdrant.sock:$QDRANT_PORT.\n\nSOCKET_PATH=\"/run/qdrant.sock\"\n\nincus config device add bootmisc\n}\nINIT\n\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER\" -- chmod +x /etc/init.d/qdrant\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER\" -- rc-update add qdrant default\nincus exec \"$CONTAINER\" -- rc-service qdrant start\n\n# ─── http://127.0.0.1:6333/healthz 2>/dev/null | grep -q ok; then\n        log \"Qdrant is healthy inside the container\"\n        break\n    fi\n    sleep 1\ndone\n\n# ─── remove NIC (container is now sealed, no network) ────────────────────────\n\nlog \"Removing container NIC (sealing network)\"\n# Alpine has eth0 added by default profile; remove any NIC devices\nfor dev in eth0 eth1 enp0 enp1; \"Testing gRPC health via Unix socket...\"\nif command -v grpc_health_probe &>/dev/null; then\n    grpc_health_probe -addr unix:\"$SOCKET_PATH\" && log \"gRPC health OK\" || true\nelse\n    # Fall back to socat + HTTP check\n    if command -v socat &>/dev/null; then\n        result=$(echo -e \"GET /healthz HTTP/1.0\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\n\\r\\n\" \\\n            | socat - UNIX-CONNECT:\"$SOCKET_PATH\" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 || true)\n        log \"Socket check: ${result:-no HTTP response (gRPC-only socket is normal)}\"\n    fi\nfi\n\n# ─── summary ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\necho \"\"\necho \"═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════\"\necho \" Qdrant ${QDRANT_VERSION} installed in Incus container)\"\necho \"═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════\"\necho \"\"\necho \" Xray routes 127.0.0.1:${QDRANT_PORT} → ${SOCKET_PATH} via ds outbound.\"\necho \" Set in your xray environment:\"\necho \"   UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS=qdrant:${SOCKET_PATH}:${QDRANT_PORT}\"\necho \"\"\necho \" rag-ingest / cognitive-mcp connects to:\"\necho \" {"timestamp":"2026-06-11T07:13:35.809Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"It’s serving empty because the running Qdrant processes are not pointed at the populated storage root.\n\nWhat I found:\n\n- Live `127.0.0.1:6333` reports no collections.\n- Rescue `127.0.0.1:6335` also reports no collections.\n- But populated stores exist on disk:\n  - `/var/lib/qdrant/storage/collections/repomix_rag`\n  - `/var/lib/qdrant-rescue/storage/collections/repomix_rag`\n- Each is about `4.5G` and contains valid-looking Qdrant segment/WAL/vector mmap files.\n- The deployed setup script configures Qdrant with `storage_path: /var/lib/qdrant`, while the populated collection is under `/var/lib/qdrant/storage/collections`.\n\nSo the likely bug is path nesting:\n\nQdrant is probably looking under:\n\n```text\n/var/lib/qdrant/collections\n```\n\nbut the data is actually under:\n\n```text\n/var/lib/qdrant/storage/collections\n```\n\nThat would make Qdrant start healthy and empty, which is exactly what we’re seeing.\n\nWe should not keep serving the empty DB. The fix is to make the active Qdrant service use the populated storage root, likely one of:\n\n```yaml\nstorage:\n  storage_path: /var/lib/qdrant/storage\n```\n\nor remount/move the data so the configured storage root contains `collections/repomix_rag` directly.\n\nI couldn’t inspect/change the live Incus container config because this user lacks Incus daemon permission, but the external symptoms and paths line up with a storage-root mismatch.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-11T07:13:35.816Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"It’s serving empty because the running Qdrant processes are not pointed at the populated storage root.\n\nWhat I found:\n\n- Live `127.0.0.1:6333` reports no collections.\n- Rescue `127.0.0.1:6335` also reports no collections.\n- But populated stores exist on disk:\n  - `/var/lib/qdrant/storage/collections/repomix_rag`\n  - `/var/lib/qdrant-rescue/storage/collections/repomix_rag`\n- Each is about `4.5G` and contains valid-looking Qdrant segment/WAL/vector mmap files.\n- The deployed setup script configures Qdrant with `storage_path: /var/lib/qdrant`, while the populated collection is under `/var/lib/qdrant/storage/collections`.\n\nSo the likely bug is path nesting:\n\nQdrant is probably looking under:\n\n```text\n/var/lib/qdrant/collections\n```\n\nbut the data is actually under:\n\n```text\n/var/lib/qdrant/storage/collections\n```\n\nThat would make Qdrant start healthy and empty, which is exactly what we’re seeing.\n\nWe should not keep serving the empty DB. The fix is to make the active Qdrant service use the populated storage root, likely one of:\n\n```yaml\nstorage:\n  storage_path: /var/lib/qdrant/storage\n```\n\nor remount/move the data so the configured storage root contains `collections/repomix_rag` directly.\n\nI couldn’t inspect/change the live Incus container config because this user lacks Incus daemon permission, but the external symptoms and paths line up with a storage-root mismatch."}],"phase":"final_answer"}}

When `qdrant_shuttle` reads `current_trace_context()`, it reads 32 bytes from offset `41` (which actually overlaps with `is_valid` and the padding bytes in the real structure), resulting in a totally corrupted `trace_id`.\ncrates/audits/op-cognitive-mcp/09_09_Test_Coverage_Examples.md:105:2.  **Offset Miscalculation**: `qdrant_shuttle.rs` extracts appended `PluginSchema` JSON bytes by offsetting `size_of::<IdentitySled>()` (which is ~73 or 80 bytes). However, the actual memory layout was structured using `interceptor.rs`'s size of `208` bytes. Malicious or malformed inputs (such as directory traversal patterns `../../` in `storage_path` or invalid characters/format strings in `dbus_path`) can lead to file system disclosure, path injection, or D-Bus controller crashes when processed by down-stream system modules.\ncrates/audits/op-dbus-model/19_19_Risk_Register_Tech_Debt.md:71:  In `upsert_document`, the fully serialized `PluginCatalogDocument` is bound directly into the database column named `base_object`. However, the domain model `Plugin` (`crates/op-dbus-model/src/models.rs:5`) lists `base_object` as a single `simd_json::OwnedValue` representational block, while `PluginCatalogDocument` contains supplementary structures like `schema`, `dbus_path`, and `storage_path`. This semantic drift and naming overlap create technical debt, making subsequent query refactorings and code maintenance error-prone.\ncrates/audits/op-dbus-model/10_10_Documentation_Completeness.md:51:* **Details**: `PluginCatalogDocument` defines several string-based operational fields, such as `dbus_path: String`, `service_name: String`, `storage_path: String`, and `source: String`. These ad-hoc fields represent infrastructure and system integration contracts that bypass version-controlled specifications.\ncrates/audits/op-dbus-model/10_10_Documentation_Completeness.md:67:* **Details**: In `upsert_document`, the catalog encodes the full `PluginCatalogDocument` as JSON and binds it directly to the `base_object` column of the `plugins` table. However, the `Plugin` model defined in `models.rs` has its own `base_object` field represented as `simd_json::OwnedValue`. This leads to a severe architectural inconsistency: the database column `base_object` contains a completely serialized `PluginCatalogDocument` object (which itself includes fields like `schema`, `dbus_path`, and `storage_path`), whereas other layers of the workspace may parse that column expecting the unstructured runtime value mapped by the `Plugin` model structure. do\n    if incus exec \"$CONTAINER\" -- wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:6333/healthz 2>/dev/null | grep -q ok; then\n        log \"Qdrant is healthy inside the container\"\n        break\n    fi\n    sleep 1\ndone\n\n# ─── remove NIC (container is now sealed, no network) ────────────────────────\n\nlog \"Removing container NIC (sealing network)\"\n# Alpine has eth0 added by default profile; remove any NIC devices\nfor dev in eth0 eth1 enp0 enp1; do\n    incus config device remove \"$CONTAINER\" \"$dev\" 2>/dev/null && \\\n        log \"  Removed NIC: $dev\" || true\ndone\n\n# ─── set socket permissions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n# The proxy device creates the socket as root; make it group-accessible\nSOCKET_GID=$(id -g jeremy 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\nchown root:\"$SOCKET_GID\" \"$SOCKET_PATH\" 2>/dev/null || true\nchmod 660 \"$SOCKET_PATH\" 2>/dev/null || true\n\n# ─── test connectivity from host via Unix socket ──────────────────────────────\n\nlog \"Testing gRPC health via Unix socket...\"\nif command -v grpc_health_probe &>/dev/null; then\n    grpc_health_probe -addr unix:\"$SOCKET_PATH\" && log \"gRPC health OK\" || true\nelse\n    # Fall back to socat + HTTP check\n    if command -v socat &>/dev/null; then\n        result=$(echo -e \"GET /healthz HTTP/1.0\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\n\\r\\n\" \\\n            | socat - UNIX-CONNECT:\"$SOCKET_PATH\" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 || true)\n        log \"Socket check: ${result:-no HTTP response (gRPC-only socket is normal)}\"\n    fi\nfi\n\n# ─── summary ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\necho \"\"\necho \"═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════\"\necho \" Qdrant ${QDRANT_VERSION} installed in Incus container '${CONTAINER}'\"\necho \" Unix socket      : ${SOCKET_PATH}  (Incus proxy → container:6334)\"\necho \" Container NIC    : none (sealed)\"\necho \" Storage          : /var/lib/qdrant (inside container)\"\necho \"═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════\"\necho \"\"\necho \" Xray routes 127.0.0.1:${QDRANT_PORT} → ${SOCKET_PATH} via ds outbound.\"\necho \" Set in your xray environment:\"\necho \"   UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS=qdrant:${SOCKET_PATH}:${QDRANT_PORT}\"\necho \"\"\necho \" rag-ingest / cognitive-mcp connects to:\"\necho \"   COGNITIVE_MCP_QDRANT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:${QDRANT_PORT}  (default)\"\necho \"\"\necho \" Check status:\"\necho \"   incus exec ${CONTAINER} -- rc-service qdrant status\"\necho \"   incus exec ${CONTAINER} -- wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:6333/collections\"\n"}}
