{"timestamp":"2026-06-11T07:18:19.467Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"`tonic-web` is for the cognitive MCP gRPC server, not Qdrant.\n\nIn this repo, cognitive MCP already wraps its gRPC services with `tonic_web::enable(...)`:\n\n- `CognitiveToolServiceServer`\n- reflection service\n- health service\n\nThat lets browser-style gRPC-Web clients talk to cognitive MCP, assuming CORS is also allowed. The current server code has both:\n\n```rust\n.accept_http1(true)\n.layer(cors)\n.add_service(tonic_web::enable(...))\n```\n\nSo for cognitive MCP: yes, `tonic-web` is the right piece and it is present.\n\nFor Qdrant: `tonic-web` is not relevant unless Qdrant itself supports gRPC-Web, which we do not control from this Rust crate. Browser access to Qdrant’s HTTP API is controlled by Qdrant’s own config, specifically `service.enable_cors: true`. The fix there is Qdrant config, not `tonic-web`.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-11T07:18:19.474Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"`tonic-web` is for the cognitive MCP gRPC server, not Qdrant.\n\nIn this repo, cognitive MCP already wraps its gRPC services with `tonic_web::enable(...)`:\n\n- `CognitiveToolServiceServer`\n- reflection service\n- health service\n\nThat lets browser-style gRPC-Web clients talk to cognitive MCP, assuming CORS is also allowed. The current server code has both:\n\n```rust\n.accept_http1(true)\n.layer(cors)\n.add_service(tonic_web::enable(...))\n```\n\nSo for cognitive MCP: yes, `tonic-web` is the right piece and it is present.\n\nFor Qdrant: `tonic-web` is not relevant unless Qdrant itself supports gRPC-Web, which we do not control from this Rust crate. Browser access to Qdrant’s HTTP API is controlled by Qdrant’s own config, specifically `service.enable_cors: true`. The fix there is Qdrant config, not `tonic-web`."}],"phase":"final_answer"}}

When asked to show the output of a command (e.g. `git show`), relay the important details in your answer or summarize the key lines so the user understands the result.\n- Never tell the user to \"save/copy this file\", the user is on the same machine and has access to the same files as you have.\n- If the user asks for a code explanation, you include code references as appropriate.\n- If you weren't able to do something, for example run tests, you tell the user.\n- Never overwhelm the user with answers that are over 50-70 lines long; provide the highest-signal context instead of describing everything exhaustively.\n- Tone of your final answer must match your personality.\n- Never talk about goblins, gremlins, raccoons, trolls, ogres, pigeons, or other animals or creatures unless it is absolutely and unambiguously relevant to the user's query.\n\n## Intermediary updates\n\n- Intermediary updates go to the `commentary` channel.\n- User updates are short updates while you are working, they are NOT final answers.\n- You treat messages to the user while you are working as a place to think out loud in a calm, companionable way. You casually explain what you are doing and why in one or two sentences.\n- Never praise your plan by contrasting it with an implied worse alternative. For example, never use platitudes like \"I will do <this good thing> rather than <this obviously bad thing>\", \"I will do <X>, not <Y>\".\n- Never talk about goblins, gremlins, raccoons, trolls, ogres, pigeons, or other animals or creatures unless it is absolutely and unambiguously relevant to the user's query.\n- You provide user updates frequently, every 30s.\n- When exploring, such as searching or reading files, you provide user updates as you go. You explain what context you are gathering and what you are learning. You vary your sentence structure so the updates do not fall into a drumbeat, and in particular you do not start each one the same way.\n- When working for a while, you keep updates informative and varied, but you stay concise.\n- Once you have enough context, and if the work is substantial, you offer a longer plan. {"timestamp":"2026-06-12T05:18:09.696Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-12</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-12T06:18:30.933Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_rEOQJVciruxzpctljZJ2uPnv","output":"Chunk ID: 75674f\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 310\nOutput:\n# aria2 under s6\n\nThis directory provides a simple s6 service for running `aria2c` as a\nlong-running RPC daemon using a standard s6 service directory.\n\n## Layout\n\n- `run` starts `aria2c` in the foreground, which is what s6 supervises.\n- `log-run` is installed as the optional `s6-log` service.\n- `aria2.conf.example` is copied into the runtime config directory on first\n  start.\n- `PKGBUILD` installs the service into `/etc/s6/sv/aria2`.\n\n## Install manually\n\n```sh\ninstall -Dm755 run /etc/s6/sv/aria2/run\ninstall -Dm755 log-run /etc/s6/sv/aria2/log/run\ninstall -Dm644 aria2.conf.example /etc/aria2/aria2.conf.example\n```\n\nEnable it using the activation mechanism for your s6 setup. For a traditional\ns6 scan directory, that is usually a symlink from the scan directory to\n`/etc/s6/sv/aria2`.\n\n## Runtime paths\n\nThe service defaults to:\n\n- home/data directory: `/var/lib/aria2`\n- config file: `/var/lib/aria2/.config/aria2/aria2.conf`\n- session file: `/var/lib/aria2/.config/aria2/session.lock`\n- log directory: `/var/log/aria2`\n\nThese can be overridden through environment variables provided by your s6\nenvironment directory or wrapper:\n\n- `ARIA2_HOME`\n- `ARIA2_CONFIG_DIR`\n- `ARIA2_CONFIG_FILE`\n- `ARIA2_SESSION_FILE`\n- `ARIA2_LOG_DIR`\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-12T07:15:06.328Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes, but use the right tunnel direction.\n\nIf your **browser is on your local laptop** and `aria2c` is running on the remote box, use a normal local forward:\n\n```sh\nssh -N -L 6800:127.0.0.1:6800 jeremy@3tched\n```\n\nThen open your local browser to an Aria2 web UI, for example AriaNg, and point it at:\n\n```text\nhttp://127.0.0.1:6800/jsonrpc\n```\n\nA **reverse** tunnel is only needed if the remote machine must connect back to a service running on your local machine:\n\n```sh\nssh -N -R 6800:127.0.0.1:6800 jeremy@3tched\n```\n\nFor your Google Drive file specifically: a browser may help if the issue is authentication/cookies, but it will not reliably bypass Google’s **download quota exceeded** page. If your logged-in browser can download it, then the workable path is to export that browser’s Google cookies and run `aria2c --load-cookies cookies.txt ...` on the remote box. If the browser also shows quota exceeded, the tunnel will not fix that.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-12T07:15:06.328Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"Yes, but use the right tunnel direction.\n\nIf your **browser is on your local laptop** and `aria2c` is running on the remote box, use a normal local forward:\n\n```sh\nssh -N -L 6800:127.0.0.1:6800 jeremy@3tched\n```\n\nThen open your local browser to an Aria2 web UI, for example AriaNg, and point it at:\n\n```text\nhttp://127.0.0.1:6800/jsonrpc\n```\n\nA **reverse** tunnel is only needed if the remote machine must connect back to a service running on your local machine:\n\n```sh\nssh -N -R 6800:127.0.0.1:6800 jeremy@3tched\n```\n\nFor your Google Drive file specifically: a browser may help if the issue is authentication/cookies, but it will not reliably bypass Google’s **download quota exceeded** page. If your logged-in browser can download it, then the workable path is to export that browser’s Google cookies and run `aria2c --load-cookies cookies.txt ...` on the remote box. If the browser also shows quota exceeded, the tunnel will not fix that."}],"phase":"final_answer"}}

If the goal is “use my normal browser, but put the downloaded file on the headless box,” the cleanest browser-based way is:\n\n1. make the remote machine’s SSH reachable on your browser machine with a reverse tunnel\n2. mount the remote download directory with `sshfs`\n3. use the browser’s normal download/save dialog and save into that mounted folder\n\nOn the remote/headless box, run:\n\n```sh\nssh -N -R 2222:127.0.0.1:22 your_local_user@your_local_machine\n```\n\nThat makes the remote box’s SSH server appear on your local machine as:\n\n```text\n127.0.0.1:2222\n```\n\nOn your local/browser machine, mount the remote Downloads folder:\n\n```sh\nmkdir -p ~/remote-downloads\n\nsshfs -p 2222 jeremy@127.0.0.1:/home/jeremy/Downloads ~/remote-downloads\n```\n\nThen open the Google Drive link in your local browser and save the file into:\n\n```text\n~/remote-downloads\n```\n\nThat writes through SSH onto the remote machine.\n\nWhen done:\n\n```sh\nfusermount -u ~/remote-downloads\n```\n\nOn macOS, use macFUSE/sshfs and unmount with:\n\n```sh\numount ~/remote-downloads\n```\n\nImportant: this still will not bypass Google’s quota if your browser shows “quota exceeded.” But if your logged-in browser is allowed to download it, this lets the browser download directly into the remote box’s filesystem over SSH.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

Your local browser can only provide auth/cookies/control.\n\nBest options:\n\n**Option 1: Browser “Copy as cURL”**\n1. On your local browser, open the Google Drive link while logged in.\n2. Open DevTools → Network.\n3. Click **Download anyway**.\n4. In Network, find the `download?...` request.\n5. Right click → **Copy → Copy as cURL**.\n6. Paste that command into the VPS shell.\n7. Add output flags if needed:\n\n```sh\n-L -o /home/jeremy/Downloads/sda3-20260524-2050.img.zst\n```\n\nThat makes the VPS download the file using its own bandwidth, but with your browser’s cookies/headers.\n\n**Option 2: Export browser cookies, then use VPS downloader**\n\nExport cookies from your local browser for:\n\n```text\n.google.com\ndrive.google.com\ndrive.usercontent.google.com\n```\n\nSave as `cookies.txt`, copy it to the VPS, then run:\n\n```sh\naria2c \\\n  --load-cookies=/home/jeremy/cookies.txt \\\n  --continue=true \\\n  --dir=/home/jeremy/Downloads \\\n  --out=sda3-20260524-2050.img.zst \\\n  'https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=15EiidpGSPC_RYHGOsWHo-AyKfMr0uVi6'\n```\n\nOr with `curl`:\n\n```sh\ncurl -L \\\n  -b /home/jeremy/cookies.txt \\\n  -o /home/jeremy/Downloads/sda3-20260524-2050.img.zst \\\n  'https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=15EiidpGSPC_RYHGOsWHo-AyKfMr0uVi6'\n```\n\n**Option 3: Run the browser on the VPS**\nIf you truly need an interactive browser on the VPS, use VNC/noVNC or X forwarding. Then Chrome/Firefox runs on the VPS, so downloads use VPS bandwidth. But cookie/cURL is usually cleaner.\n\nImportant: none of these bypass Google’s “quota exceeded” block. They only solve auth/browser/headless issues and make the VPS, not your 4G link, pull the 54 GB file.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-12T08:22:43.574Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Fixed. The problem was real: `/etc/s6/sv/chrome-remote-desktop/run` had been changed to:\n\n```sh\nexport CHROME_REMOTE_DESKTOP_USE_WAYLAND=COSMIC\n```\n\nThat forced CRD into the COSMIC Wayland path and left `start-cosmic` defunct.\n\nI changed it back to X11/Xfce:\n\n```sh\nexport XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11\nexport XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=XFCE\nexport DESKTOP_SESSION=xfce\nexport XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000\nunset CHROME_REMOTE_DESKTOP_USE_WAYLAND\nunset WAYLAND_DISPLAY\n```\n\nI also installed `xfce4-settings` because `xfsettingsd` was missing.\n\nCurrent status:\n\n```text\nSTARTED\nHost ready to receive connections.\n```\n\nRunning session is now Xvfb + Xfce, not COSMIC:\n\n```text\nXvfb :20\nxfce4-session\nxfce4-panel\nchrome-remote-desktop-host\n```\n\nYou should be able to reconnect from Chrome Remote Desktop now.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-12T05:22:24.388Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"I’m adding a portable s6 service definition under `contrib/s6`: a foreground `run` script, an optional `s6-log` logger, an example aria2 config, and a PKGBUILD that installs s6 service assets instead of systemd units."}],"phase":"commentary"}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-12T05:22:47.016Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call","status":"completed","call_id":"call_0Dubg2oW6aYa2qeHuW3Yy69V","name":"apply_patch","input":"*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: /home/jeremy/git/aria/contrib/s6/README.md\n+# aria2 under s6\n+\n+This directory provides a simple s6 service for running `aria2c` as a\n+long-running RPC daemon. It replaces the systemd unit approach with a standard\n+s6 service directory.\n+\n+## Layout\n+\n+- `run` starts `aria2c` in the foreground, which is what s6 supervises.\n+- `log/run` is an optional `s6-log` service.\n+- `aria2.conf.example` is copied into the runtime config directory on first\n+  start.\n+- `PKGBUILD` installs the service into `/etc/s6/sv/aria2`.\n+\n+## Install manually\n+\n+```sh\n+install -Dm755 run /etc/s6/sv/aria2/run\n+install -Dm755 log/run /etc/s6/sv/aria2/log/run\n+install -Dm644 aria2.conf.example /etc/aria2/aria2.conf.example\n+```\n+\n+Enable it using the activation mechanism for your s6 setup. For a traditional\n+s6 scan directory, that is usually a symlink from the scan directory to\n+`/etc/s6/sv/aria2`.\n+\n+## Runtime paths\n+\n+The service defaults to:\n+\n+- home/data directory: `/var/lib/aria2`\n+- config file: `/var/lib/aria2/.config/aria2/aria2.conf`\n+- session file: `/var/lib/aria2/.config/aria2/session.lock`\n+- log directory: `/var/log/aria2`\n+\n+These can be overridden through environment variables provided by your s6\n+environment directory or wrapper:\n+\n+- `ARIA2_HOME`\n+- `ARIA2_CONFIG_DIR`\n+- `ARIA2_CONFIG_FILE`\n+- `ARIA2_SESSION_FILE`\n+- `ARIA2_LOG_DIR`\n*** Add File: /home/jeremy/git/aria/contrib/s6/PKGBUILD\n+# Maintainer: aria2 contributors\n+pkgname=aria2-s6\n+pkgver=1.0\n+pkgrel=1\n+pkgdesc=\"s6 service definition for aria2\"\n+arch=('any')\n+depends=('aria2' 's6')\n+backup=('etc/aria2/aria2.conf.example')\n+source=('run' 'log-run' 'aria2.conf.example')\n+sha256sums=('SKIP' 'SKIP' 'SKIP')\n+\n+package() {\n+    install -Dm755 \"$srcdir/run\" \"$pkgdir/etc/s6/sv/aria2/run\"\n+    install -Dm755 \"$srcdir/log-run\" \"$pkgdir/etc/s6/sv/aria2/log/run\"\n+    install -Dm644 \"$srcdir/aria2.conf.example\" \"$pkgdir/etc/aria2/aria2.conf.example\"\n+}\n*** Add File: /home/jeremy/git/aria/contrib/s6/aria2.conf.example\n+# Download directory. Relative paths resolve under ARIA2_HOME.\n+dir=Downloads/aria2\n+\n+# RPC\n+enable-rpc=true\n+rpc-listen-port=6800\n+rpc-allow-origin-all=true\n+rpc-listen-all=true\n+# rpc-secret=<TOKEN>\n+\n+# Downloads\n+continue=true\n+max-concurrent-downloads=5\n+split=16\n+min-split-size=1M\n+max-connection-per-server=16\n+lowest-speed-limit=0\n+max-overall-download-limit=0\n+max-download-limit=0\n+max-overall-upload-limit=0\n+max-upload-limit=0\n+disable-ipv6=false\n+max-tries=5\n+retry-wait=0\n+\n+# Session state\n+input-file=.config/aria2/session.lock\n+save-session=.config/aria2/session.lock\n+save-session-interval=30\n+force-save=false\n+\n+# Event loop\n+event-poll=epoll\n+\n+# BitTorrent\n+follow-torrent=true\n+bt-max-peers=55\n+enable-dht=false\n+bt-enable-lpd=false\n+enable-peer-exchange=false\n+peer-id-prefix=-TR2770-\n+user-agent=Transmission/2.77\n+seed-ratio=0\n+bt-hash-check-seed=true\n+bt-seed-unverified=true\n+bt-save-metadata=true\n+bt-require-crypto=true\n+\n+# Disk\n+enable-mmap=true\n+file-allocation=trunc\n+disk-cache=64M\n*** Add File: /home/jeremy/git/aria/contrib/s6/log-run\n+#!/bin/sh\n+set -eu\n+\n+log_dir=${ARIA2_LOG_DIR:-/var/log/aria2}\n+mkdir -p \"$log_dir\"\n+\n+exec s6-log -b n20 s1000000 T \"$log_dir\"\n*** Add File: /home/jeremy/git/aria/contrib/s6/run\n+#!/bin/sh\n+set -eu\n+\n+home_dir=${ARIA2_HOME:-/var/lib/aria2}\n+config_dir=${ARIA2_CONFIG_DIR:-$home_dir/.config/aria2}\n+config_file=${ARIA2_CONFIG_FILE:-$config_dir/aria2.conf}\n+session_file=${ARIA2_SESSION_FILE:-$config_dir/session.lock}\n+example_config=/etc/aria2/aria2.conf.example\n+\n+mkdir -p \"$home_dir\" \"$config_dir\" \"$(dirname \"$session_file\")\"\n+touch \"$session_file\"\n+\n+if [ ! -f \"$config_file\" ]; then\n+    install -m 0644 \"$example_config\" \"$config_file\"\n+fi\n+\n+export HOME=$home_dir\n+cd \"$home_dir\"\n+\n+exec /usr/bin/aria2c --conf-path=\"$config_file\"\n*** End Patch\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-12T05:34:33.589Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Use `aria2c` directly for a one-off download:\n\n```sh\naria2c https://example.com/file.iso\n```\n\nTo download into the s6 daemon through RPC, use the token from:\n\n```sh\nsudo rg '^rpc-secret=' /var/lib/aria2/.config/aria2/aria2.conf\n```\n\nThen call RPC:\n\n```sh\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:6800/jsonrpc \\\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\\n  -d '{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":\"1\",\"method\":\"aria2.addUri\",\"params\":[\"token:YOUR_TOKEN_HERE\",[\"https://example.com/file.iso\"]]}'\n```\n\nDownloads go under:\n\n```sh\n/var/lib/aria2/Downloads/aria2\n```","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-12T05:43:56.825Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_8ErtTfjFLcNfuECpTSkJYT8R","output":"Chunk ID: 169bb2\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1647\nOutput:\n---\nname: browser-automation\ndescription: Browser automation powers web testing, scraping, and AI agent\n  interactions. The difference between a flaky script and a reliable system\n  comes down to understanding selectors, waiting strategies, and anti-detection\n  patterns.\nrisk: unknown\nsource: vibeship-spawner-skills (Apache 2.0)\ndate_added: 2026-02-27\n---\n\n# Browser Automation\n\nBrowser automation powers web testing, scraping, and AI agent interactions.\nThe difference between a flaky script and a reliable system comes down to\nunderstanding selectors, waiting strategies, and anti-detection patterns.\n\nThis skill covers Playwright (recommended) and Puppeteer, with patterns for\ntesting, scraping, and agentic browser control. Key insight: Playwright won\nthe framework war. Unless you need Puppeteer's stealth ecosystem or are\nChrome-only, Playwright is the better choice in 2025.\n\nCritical distinction: Testing automation (predictable apps you control) vs\nscraping/agent automation (unpredictable sites that fight back). Different\nproblems, different solutions.\n\n## Principles\n\n- Use user-facing locators (getByRole, getByText) over CSS/XPath\n- Never add manual waits - Playwright's auto-wait handles it\n- Each test/task should be fully isolated with fresh context\n- Screenshots and traces are your debugging lifeline\n- Headless for CI, headed for debugging\n- Anti-detection is cat-and-mouse - stay current or get blocked\n\n## Capabilities\n\n- browser-automation\n- playwright\n- puppeteer\n- headless-browsers\n- web-scraping\n- browser-testing\n- e2e-testing\n- ui-automation\n- selenium-alternatives\n\n## Scope\n\n- api-testing → backend\n- load-testing → performance-thinker\n- accessibility-testing → accessibility-specialist\n- visual-regression-testing → ui-design\n\n## Tooling\n\n### Frameworks\n\n- Playwright - When: Default choice - cross-browser, auto-waiting, best DX Note: 96% success rate, 4.5s avg execution, Microsoft-backed\n- Puppeteer - When: Chrome-only, need stealth plugins, existing codebase Note: 75% success rate at scale, but best stealth ecosystem\n- Selenium - When: Legacy systems, specific language bindings Note: Slower, more verbose, but widest browser support\n\n### Stealth_tools\n\n- puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth - When: Need to bypass bot detection with Puppeteer Note: Gold standard for anti-detection\n- playwright-extra - When: Stealth plugins for Playwright Note: Port of puppeteer-extra ecosystem\n- undetected-chromedriver - When: Selenium anti-detection Note: Dynamic bypass of detection\n\n### Cloud_browsers\n\n- Browserbase - When: Managed headless infrastructure Note: Built-in stealth mode, session management\n- BrowserStack - When: Cross-browser testing at scale Note: Real devices, CI integration\n\n## Patterns\n\n### Test Isolation Pattern\n\nEach test runs in complete isolation with fresh state\n\n**When to use**: Testing, any automation that needs reproducibility\n\n# TEST ISOLATION:\n\n\"\"\"\nEach test gets its own:\n- Browser context (cookies, storage)\n- Fresh page\n- Clean state\n\"\"\"\n\n## Playwright Test Example\n\"\"\"\nimport { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';\n\n// Each test runs in isolated browser context\ntest('user can add item to cart', async ({ page }) => {\n  // Fresh context - no cookies, no storage from other tests\n  await page.goto('/products');\n  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to Cart' }).click();\n  await expect(page.getByTestId('cart-count')).toHaveText('1');\n});\n\ntest('user can remove item from cart', async ({ page }) => {\n  // Completely isolated - cart is empty\n  await page.goto('/cart');\n  await expect(page.getByText('Your cart is empty')).toBeVisible();\n});\n\"\"\"\n\n## Shared Authentication Pattern\n\"\"\"\n// Save auth state once, reuse across tests\n// setup.ts\nimport { test as setup } from '@playwright/test';\n\nsetup('authenticate', async ({ page }) => {\n  await page.goto('/login');\n  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('user@example.com');\n  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('password');\n  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();\n\n  // Wait for auth to complete\n  await page.waitForURL('/dashboard');\n\n  // Save authentication state\n  await page.context().storageState({\n    path: './playwright/.auth/user.json'\n  });\n});\n\n// playwright.config.ts\nexport default defineConfig({\n  projects: [\n    { name: 'setup', testMatch: /.*\\.setup\\.ts/ },\n    {\n      name: 'tests',\n      dependencies: ['setup'],\n      use: {\n        storageState: './playwright/.auth/user.json',\n      },\n    },\n  ],\n});\n\"\"\"\n\n### User-Facing Locator Pattern\n\nSelect elements the way users see them\n\n**When to use**: Always - the default approach for selectors\n\n# USER-FACING LOCATORS:\n\n\"\"\"\nPriority order:\n1. getByRole  - Best: matches accessibility tree\n2. getByText  - Good: matches visible content\n3. getByLabel - Good: matches form labels\n4. getByTestId - Fallback: explicit test contracts\n5. CSS/XPath - Last resort: fragile, avoid\n\"\"\"\n\n## Good Examples (User-Facing)\n\"\"\"\n// By role - THE BEST CHOICE\nawait page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click();\nawait page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Sign up' }).click();\nawait page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Dashboard' }).isVisible();\nawait page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Search' }).fill('query');\n\n// By text content\nawait page.getByText('Welcome back').isVisible();\nawait page.getByText(/Order #\\d+/).click();  // Regex supported\n\n// By label (forms)\nawait page.getByLabel('Email address').fill('user@example.com');\nawait page.getByLabel('Password').fill('secret');\n\n// By placeholder\nawait page.getByPlaceholder('Search...').fill('query');\n\n// By test ID (when no user-facing option works)\nawait page.getByTestId('submit-button').click();\n\"\"\"\n\n## Bad Examples (Fragile)\n\"\"\"\n// DON'T - CSS selectors tied to structure\nawait page.locator('.btn-primary.submit-form').click();\nawait page.locator('#header > div > button:nth-child(2)').click();\n\n// DON'T - XPath tied to structure\nawait page.locator('//div[@class=\"form\"]/button[1]').click();\n\n// DON'T - Auto-generated selectors\nawait page.locator('[data-v-12345]').click();\n\"\"\"\n\n## Filtering and Chaining\n\"\"\"\n// Filter by containing text\nawait page.getByRole('listitem')\n  .filter({ hasText: 'Product A' })\n  .getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' })\n  .click();\n\n// Filter by NOT containing\nawait page.getByRole('listitem')\n  .filter({ hasNotText: 'Sold out' })\n  .first()\n  .click();\n\n// Chain locators\nconst row = page.getByRole('row', { name: 'John Doe' });\nawait row.getByRole('button', { name: 'Edit' }).click();\n\"\"\"\n\n### Auto-Wait Pattern\n\nLet Playwright wait automatically, never add manual waits\n"}}

<<'PY'\\nimport asyncio\\nfrom pathlib import Path\\nfrom playwright.async_api import async_playwright\\nURL='https://drive.google.com/file/d/15EiidpGSPC_RYHGOsWHo-AyKfMr0uVi6/view?usp=sharing'\\nDEST=Path('/var/lib/aria2/Downloads/aria2')\\nasync def main():\\n DEST.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\\n async with async_playwright() as p:\\n  ctx=await p.chromium.launch_persistent_context('/home/jeremy/.cache/playwright-google-drive-profile', executable_path='/usr/bin/chromium', headless=True, accept_downloads=True, downloads_path=str(DEST), viewport={'width':1400,'height':900})\\n  page=ctx.pages[0] if ctx.pages else await ctx.new_page()\\n  await page.goto(URL, wait_until='domcontentloaded', timeout=60000)\\n  await page.wait_for_timeout(3000)\\n  print('page ready', page.url)\\n  locator=page.locator('div[role=\\\"button\\\"][aria-label=\\\"Télécharger\\\"]').last\\n  print('locator count', await page.locator('div[role=\\\"button\\\"][aria-label=\\\"Télécharger\\\"]').count())\\n  async with page.expect_popup(timeout=15000) as pi:\\n   await locator.click(force=True)\\n  pop=await pi.value\\n  await pop.wait_for_load_state('domcontentloaded', timeout=30000)\\n  await pop.wait_for_timeout(1000)\\n  print('popup', pop.url)\\n  print((await pop.locator('body').inner_text())[:500])\\n  async with pop.expect_download(timeout=120000) as di:\\n   await pop.locator('input[type=\\\"submit\\\"][value=\\\"Download anyway\\\"]').click(force=True)\\n  dl=await di.value\\n  print('download started', dl.suggested_filename)\\n  target=DEST/(dl.suggested_filename or 'sda3-20260524-2050.img.zst')\\n  await dl.save_as(str(target))\\n  print('saved', target)\\n  await ctx.close()\\nasyncio.run(main())\\nPY\",\"workdir\":\"/home/jeremy\",\"yield_time_ms\":30000,\"max_output_tokens\":12000}","call_id":"call_oFSGJCuzECzz548AAl7pUx1K"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-12T08:17:24.626Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_Eykoz2pnclynAk07wnM3GP59","output":"Chunk ID: 1bde81\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1149\nOutput:\n#!/bin/bash\n\nset -e\n\n# From: https://people.debian.org/~mpitt/systemd.conf-2016-graphical-session.pdf\n\nif command -v systemctl >/dev/null; then\n    # robustness: if the previous graphical session left some failed units,\n    # reset them so that they don't break this startup\n    for unit in $(systemctl --user --no-legend --state=failed --plain list-units | cut -f1 -d' '); do\n        partof=\"$(systemctl --user show -p PartOf --value \"$unit\")\"\n        for target in cosmic-session.target graphical-session.target; do\n            if [ \"$partof\" = \"$target\" ]; then\n                systemctl --user reset-failed \"$unit\"\n                break\n            fi\n        done\n    done\nfi\n\n# use the user's preferred shell to acquire environment variables\n# see: https://github.com/pop-os/cosmic-session/issues/23\nif [ -n \"${SHELL}\" ]; then\n    # --in-login-shell: our flag to indicate that we don't need to recurse any further\n    if [ \"${1}\" != \"--in-login-shell\" ]; then\n        # `exec -l`: like `login`, prefixes $SHELL with a hyphen to start a login shell\n        exec bash -c \"exec -l '${SHELL}' -c '${0} --in-login-shell'\"\n    fi\nfi\n\nexport XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=\"${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP:=COSMIC}\"\nexport XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP=\"${XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP:=COSMIC}\"\nexport XDG_SESSION_TYPE=\"${XDG_SESSION_TYPE:=wayland}\"\nexport _JAVA_AWT_WM_NONREPARENTING=1\nexport GDK_BACKEND=wayland,x11\nexport MOZ_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1\nexport QT_QPA_PLATFORM=\"wayland;xcb\"\nexport QT_AUTO_SCREEN_SCALE_FACTOR=1\nexport QT_ENABLE_HIGHDPI_SCALING=1\nexport DCONF_PROFILE=/usr/share/dconf/profile/cosmic\n\n# Set the QT platform theme to CuteCosmic. Fallback to qt6ct if CuteCosmic is not installed.\nif [ -z \"$QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME\" ]; then\n    export QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=cosmic\n    for QT_PLUGIN_PATH in /usr/lib{*,/*}/qt6/plugins; do\n        if [ -f \"${QT_PLUGIN_PATH}/platformthemes/libcutecosmictheme.so\" ]; then\n            # CuteCosmic found, no need for a fallback.\n            export QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=cosmic\n            break\n        elif [ -f \"${QT_PLUGIN_PATH}/platformthemes/libqt6ct.so\" ] || [ -f \"${QT_PLUGIN_PATH}/platformthemes/libqt5ct.so\" ]; then\n            # Fallback to qt6ct, but keep looking for CuteCosmic.\n            # Note that \"qt5ct\" is compatible with both qt5ct and qt6ct.\n            export QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=qt5ct\n        fi\n    done\nfi\n\n# Start gnome keyring components if the daemon is active\n# -> check if /run/user/$UID/keyring exists\nif [ -d \"/run/user/$(id -u)/keyring\" ]; then\n\n    # Use PATH lookup instead of hardcoding /usr/bin\n    if command -v gnome-keyring-daemon >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        eval \"$(gnome-keyring-daemon --start --components=pkcs11,secrets,ssh > /dev/null 2>&1)\"\n    else\n        echo \"gnome-keyring-daemon not found in PATH\" >&2\n    fi\n\n    # Only set SSH_AUTH_SOCK if the socket actually exists. Either\n    # set the correct one, or don't set one at all. Don't set the\n    # wrong value.\n    if [ -S \"/run/user/$(id -u)/gcr/ssh\" ]; then\n        export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=\"/run/user/$(id -u)/gcr/ssh\"\n    elif [ -S \"/run/user/$(id -u)/keyring/ssh\" ]; then\n        export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=\"/run/user/$(id -u)/keyring/ssh\"\n    fi\nfi\n\nif command -v systemctl >/dev/null; then\n    # Import some variables that we explicitly want to have available\n    # in the user session.\n    systemctl --user import-environment XDG_SESSION_TYPE XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP DCONF_PROFILE SSH_AUTH_SOCK\n\n    # For environment variables already imported into the user's\n    # session, if the value imported differs from the value in this\n    # environment, update it.\n    mapfile -t existing_env_vars < <(systemctl --user show-environment)\n    for env_var in \"${existing_env_vars[@]}\"; do\n        env_var_name=\"${env_var%%=*}\"\n        env_var_value=${!env_var_name:-}\n\n        # Skip current iteration if the environment variable's value\n        # in the current envionment is unset.\n        if [[ -z \"${env_var_value}\" ]]; then\n            continue\n        fi\n\n        env_var_val_str_to_compare=\"${env_var_name}=${env_var_value}\"\n        env_var_val_str_to_compare_ansi_c_quoted=\"${env_var_name}=\\$'$(printf '%q' \"${env_var_value}\")'\"\n        if [[ \"${env_var}\" == \"${env_var_val_str_to_compare}\" ]]; then\n            continue\n        elif [[ \"${env_var}\" == \"${env_var_val_str_to_compare_ansi_c_quoted}\" ]]; then\n            continue\n        fi\n        systemctl --user import-environment \"${env_var_name}\" ||:\n    done\nfi\n\n# Run cosmic-session\nif [[ -z \"${DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS}\" ]]; then\n    exec /usr/bin/dbus-run-session -- /usr/bin/cosmic-session\nelse\n    exec /usr/bin/cosmic-session\nfi\n"}}

systemd_environment:\n      if setting.startswith(wayland_env_prefix):\n        self._wayland_socket = setting[len(wayland_env_prefix):]\n        self.child_env[wayland_display_env] = self._wayland_socket\n        logging.info(\"Fetched Wayland socket name: %s\" % self._wayland_socket)\n        return True\n\n    runtime_dir = xdg.BaseDirectory.get_runtime_dir(strict=True)\n    for socket_name in sorted(os.listdir(runtime_dir)):\n      socket_path = os.path.join(runtime_dir, socket_name)\n      if socket_name.startswith(\"wayland-\") and stat.S_ISSOCK(\n          os.stat(socket_path).st_mode):\n        self._wayland_socket = socket_name\n        self.child_env[wayland_display_env] = self._wayland_socket\n        logging.info(\"Found Wayland socket: %s\" % self._wayland_socket)\n        return True\n\n    logging.error(\"%s not found in systemd environment or %s\" %\n                  (wayland_display_env, runtime_dir))\n    return False\n\n"}}
